articles.title: Nations League: Haaland at the double for Norway while Republic of Ireland lose
articles.summary: The Manchester City man cannot stop scoring
articles.content:
Nations League: Haaland at the double for Norway while Republic of Ireland lose

The Manchester City man cannot stop scoring

Last Update:

Erling Haaland was at it again, bagging a decisive brace to power Norway to a thrilling 3-2 victory over Denmark in their Nations League opener.

Fresh from a remarkable World Cup campaign where he scored seven goals to fire Norway to the quarter-finals, the Manchester City talisman was once again the difference-maker in Oslo.

A chaotic first-half set the tone with three goals in 11 minutes.

Fulham’s Oscar Bobb opened the scoring by collecting a neat delivery from Arsenal playmaker Martin Odegaard and curling a fine finish into the far corner. Just four minutes later, Antonio Nusa danced into the Denmark box before slipping through a pass to Haaland, who applied an instinctive first-time finish past Filip Jorgensen.

Brentford’s Mikkel Damsgaard halved the deficit almost immediately with a sensational 25-yard free-kick and Denmark mounted a fightback on the hour mark when former Manchester United striker Rasmus Hojlund drew the visitors level at 2-2.

Haaland had the final say, however from a smart corner routine, the lethal marksman finding space inside the area to rifle home the winner.

Elsewhere, the Republic of Ireland were flat in defeat to Kosovo while Greece won in Serbia.

Israel forward ​Saied Abu Farchi was sent off after scoring an ⁠equaliser against Austria, following ⁠a ​celebration in ⁠which he used the corner ⁠flag to simulate a ​gun.

Austria went on to win 3-1 with two late goals.

articles.title: Madrid confirm Konate knee ligament injury after defender pulls out of France squad
articles.summary: Konate has avoided a serious injury.
articles.content:
Madrid confirm Konate knee ligament injury after defender pulls out of France squad

Konate has avoided a serious injury.

Last Update:

Real Madrid have confirmed defender Ibrahima Konate has suffered a knee ligament injury, though he is expected to be available after the international break.

The France centre-back pulled out of Zinedine Zidane’s first Les Bleus squad for their UEFA Nations League matches after being unable to finish training on Wednesday.

The French Football Federation said Konate had suffered from a “slight sprain”, with the former Liverpool centre-back replaced in the squad by Manchester United’s Lenny Yoro.

And in a statement released on Thursday, Madrid revealed the nature of the injury.

It read: “Following the tests carried out today on our player Ibrahima Konate by the Real Madrid Medical Services, he has been diagnosed with a collateral ligament injury in his right leg.”

Reports in Spain have claimed that, should his recovery go to plan, Konate will be able to feature after the break.

Madrid face Villarreal on October 10, when they will look to bounce back from a contentious 2-1 defeat to rivals Atletico Madrid.

Centre-back Dean Huijsen will be suspended for that game, having been sent off in the derby loss, which left Madrid six points behind LaLiga leaders Barcelona.

articles.title: Tuchel reveals thoughts on Kane’s 2030 World Cup hopes as he backs England captain for Ballon d’Or
articles.summary: The England and Bayern star is the odds-on favourite.
articles.content:
Tuchel reveals thoughts on Kane’s 2030 World Cup hopes as he backs England captain for Ballon d’Or

The England and Bayern star is the odds-on favourite.

Last Update:

England manager Thomas Tuchel believes Harry Kane deserves to win the Ballon d’Or and would have no problem with picking the Bayern Munich star for the 2030 World Cup.

Kane is the odds-on favourite to win the most illustrious individual prize in football, which will be awarded at a ceremony in London on October 26.

The former Tottenham star scored 61 goals in helping Bayern to a Bundesliga and DFB-Pokal double last season, before finding the net six times as England reached the semi-finals of the 2026 World Cup.

England return to action on Saturday in their UEFA Nations League opener against world champions Spain on Saturday, and, speaking ahead of that game, Tuchel has thrown his support behind Kane’s candidacy for the award.

Asked in an interview with ITV if Kane is his choice for the prize, Tuchel replied: “After this season, yeah.

“Seventy-plus goals, three titles with Bayern Munich, semifinals at the World Cup and in the Champions League.

“He’s getting better and better. I think he added a level of physicality to his match.

“He’s just so committed to high press and so committed to being involved in every part of the match. Be it in deep build-up, be it in finishing, be it in build-up play in the middle block, be it in defending. It’s just the full package.”

Should Kane win the Ballon d’Or, he would become the first Englishman to do so since Michael Owen in 2001.

Kane will be 36 when the 2030 World Cup, which will be held in Spain, Portugal, Morocco with centenary games held in Argentina, Paraguay and Uruguay, kicks off.

But Tuchel does not see that as a barrier to him being involved in a fourth World Cup finals.

“Yeah, no problem. Age is age,” Tuchel said. “It doesn’t matter. It’s only about quality, and he has a long way to go.”

articles.title: Cucurella reveals attempts to convince Rodri to make Real Madrid move before Barcelona switch
articles.summary: Marc Cucurella admits he tried to convince Rodri to follow him to Real Madrid this summer.
articles.content:
Cucurella reveals attempts to convince Rodri to make Real Madrid move before Barcelona switch

Marc Cucurella admits he tried to convince Rodri to follow him to Real Madrid this summer.

Last Update:

Marc Cucurella has revealed he sent Rodri a “subtle message” encouraging the Spain midfielder to join him at Real Madrid before he ultimately opted to move to Barcelona.

Rodri had been heavily linked with a move to the Bernabeu during Real Madrid’s major rebuild this summer, but the Manchester City midfielder instead joined their LaLiga rivals, with Barcelona now six points clear at the top of the table.

Cucurella was one of six new signings at Madrid during the summer and has since been reunited with Rodri in the Spain squad ahead of Saturday’s Nations League meeting with England at Wembley.

Speaking to Cadena SER, the defender admitted he had made his preference clear to Rodri before his transfer was confirmed.

“I don’t really like pressuring or influencing teammates,” Cucurella said.

“These are personal things. It’s true that I sent him a subtle message, before the news broke, saying I hoped we’d become teammates.

“He replied, but didn’t give anything away. I’m happy for him [at Barca], though I hope he doesn’t have too much success.”

Rodri ultimately chose Barcelona, with Hansi Flick’s side making a strong start to the season despite the midfielder’s arrival being one of the most high-profile transfers of the summer.

Cucurella, meanwhile, has been tasked with helping Jose Mourinho’s new-look Real Madrid side challenge for silverware after joining from Chelsea.

The start to life at the Bernabeu has not gone completely to plan, however, with Madrid already suffering defeats against Real Betis and Atletico Madrid.

The latter loss came in the most recent match before the international break, with Atletico running out comfortable winners in the derby.

Cucurella acknowledged that Madrid still have work to do after their difficult start but insisted the players remain focused on developing as a group.

“We didn’t finish the period before the break in the best way,” Cucurella said.

“It’s all a process, but the important thing is to build a solid foundation… Let’s see if we can find a good balance and build a strong, united group. If the season ends the way we all want it to, no one will remember the start.”

articles.title: ‘I still want to achieve something special’ – Udinese sign former Real Madrid and Bayern star Alaba
articles.summary: The Austria international still has a desire to compete.
articles.content:
‘I still want to achieve something special’ – Udinese sign former Real Madrid and Bayern star Alaba

The Austria international still has a desire to compete.

Last Update:

Udinese have signed former Real Madrid and Bayern Munich defender David Alaba.

Alaba, who was a free agent following the expiration of his contract with Madrid, has joined the Serie A club on a deal until the end of the season.

The Austria international has won 10 Bundesliga titles, four Champions Leagues and two LaLiga titles in his illustrious career.

But the 34-year-old now joins an Udinese team that has taken just four points from their first five Serie A games of the new season.

Udinese, who finished 10th last season, will hope Alaba can help improve their fortunes as they target a second successive top-half finish for the first time since 2013.

“Signing David Alaba is a source of immense satisfaction for the entire club,” GM Franco Collavino said in a statement.

“We are welcoming an established champion, a leader and an exemplary professional. His arrival shows Udinese’s determination to grow and compete at the highest level as well as build an increasingly ambitious squad.”

Alaba added: “I’ve had many experiences and won a lot over the course of my career, but one thing hasn’t changed, I still want to win. I still want to compete. And I still want to achieve something special. That is the mindset I’m bringing to Udinese.

“The coach [Kosta Runjaić] made it very clear what role he has in mind for me and what he wants us to achieve together. Naturally, I want to bring my experience to the dressing room, take on responsibility, and help out whenever possible, especially with the younger players.

“I’m not coming here just to be the veteran of the squad, and I certainly didn’t come here to wind down my career. I’m still too ambitious for that, and I still strongly believe in what I can do on the pitch.

“I want to keep pushing, perform at the highest level in Serie A week in and week out, and achieve something meaningful. I’m really excited about this challenge, and I still have a lot to prove to myself.”

Alaba could make his debut for Udinese when they face Torino after the international break on October 12.

articles.title: Anthony Gordon calls on England utilise own strengths rather than replicate Spain’s style at future tournaments
articles.summary: Anthony Gordon says England must follow their own path rather than try to copy other teams' styles of play.
articles.content:
Anthony Gordon calls on England utilise own strengths rather than replicate Spain’s style at future tournaments

Anthony Gordon says England must follow their own path rather than try to copy other teams' styles of play.

Last Update:

Anthony Gordon believes England have enough quality to win major tournaments without trying to replicate Spain’s possession-based approach.

The Barcelona winger was speaking at St George’s Park ahead of England’s meeting with the world champions at Wembley on Saturday, their first match since the World Cup.

“[The] scar doesn’t have to be a negative one because it might lead us to victory in the next tournaments,” Gordon said.

“We can’t keep looking at other countries and trying to be like them, because we’re not them – we’re English and we have our own strengths which they don’t have, so maybe we start playing the way we’re good at.”

Gordon sees Spain differently after Barcelona move

Gordon joined Barcelona from Newcastle for £69.3m during the summer and believes playing in La Liga has changed his understanding of Spanish football.

The 25-year-old has spent the early part of his Barcelona career training and playing alongside some of Spain’s leading players, giving him a closer look at the technical and tactical qualities behind their possession game.

“I’m speaking from a point of view where I feel like we are trying to replicate Spain,” Gordon said.

“Because I’m in Spain, I know we have just as good players, but they have different qualities, so why are you trying to make those players the same as the Spanish players? Because the Spanish players lack the things that we have and vice versa.”

England have lost two successive European Championship finals and were eliminated by France and Argentina at the last two World Cups.

Gordon says controlling games is not in England’s DNA

Spain dominated possession in their World Cup final win over Argentina, having 65% of the ball and restricting Lionel Messi’s side to just two shots during 120 minutes. Neither attempt was on target.

Gordon has experienced that style first-hand since moving to Barcelona and says the way Spanish players control games is rooted in qualities that are difficult to teach.

“It’s not in the English DNA,” Gordon said.

“I’m not sure it’s something that can be taught because now I think, playing in Spain, I can speak with an educated view on the way they keep the ball is different.

“I even look at some of the decisions they take on the ball sometimes and think I’m not sure how you’ve seen that.

“It’s the way they’re built. I don’t know whether it is something that maybe we can’t ever put a name to, but they’re definitely built different.”

articles.title: ‘Utter nonsense’: Virgil van Dijk hits back at claims he influenced Ronald Koeman’s World Cup tactics in fiery press conference
articles.summary: Van Dijk took the time to deny claims he influenced the Netherlands' tactics
articles.content:
‘Utter nonsense’: Virgil van Dijk hits back at claims he influenced Ronald Koeman’s World Cup tactics in fiery press conference

Van Dijk took the time to deny claims he influenced the Netherlands' tactics

Last Update:

Virgil van Dijk has spikily hit back at claims he influenced Ronald Koeman’s tactics during the Netherlands’ World Cup campaign.

Iin an unusually heated press conference from the Liverpool captain, the centre-back made a point of strongly refuting the notion that he had a hand in the tactics in the Round of 32 defeat against Morocco which saw them exit the competition.

“One of your colleagues also said, of course, that it was my idea to switch to playing with a back five. That is utter nonsense,” Van Dijk told one reporter.

“The fact is we simply failed at the World Cup; those are the hard facts.

“We didn’t play a good World Cup. It’s not about me. You perform together; you’re a team. Your claim that I destroyed Dutch football after the World Cup – that sort of thing is completely baseless.

“The plan is devised by the staff. Nonsense is being spread so that I look even worse. That happens far too often.

“I was told that it was my fault we played with five, that Ronald Koeman and I have destroyed Dutch football.

“The plan worked for 89 minutes, even though it was a bad match. We almost broke through. The idea that I destroyed Dutch football makes absolutely no sense. I didn’t decide that.”

Van Dijk excited to continue under Xavi

Van Dijk, 35, could win his 100th Netherlands cap if he plays in all four of their Nations League fixtures against Germany, Greece and twice against Serbia.

The centre-back admitted he considered retiring from international football after the World Cup but said one conversation with new manager Xavi, formerly of Barcelona, was enough to keep him in the national fold.

“I needed a holiday with my family and then an important meeting with the national coach: After 10 seconds it was already clear that I would continue,” the defender added.

“What he said? That I am Virgil van Dijk. It is about trust, appreciation, how important you are for the team. Physically there is – and was – no doubt but you also want to feel appreciation and pleasure.”

articles.title: Harry Kane: England captain reiterates aims to become NFL kicker post-football career and weighs up MLS move
articles.summary: Harry Kane says he is serious about the potential of becoming a kicker in the NFL when his football playing career is over. Kane’s football career is showing no signs of slowing down, with the England and Bayern Munich star the favourite to win the Ballon d’Or after scoring an astonishing 73 goals in 2026. […]
articles.content:
Harry Kane: England captain reiterates aims to become NFL kicker post-football career and weighs up MLS move

Last Update:

Harry Kane says he is serious about the potential of becoming a kicker in the NFL when his football playing career is over.

Kane’s football career is showing no signs of slowing down, with the England and Bayern Munich star the favourite to win the Ballon d’Or after scoring an astonishing 73 goals in 2026.

But the 33-year-old has admitted he will eventually look to switch sports when his football career does end, with the striker once again admitting becoming an NFL kicker is a serious aim.

“That is something I will try and look at a bit more seriously,” Kane said. “It all depends on what happens in my career over the next five or six years, the motivation and what I want to do.

“The NFL is a lot more realistic than the golf one, let’s put it that way.”

Kane could take inspiration from Dallas Cowboys kicker Brandon Aubrey, widely regarded as one of the NFL’s top kickers after previously playing football and being drafted by MLS side Toronto FC.

Former Tottenham striker Clive Allen also made the switch to American football, turning out for the London Monarchs in NFL Europe. Now, Kane – an even more prolific scorer for Spurs – believes his own set-piece prowess could help him follow in their footsteps and split the uprights.

“I take penalties and it is a very similar pressure, technique,” the striker added. “If I did that, in terms of training, I would be closer to that more than any other sport.

“But as I know with all elite sports, when you watch it on TV people make it look easy you think it is possible but that is not always the case.

“If I was to do it, it is something I would take seriously. I would take maybe six months to a year of trying to practice before.”

Kane: MLS move a possibility

Kane has even said he is open to eventually moving to MLS to see out his football career to ease the potential move to MLS.

“Maybe if I am in the MLS in the future or somewhere like that it might be a thing where you could connect the two maybe with the seasons,” he said.

“But, again, it is in the back of my mind because right now I am feeling that I want to play as long as I can here.

“I think sometimes it is easy, you to get to my age, 33, you start thinking about retirement or the future, but I am trying to extract everything I can from the last two, five or 10 years, I will keep going.”

Harry Kane Ballon d’Or favourite

Kane also spoke about the possibility of winning the Ballon d’Or, becoming the first Englishman to do it since Michael Owen in 2001, making no secret of his desire to be recognised with the accolade.

“From my point of view, it would be unbelievable to win it,” Kane said. “I’d be extremely proud to win it.

“I think I’m definitely in the running to win it, without a doubt, so time will tell, the voters will vote for who they want.

“It makes me more proud when other people talk about me, when other team-mates or ex-players or whoever it is, people who compliment me on what I achieved.

“I think that makes me more proud than me trying to talk about it myself.”

articles.title: Cristiano Ronaldo: Portugal legend considered retirement after World Cup but now targeting 1,000th goal and Nations League triumph
articles.summary: Ronaldo will earn his 234th Portugal cap on Thursday
articles.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo: Portugal legend considered retirement after World Cup but now targeting 1,000th goal and Nations League triumph

Ronaldo will earn his 234th Portugal cap on Thursday

Last Update:

Cristiano Ronaldo has admitted he considered retirement from international football after the World Cup, before eventually opting to stay on for Portugal.

Ronaldo, who turns 42 in February, will earn his 234th Portugal cap against Wales on Thursday, with new manager Jorge Jesus already confirming that the former Real Madrid and Manchester United star will start in Lisbon.

Some thought the game at the Jose Alvalade Stadium – the home of Ronaldo’s first club Sporting – could be his farewell match but the forward insists he still has work to do for his country.

Asked if he considered leaving Portugal after the World Cup, Ronaldo said: “Yes I did. Of course, I’m always thinking on my decisions, my future, the present also.

“I’m a thinker. You have to think. This is why you see me here now. It means I will continue.

“I had a conversation with our president, with our coach. I still believe that I’m able to help the national team to reach what they want, and will finish when I feel like I’m not doing anything here.

“I can give to the national team my support, not only through the goals, but also outside of football.

“This is a new young generation. But for me the basic point is to be able on the pitch to score the goals and to help the team win games.”

Ronaldo: Portugal are counting on me

Ronaldo will be reunited with his former Al-Nassr boss Jesus for his country, with the five-time Ballon d’Or winner convinced he can make a difference at international level.

He added: “I’m coming to the national team because I make a difference at my club. Whatever the coach needs, I’m available – whether it’s to play, come on as a substitute, or not play.

“Nobody has more international caps than me and I’m here because I want to help the national team. I know the coach is counting on me and I’m not here because of my resume, but because of what I do at my club.

“If the manager or the president doesn’t count on me, I’ll leave immediately.

“When I feel I’m no longer contributing anything here or that there’s a bad atmosphere, I’ll be the first to pack my bags and leave. If you look at the numbers, you’ll still see the difference I make.

“I will always be a fan of this federation and will always be available to help this federation. I’m only thinking about the present moment… I know many people want me to leave now but my motivation comes from the people who want to keep seeing me.”

Ronaldo: 1,000 goals is the aim

With a European Championship and Nations League triumph under his belt for his national team, you may think Ronaldo has little left to prove. But the 42-year-old his 1,000 career and another trophy is firmly his priority.

The Al-Nassr forward, who is currently on 979 goals, said: “Scoring my 1,000th goal for the national team would be the ‌culmination of something – a beautiful story.

“It wouldn’t be the end of it, but it would be a beautiful story.

“I’ve already admitted that I want to get there, and I will get ‌there. An obsession? No. The rest is about enjoying it, enjoying every day.

“I know why young kids love Cristiano, because they see me as an example, and I will continue to do that. Even when I am retired… in 10 years.

“I’m happy with myself. It doesn’t matter if I play tomorrow, if I rest the next game, for me the most important thing is that I feel good.”

Kick-off on Thursday is at 19:45 BST (14:45 ET / 11:45 PT). In the UK, live TV coverage is on BBC One Wales, BBC Two and S4C.

Streaming on a vast range of devices is available through the BBC iPlayer app and BBC Sport website, as well as S4C Online.

articles.title: Paul Gascoigne slams muted England celebrations at World Cup and says they ‘drive me nuts’
articles.summary: Paul Gascoigne has opened up on how frustrated the current England squad makes him.
articles.content:
Paul Gascoigne slams muted England celebrations at World Cup and says they ‘drive me nuts’

Paul Gascoigne has opened up on how frustrated the current England squad makes him.

Last Update:

England legend Paul Gascoigne has criticised the lack of emotion shown by some players when scoring for the national team, saying their muted celebrations “drive me nuts”.

Thomas Tuchel’s side are preparing for four Nations League fixtures, beginning with a meeting against World Cup winners Spain at Wembley on Saturday.

England will then face Czechia twice and Croatia as Tuchel continues to shape his squad ahead of the next major tournament.

Gascoigne, who earned 57 caps and became one of the iconic figures of the national team during the 1990 World Cup and Euro 96, believes representing England should mean more to the current generation.

“I loved playing for my country. You know, putting on that white shirt, I just thought of my family, made them proud,” Gascoigne told talkSPORT.

❤️ "I loved playing for my country… I'm quite emotional now!"😡 "I see some players score and they don't even celebrate and that drives me nuts!"Paul Gascoigne does not like the amount of players pulling out of the England squad! 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿😫 pic.twitter.com/pQ5lrk8TRy

“It’s quite emotional now talking about it. Playing for your country means so much.

“I see some of the players when they score and they don’t really celebrate. And that drives me nuts.”

Gascoigne recalled a story from his early days with England to underline how much scoring for his country meant to him.

“I scored and there was no one in the crowd. So I jumped over the fence and celebrated on the motorway.”

Gascoigne questions England withdrawals

Gascoigne also criticised the number of players who have withdrawn from Tuchel’s latest England squad.

Declan Rice, Marcus Rashford, Tino Livramento and Kobbie Mainoo have all pulled out of the group for the four Nations League matches, with The Athletic suggesting the players are out because of their accumulated minutes over a sustained period of time.

Morgan Gibbs-White and James Garner have subsequently been called up, while John Stones, Reece James and Djed Spence were already unavailable through injury.

Cole Palmer is also absent from the squad after being overlooked for England’s World Cup campaign in North America.

“You see some of them and they pull out the squad. It’s not very good,” Gascoigne said.

articles.title: Sebastien Pocognoli admits to ‘positive nervousness’ ahead of first Scotland game
articles.summary: The new Scotland head coach is looking forward to his debut in charge of the national team.
articles.content:
Sebastien Pocognoli admits to ‘positive nervousness’ ahead of first Scotland game

The new Scotland head coach is looking forward to his debut in charge of the national team.

Last Update:

Scotland head coach Sebastien Pocognoli has admitted to feeling a “positive nervousness” ahead of his first match in charge of the national team.

The Belgian was appointed in August following the departure of Steve Clarke, whose seven-year spell as Scotland manager ended after their group-stage exit at the World Cup.

Pocognoli’s first assignment comes against Slovenia in Ljubljana on Saturday, beginning a demanding run of four Nations League fixtures in just 11 days.

Scotland will then face Switzerland at Hampden before travelling to North Macedonia, with a home meeting against Slovenia completing the sequence.

“If we talk about nerves, yes, but it’s a positive nervousness,” he told BBC Sport Scotland. “We have a job with responsibility. It’s excitement and I’m just passionate about being on the touchline.”

Pocognoli has made significant changes to the squad, with eight players yet to win a senior Scotland cap.

Among those included are 19-year-old James Wilson, four players aged 20 in Findlay Curtis, Ben Gannon-Doak, Lennon Miller and Colby Donovan, plus 22-year-olds Kristi Montgomery, Luke Graham and Robbie Ure.

Montgomery was called into the squad after Blackburn teammate Kenny McLean withdrew through injury, taking the number of uncapped players to eight.

Pocognoli keeps Scotland flexible

Pocognoli confirmed that he already knows the formation and starting team he intends to use against Slovenia, but believes Scotland need the ability to adapt throughout the Nations League campaign.

“I always think the players select themselves,” he added. “We have four games, so we need to plan. We need to have a periodisation [managing training loads, games and recovery] about the tactical aspect and the physical aspect.

“This team can be flexible. We’re ready for the four games in terms of what kind of approach we want to give.”

Pocognoli has also spoken to Clarke since taking the Scotland job, describing their conversation as a positive experience.

“He was very kind, very… humble. That was very helpful for me. It just was to let me know that he’s behind the team. He was very happy [in his time in the job] but he also felt that it was the right time [to leave]. He wished me all the best.

“I will try to be as successful as the previous staff because we want to play in a big tournament. We want to create this moment for the country.”

articles.title: Tottenham defender Pedro Porro set to miss four weeks with hamstring injury
articles.summary: Tottenham defender Pedro Porro is out injured for a month
articles.content:
Tottenham defender Pedro Porro set to miss four weeks with hamstring injury

Tottenham defender Pedro Porro is out injured for a month

Last Update:

Tottenham defender Pedro Porro is expected to spend around a month on the sidelines after suffering a hamstring injury.

The 27-year-old has withdrawn from Spain’s squad for the current international break and is unlikely to be available when Roberto De Zerbi’s side return to Premier League action against Manchester United on October 10.

Porro could also miss Tottenham’s home meeting with Coventry City on October 19, although there is confidence that he will recover in time to face Chelsea at Stamford Bridge five days later.

The right-back was forced off during Saturday’s 3-2 defeat at home to Aston Villa in the top flight after going down in the 17th minute at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. Archie Gray replaced him for the remainder of the match.

Porro had already missed Tottenham’s games against Everton and Liverpool this month and will now face another spell on the sidelines.

Porro withdraws from Spain squad

Porro had initially been named in Luis de la Fuente’s Spain squad for the international break, but the injury forced him to pull out.

Sporting CP full-back Ivan Fresneda was subsequently called up as his replacement.

Djed Spence left Tottenham during the summer to join Inter, leaving Gray as the main alternative to Porro in the position.

articles.title: Manchester United spending ‘financially sustainable’ in summer after recording more losses
articles.summary: Manchester United have had their say on recent spending after publishing the latest accounts.
articles.content:
Manchester United spending ‘financially sustainable’ in summer after recording more losses

Manchester United have had their say on recent spending after publishing the latest accounts.

Last Update:

Manchester United CEO Omar Berrada has said the club’s summer transfer strategy was shaped by the need to maintain “financial sustainability” after the latest accounts revealed increased overall losses.

United reported record full-year revenue of £677.6 million on Wednesday, alongside an operating profit of £22.6m.

Despite those figures, the club recorded an overall loss of £43m, up from £33m the previous year.

Borrowing also increased by £95m, taking the club’s total debt to £583m.

United spent £155m on midfielders Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans and Carlos Baleba during the summer transfer window, but their overall expenditure was considerably lower than that of their traditional top-six rivals.

Manchester City, Liverpool, Arsenal, Tottenham and Chelsea all spent more, with City, Liverpool, Tottenham and Chelsea each paying at least £100m for an individual player.

United remain the only traditional top-six club yet to spend £100m on a single signing.

Speaking as the club published its fourth-quarter and full-year financial results, Berrada said United would continue to be cautious with their spending.

“While these results confirm that we are on the right trajectory, we will continue to take a disciplined approach to ensure our finances remain sustainable,” said Berrada.

“With that financial sustainability in mind, we have strengthened both our men’s and women’s teams during the summer window and our men’s team has seen the return of Champions League football to Old Trafford.”

United continue to cut costs

The club’s latest figures also underline the financial pressures United have faced while attempting to improve the business.

In a statement accompanying the results, United said the club “continues on its journey to improve operational efficiency and financial sustainability.”

A club source added: “stabilising the business has required, and will continue to require, hard work and financial discipline.”

One of the significant costs recorded during the financial year was the £8.2m paid to Ruben Amorim and his coaching staff following the Portuguese manager’s dismissal in January.

United subsequently saved around £8.5m when Amorim agreed to take charge of AC Milan during the summer.

The club also repaid around £150m from its revolving credit facility between March and June as part of efforts to reduce its financial commitments.

United’s accounts also revealed a £63.5m ($84m) payment for land connected to plans for a new stadium.

articles.title: Lamine Yamal explains why goals should not decide the Ballon d’Or
articles.summary: Lamine Yamal has put forward another reason why he should win the Ballon d'Or.
articles.content:
Lamine Yamal explains why goals should not decide the Ballon d’Or

Lamine Yamal has put forward another reason why he should win the Ballon d'Or.

Last Update:

Lamine Yamal believes the Ballon d’Or should reward the player who brings the most joy to supporters rather than simply going to the footballer with the best scoring record.

The Barcelona forward finished second to Paris Saint-Germain winger Ousmane Dembele last year and is among the leading contenders again, with the winner set to be announced at a ceremony in London on October 26.

Yamal is up against a field that includes Dembele, Real Madrid’s Kylian Mbappe and Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane, who enjoyed a prolific campaign in front of goal.

Kane scored 61 goals for Bayern as they won the Bundesliga, while Mbappe scored 42 for Real Madrid. Yamal found the net 24 times and Dembele scored 20 as PSG won the European title.

The 19-year-old does not believe raw numbers should determine who wins the game’s most prestigious individual award.

“It’s fun that there are more players [up for the prize], more debate and people can have different opinions,” Yamal told L’Equipe.

“At the end of the day, it comes down to the journalists. It’s a difficult job for them. We all have good arguments to win it. We are all great players, so let’s see.

“The Ballon d’Or is for the best player of the year, someone different, someone we have enjoyed watching, who has that magic, makes you smile and look forward to watching games just to see them play.

“It’s not to do with the sheer number of goals. When I think of the Ballon d’Or, I think of [Lionel] Messi, Ronaldinho… different players, players that make you dream.”

Yamal points to style over trophies

There is also a strong statistical case for Kane based purely on his output, but Yamal believes other elements should carry greater weight.

The Barcelona youngster won multiple trophies with his club and was also part of the Spain side that lifted the World Cup, adding another major honour to a collection that already includes the European Championship.

Yamal believes those achievements, alongside his performances, strengthen his claim for the award.

“On the pitch I enjoy myself,” he added. “I have also been lucky enough to win a lot of trophies with Barcelona.

“And I won the biggest trophy of them all, the World Cup with my national team. But beyond all that, I think the way I play is the strongest argument and what makes me different.”

Yamal dreams of joining football’s greats

Despite insisting the Ballon d’Or is not an obsession, Yamal admits he dreams of winning it and wants his career to leave a lasting mark.

The teenager has repeatedly spoken about establishing his own identity rather than being compared with the likes of Messi or Pele.

“Yes, I dream of winning [the Ballon d’Or],” he said. “I always say that everyone has to aim as high as possible. If I was a waiter, I would want to own the restaurant.

“I play to make history, so that in 30 years kids say: ‘He was really good.’ But it’s not an obsession. I never think ‘I want to be better than Pele or Messi.’ I don’t want to compare myself with others.

“I want to be Lamine Yamal. I want to be remembered as Lamine Yamal. I hope to be remembered among the greats. I have the capacity to do it; it depends on me.”

“I already knew he scored loads of goals, but training with him every day, seeing his mentality, he has dazzled me even more,” Diaz told ESPN.

“It’s difficult to sum him up in one word. Brutal, maybe… magnificent. For me, it’s hard to find the perfect word to describe him.

“For me, he’s the No.1 candidate to win the Ballon d’Or. I hope he wins it.”

articles.title: Roberto De Zerbi still the man to turn Tottenham’s fortunes around despite sitting bottom of Premier League
articles.summary: Proof Roberto De Zerbi has Tottenham heading in the right direction
articles.content:
Roberto De Zerbi still the man to turn Tottenham’s fortunes around despite sitting bottom of Premier League

Proof Roberto De Zerbi has Tottenham heading in the right direction

Last Update:

Tottenham are bottom of the Premier League after five matches. They have not won a game while scoring only twice, conceding  eight times and collecting two points.

It is the club’s worst start to a Premier League season after five games, surpassing the 2008-09 campaign when they also had two points but a slightly better goal difference of -3.

They have also lost 22 home league matches since the beginning of 2024-25, only one fewer than they had suffered across the previous four seasons combined.

Yet the league table only tells part of the story.

Across their first five league games, Spurs have taken 71 shots, with 19 on target, while averaging 60.4% possession. Their 4.47 expected goals is more than twice the two goals they have actually scored. At the other end, they have conceded eight goals from 9.22 expected goals against.

The attacking output remains poor. An average of 0.89 xG per game is nowhere near the level expected from a side who spent more than £300 million rebuilding their squad in the summer.

The numbers do show a team capable of getting into useful positions.

The first match, a 3-0 defeat at Brentford, was poor. Spurs managed only nine shots and generated just 0.47 xG, while Brentford produced 25 shots and more than four times as much expected goal value.

The next three league games produced more encouraging attacking numbers.

Against Newcastle, Spurs lost 2-0 despite having 17 shots and six on target. They had 57.5% possession and created 1.05 xG. At Nottingham Forest, they had almost 60% possession and 11 attempts but failed to put a single shot on target.

Against Everton, they had 62.3% possession, 14 shots and 37 touches inside the opposition box. They did not score. Then came Aston Villa.

Tottenham lost 3-2, but had 20 shots and seven on target, controlled 63.8% of possession and won 11 corners.

The problem is conversion. Tottenham’s first Premier League goal did not arrive until their 67th shot of the campaign, when Conor Gallagher finally scored against Villa.

It ended a 492-minute drought dating back to Joao Palhinha’s strike against Everton on the final day of last season.

That is a serious attacking issue, although it is one that can change quickly with better finishing, a settled front line and the integration of new players.

Premier League 2026

England

Rebuilds require time

The scale of Tottenham’s summer overhaul is the main focus of any assessment of their start.

More than £300 million was spent, with Sandro Tonali, Mateus Fernandes, Jan Paul van Hecke, Marcos Senesi, Andy Robertson, Savio and Omar Marmoush among the arrivals.

Savio and Marmoush were signed after the opening-day defeat at Brentford, so two of the most significant attacking additions were not available for the first fixture.

The defensive unit changed too. Robertson, Senesi and Van Hecke arrived while Cristian Romero, Djed Spence and Guglielmo Vicario departed. Antonin Kinsky became the first-choice goalkeeper.

This was a fundamental change of direction rather than a routine transfer window, which usually consists of adding weapons to an already existing firing squad.

De Zerbi admitted as much after the opening-day defeat at Brentford when he said: “We are not a team yet.” Four new defenders had started that game and the squad was still being assembled at the time.

Opta’s analysis of the first four matches found that Spurs had made 12 changes to their starting XI from game to game, more than they had ever made in the opening four matches of a Premier League season.

They were also the 12th non-promoted side in Premier League history to give 20 or more starts in their first four matches to players who had not played for the club the previous season.

Of the previous 11, only five improved their league position from one season to the next.

That record does not guarantee Spurs will improve. It does illustrate how unusual their opening weeks have been.

There is another reason to expect the side to look different later in the season: last year’s Tottenham attack was already short of the required standard.

Spurs scored only 48 Premier League goals in 2025-26, their lowest total over the previous four seasons, while finishing with a -9 goal difference.

Set pieces carried a huge portion of the attacking workload. 36.9% of Tottenham’s expected goals and 39.6% of their actual goals came from set plays, the highest proportions in the league.

That route has been reduced by the departures of players such as Palhinha and Romero. The new Tottenham is designed to create more through controlled possession and positional play instead of relying so heavily on dead-ball situations.

De Zerbi’s record at Brighton provides some evidence for what Tottenham are attempting to build.

From his first Premier League game in charge in October 2022, Brighton averaged 1.97 non-penalty expected goals per game, the best figure in the division over that period at the time.

His first full season ended with Brighton finishing sixth, scoring 72 goals and collecting 62 points, all club records at the time.

There were obvious risks in his approach. Brighton regularly invited pressure in their own half before trying to play through it. Over almost two seasons under De Zerbi, only three Premier League teams had more high turnovers than Brighton, while only two had conceded more high turnovers that led to an opposition shot.

That risk has appeared at Tottenham as well. The difference is that De Zerbi now has a group recruited specifically to execute his ideas.

Patterns from last season

De Zerbi is not starting from zero at Tottenham. He already had seven Premier League matches in charge at the end of last season.

That spell produced three wins, two draws and two defeats. He collected 11 points and kept Spurs in the Premier League on the final day with a 1-0 win over Everton.

So far this term, De Zerbi has taken two points from five league games, leaving questions over whether his methods are translating quickly enough into results.

He has had a full pre-season, substantial financial backing and a squad strengthened around his tactical preferences. Spurs remain vulnerable when matches become chaotic and have struggled to convert long periods of possession into goals.

Tottenham’s first four league matches produced just 2.22 xG from open play, the lowest figure in the Premier League at that stage. Their set-piece xG stood at only 1.22, also among the lowest figures in the division.

That means the argument cannot simply be that Spurs have been unlucky in front of goal.

There are signs of a side that is still becoming familiar with the new system. James Maddison is an important example.

Maddison only returned to team training shortly before the Aston Villa game after a lengthy absence and had played just 15 minutes against Liverpool in the Carabao Cup.

His return is relevant because Tottenham have been short of creativity in central areas. A fit Maddison gives De Zerbi another player capable of dictating the tempo and finding passes between the lines.

Tottenham’s next five games will reveal all

The international break gives De Zerbi another period to work with the squad.

Tottenham will not play another Premier League fixture until October 10, when they travel to Manchester United. They then face Coventry City at home, Chelsea away, Crystal Palace at home and Leeds United away before November.

There is little margin for more bad results, but there is time for the team to settle.

Savio has already started four of Spurs’ five league matches. Marmoush has played regularly. Tonali has become a central figure in midfield. Maddison is back in the group. Mohammed Kudus is finally fit again.

Spurs are creating more territory than their position suggests, averaging 60.4% possession and 14.2 shots per game across the opening five matches. They took 37 touches inside the Everton box and produced 20 shots against Villa. Their 4.47 xG is not remotely compatible with only two goals unless the finishing and final ball are major problems.

The defensive figures are less alarming than the scoreline either. Eight goals conceded from 9.22 xGA suggests Spurs have not consistently been overwhelmed by chance quality. Individual errors and lapses have proved expensive.

Five matches is also a tiny sample when compared with an entire season. Tottenham themselves provide a historical reminder. They were bottom of the Premier League after five matches in 2008-09 and eventually finished eighth.

That should not be used as a forecast for De Zerbi’s team, as the circumstances are completely different. It does show how quickly an early table can change.

The more relevant question is whether Tottenham’s current squad possesses the ingredients for a substantial improvement.

The attack needs to become far more productive. Two goals from 71 shots cannot continue. The defence has to cut out cheap mistakes. De Zerbi also has to demonstrate that his possession-heavy style can survive the Premier League’s physical demands.

Benjamin Sesko vows to ‘fully dedicate’ himself to recovery from shin injury

Benjamin Sesko has opened up on his recent injury issues at Manchester United

Last Update:

Manchester United striker Benjamin Sesko has vowed to “fully dedicate” himself to recovering from his ongoing shin problem after being ruled out of Slovenia’s upcoming matches.

The 23-year-old joined United from Leipzig last August in a deal worth £66.3m and scored 12 goals during his first season at Old Trafford, but his campaign ended prematurely after he suffered a shin problem in May.

The injury also prevented Sesko from featuring in any of United’s pre-season friendlies, although he returned to action at the start of the new campaign and played in each of their first six matches.

Sesko scored twice during that run before experiencing a recurrence of the shin pain, ruling him out of Sunday’s 1-1 draw at Fulham.

Nations League 2026: Sesko ‘sorry’ to miss Slovenia games

Sesko said he was “very sorry” to be missing Slovenia’s Nations League games in September and October, hosting Scotland and North Macedonia and visiting Switzerland and the Tartan Army.

“I have always played for Slovenia and will always play with heart and pride,” Sesko wrote on Instagram. “The most important thing now is to fully dedicate myself to recovery.

“I am already working on getting back on the field as soon as possible and helping the national team and the club again.

“I believe in our boys, and I am sure that they will show the team spirit that has always adorned us this time.

“I can’t wait to be able to wear the jersey with the national emblem again and, until then, I will be Slovenia’s biggest fan.”

Sesko among four United players to miss international duty

Sesko is one of four United players who have withdrawn from international duty during the three-week break.

Kobbie Mainoo and Marcus Rashford have both pulled out of the England squad, while Karl Darlow will not join up with Wales.

United confirmed that each player will undergo an individual recovery programme while the club’s first team is not in action.

“Each of the players will be assessed and undergo individual recovery plans during the current three-week international break.”

articles.title: Javier Tebas: Real Madrid call for La Liga president to leave over ‘intolerable attacks’
articles.summary: Madrid want La Liga boss Javier Tebas replaced
articles.content:
Javier Tebas: Real Madrid call for La Liga president to leave over ‘intolerable attacks’

Madrid want La Liga boss Javier Tebas replaced

Last Update:

Real Madrid have said La Liga president Javier Tebas should be replaced by “a leader capable of managing” the competition “with the fundamental duty of neutrality”.

Tebas, who was appointed in 2013, claimed Madrid were “living in another galaxy” after the club and manager Jose Mourinho criticised referee Miguel Angel Ortiz Arias, Video Assistant Referee official Daniel Trujillo Suarez and the standard of officiating in Spain following their 2-1 defeat at Atletico Madrid on Sunday.

In a statement hours after Tebas’ remarks on social media, Madrid accused the 64-year-old of being “obsessively focused” on them and “turning our club into the constant target of his public attacks”.

Real Madrid: Full statement on Javier Tebas

“Our club considers it intolerable that the president of La Liga uses his institutional position to continue discrediting and attacking Real Madrid in the manner he does during each of his public appearances,” said Madrid.

“It is very concerning that someone responsible for representing and protecting the interests of all La Liga clubs remains obsessively focused on Real Madrid, turning our club into the constant target of his public attacks.

“His latest remarks are especially serious and incomprehensible, unbecoming of a responsible executive, as they are based on an article by an independent journalist in a digital publication.

“However, he reacts against our club, even going so far as to evaluate our sporting strategy, which is utterly inappropriate and irresponsible.

“It is entirely surprising that the president of LaLiga dedicates his time and personal platforms to consistently attempting to discredit Real Madrid publicly, rather than contributing, as his position demands, to fostering trust in the institutions that are supposed to ensure the impartiality of the competition.

“By doing so, he continues to damage the image of our competition and Spanish football worldwide.

“Given this inappropriate and persistent behavior, we believe that the professional football competition in Spain urgently needs a leader capable of managing it and realising its full potential with the fundamental duty of neutrality.

“It requires someone who understands the nature of their role, as the president of LaLiga is not the owner of the competition but a manager serving the clubs that comprise it and entrust him with its leadership.

“The clubs need someone who serves this mission with honesty.”

What did Javier Tebas say about Real Madrid?

“Claiming that referees are directed against Real Madrid is living in another galaxy,” Tebas wrote, also referencing the two defeats Madrid have suffered across their past three matches, leaving them six points behind leaders Barcelona after seven league games of Mourinho’s second spell in charge.

“That narrative serves as an excuse to cover up other shortcomings that are plain to see in these first matches of the season.

“It’s more comfortable to point to a conspiracy than to explain what’s happening on the pitch.”

Atletico vs Real Madrid: Mourinho criticises Arias

After holding up photos of challenges between Madrid’s Jude Bellingham and Federico Valverde and Atleti’s Cristian Romero and Lee Kang-in, Mourinho said he had not reviewed Dean Huijsen’s second-half red card for pulling back Giuliano Simeone, which resulted in Alejandro Grimaldo scoring a penalty before Jonathan David added the hosts’ second to move 2-0 ahead..

Mourinho alleged that the circumstances surrounding the referee’s appointment had been wrong and suggested the VAR official had a history of poor decisions against Madrid.

Arias is in his seventh season as a Liga official and is the first from Madrid to have overseen the fixture, according to Marca. The outlet, who named him as their best referee of the 2021/22 season, said he is a PE teacher.

What Jose Mourinho said about referees after Atleti vs Madrid

“It was all very strange,” Mourinho said. “The first thing is that a week before the match, it was already known who the referee would be when, as I’ve been told, it should be announced 24 hours before.

“A week before, it was already known who the referee was. Then, it’s a 41-year-old referee who isn’t even international, and it’s not because he’s a great referee.

“The poor guy came here and couldn’t handle the pressure, which I call the pressure of the ’80s – something you rarely see today.

“Then there’s Mr Trujillo, who was on VAR… he has a very complete history as a VAR in Real Madrid matches.

“Last season alone, there was the Real Sociedad match in the Copa del Rey, and then there [were games against] Osasuna and Girona.

“This is a VAR with a lot of history. This combination: a poor referee who has only officiated small games and a VAR official with a long history.

“Congratulations to the referee appointment committee.”

Atletico vs Real Madrid: Mourinho wants ‘peace’

“If they leave us alone, in peace and let us compete on equal terms with everyone, there’s still a long way to go,” Mourinho said of his complaints in the context of a potential title challenge.

“I don’t want to go too far and say this was prepared. I don’t want to think that. I want to think they simply made mistakes. Just as a coach or a player can make mistakes, I want to think the referee committee made mistakes.

“Poor people – they made mistakes, sending someone who’s 41 years old and has never been in a situation like this, alongside someone else with a very rich history against Real Madrid.”

Atletico Madrid: Jose Mourinho ‘referee harassment’

Having moved a point ahead of Madrid, Atleti were quick to poke fun at their rivals with a series of tweets on X.

The first was a video showing a sheet of paper coming out of a printer with the words #StopAcosoArbitralYA, meaning “stop referee harassment now”.

A second post showed a picture of Mourinho at the news conference with the same message.

articles.title: Kylian Mbappe reveals his mother ‘fell in love’ with Liverpool during transfer talks
articles.summary: Kylian Mbappe has opened up on how he nearly joined Liverpool.
articles.content:
Kylian Mbappe reveals his mother ‘fell in love’ with Liverpool during transfer talks

Kylian Mbappe has opened up on how he nearly joined Liverpool.

Last Update:

Kylian Mbappe has revealed that his mother “fell in love” with Liverpool during negotiations over a potential move to Anfield before he ultimately chose to join Paris Saint-Germain.

Mbappe was one of the most sought-after young players in Europe when he left Monaco in 2017, with Liverpool among the clubs attempting to convince the France international to continue his career on Merseyside.

The forward has now explained that he was “close to Liverpool”, with his mother particularly keen on the idea of seeing her son play at Anfield.

“It was while I was playing in Monaco. I had to take a decision. And yes, I was close to Liverpool. My mum was a big fan of Jürgen Klopp and the favourite destination for my mum was Liverpool. She wanted me to go there.

“I didn’t listen because I wanted to play in my city, Paris. I didn’t want to leave my country before I was someone. But yes, my mum was always saying ‘Liverpool – you’re going to be there, playing at Anfield, it’s going to be insane for you.’ I was like, ‘OK!'”

Mbappe’s mother even travelled to Liverpool as part of the early negotiations, visiting the city and Anfield before returning to discuss the possibility with her son.

“She went there [for] the first step of the negotiations. She went to the city, she went to the stadium, she met the people. She was like, ‘It’s a wonderful club, everybody’s so kind, it’s a family club, a big club.’

“She went to Anfield and fell in love with it. She watched a few games alone, to feel the atmosphere, because she wanted to imagine me in this stadium.”

Klopp went all out to convince Mbappe

Former Liverpool manager Jurgen Klopp has previously revealed just how far the club went in an attempt to sign Mbappe.

Speaking while working as a pundit during the World Cup, Klopp recalled how a Liverpool delegation travelled from Blackpool to Nice to meet Mbappe and his family on a private jet.

“Liverpool really pulled out all the stops,” Klopp said. “We just flew in circles, talked with the family, and had a delicious meal. We weren’t allowed to be seen.

“We flew in circles – it was great – and then he went to Paris!”

Mbappe also remembered the unusual meeting, explaining how Klopp used the flight to outline Liverpool’s plans for his future.

“I remember we were on the plane and we were turning around and around in the air while he was explaining his project,” Mbappe said.

“I said, ‘You don’t need to convince me. You’re Jürgen Klopp, it’s Liverpool, a great club, so of course if I’m here, I have some interest. But I have other things, other projects, that are also good.’

“I said to him, ‘Whatever decision I take is going to be a good decision because we are talking about some of the biggest clubs in the world.'”

articles.title: ‘Stop blaming the refs, Jose!’ La Liga chief Tebas says Mourinho needs to look closer to home to sort Real Madrid issues
articles.summary: Real Madrid are fourth in La Liga and Javier Tebas believes Jose Mourinho has more pressing issues than the standard of refereeing
articles.content:
‘Stop blaming the refs, Jose!’ La Liga chief Tebas says Mourinho needs to look closer to home to sort Real Madrid issues

Real Madrid are fourth in La Liga and Javier Tebas believes Jose Mourinho has more pressing issues than the standard of refereeing

Last Update:

La Liga president Javier Tebas has laughed off suggestions that Real Madrid are victimised by Spanish referees and suggested Jose Mourinho looks a little closer to home to find the root cause of their current problems.

Mourinho took the predictable step of blaming match official Miguel Ángel Ortiz Arias and VAR Daniel Trujillo Suárez for the 2-1 defeat at city rivals Atletico at the weekend.

The Portuguese even brought printed photos of incidents that he claimed should have resulted in the dismissals of Cristian Romero and Lee Kang-in to the post-match press conference.

Instead, the only player to see red in Atleti’s victory was Madrid defender Dean Huijsen for bringing down Giuliano Simeone.

The officiating has brought accusations of bias from sections of the Madrid-based media but Tebas says that is not the case.

He wrote on social media: “Claiming that referees are directed against Real Madrid is living in another galaxy.

“That narrative serves as an excuse to cover up other shortcomings that are plain to see in these first matches of the season.

“It’s more comfortable to point to a conspiracy than to explain what’s happening on the pitch.”

Jury still out on Mourinho’s second stint at Real Madrid

His remarks were clearly directed at Mourinho, whose antics on Sunday did little to quell the suspicion he is ill-suited to close the gaping chasm between Madrid and two-time defending champions Barcelona.

“The story of the game is here,” Mourinho said after the game at the Metropolitano, holding up the images of the two challenges. “They’re two clear red cards. With the difficulties we had afterwards – with 11 versus 10 [players] – you could imagine what it would have been like [for us] for 50 minutes with 11 versus nine.

“It’s the CTA [the referee’s committee]. It’s all been very strange. It’s a referee [Ortiz Arias] who, at 41, doesn’t have international experience. I don’t know why he was the referee. The poor guy came here and couldn’t cope with the pressure.

“But for [the VAR] there’s no pressure, at [RFEF HQ] Las Rozas there’s no pressure. Or maybe there is and we don’t know. That combination – a poor referee, who’s only done small games, and a VAR with a big history. Congratulations to the CTA.”

Atletico quick to poke fun at Mourinho’s Madrid

The result left Madrid in fourth, already six points adrift of table-topping Barca and one behind Atletico, who were quick to poke fun at their rivals with a series of tweets on X.

The first was a video showing a sheet of paper coming out of a printer with the words #StopAcosoArbitralYA, meaning “stop referee harassment now”.

A second post showed a picture of Mourinho at the news conference with the same message.

articles.title: Wayne Rooney opens up on possibility of Manchester United losing ‘special talent’ JJ Gabriel
articles.summary: Wayne Rooney has had his say on the potential departure of JJ Gabriel.
articles.content:
Wayne Rooney opens up on possibility of Manchester United losing ‘special talent’ JJ Gabriel

Wayne Rooney has had his say on the potential departure of JJ Gabriel.

Last Update:

Wayne Rooney has admitted it would be “disappointing” for Manchester United to lose highly-rated youngster JJ Gabriel, describing the 15-year-old as a “special talent”.

Gabriel has asked to leave United despite being regarded as one of the club’s most promising academy players, with Barcelona and Real Madrid among the clubs monitoring his situation.

The teenager turns 16 next month and recently made an impressive UEFA Youth League debut against Sabah, scoring a hat-trick.

Rooney, who has watched Gabriel develop through his son Kai’s age group, said United have made significant efforts to convince the youngster to remain at Old Trafford.

“I have seen JJ grow up, he has been in [my son] Kai’s team,” Wayne Rooney told Stick To Football on Disney+. “Anyone close to it knew that was coming.

“In fairness to Manchester United they have done everything, absolutely everything, to keep him at the club.

“The club have treated him probably differently to the other players because he is such a special player. I know, I recognise that, because I was that player at Everton. I was getting that treatment at Everton.

“As a club, you need to do [it] to try to keep the better players.

“It’s disappointing because he is such a top player and a lovely kid.

“You never know whether it’s gone too far or whether there is a chance for him to stay.”

Rooney compares Gabriel to his own Everton breakthrough

Rooney knows better than most what it is like to be identified as an exceptional young player at an early age.

The former England and Manchester United striker became the Premier League’s youngest goalscorer when he scored for Everton against Arsenal in 2002 at the age of 16 years and 360 days.

That record has since been broken by Arsenal youngster Max Dowman, who scored against Everton in March aged 16 years and 73 days.

Rooney believes Gabriel has shown many of the qualities required to progress through the age groups and eventually make the step into senior football.

“He is a top player,” Rooney said of the 15-year-old. “His ability, his balance, he has shown he can go up the ages and score goals. The next step is first-team football where it’s different, and you never know until you’re in there.

“But he’s such a special talent who understands the game really well.”

Rooney expects Gabriel to be ready for first-team football

United are understood to believe there is still a possibility of resolving the situation and keeping Gabriel at the club.

Rooney suggested the youngster could have been given an opportunity in Ruben Amorim’s first team at some point this season had he remained at Old Trafford.

The former United captain said Gabriel’s development means he is already approaching the point where senior football could become his next challenge.

“At some point this season he would [have] made his debut for the first-team, I’d imagine, so that’s where it’s disappointing.”

articles.title: Infantino open to FIFA reform amid ongoing criticism
articles.summary: FIFA President GIanni Infantino is open to reform.
articles.content:
Infantino open to FIFA reform amid ongoing criticism

FIFA President GIanni Infantino is open to reform.

Last Update:

FIFA president Gianni Infantino says he is open to an independent review of the governing body’s decision-making processes following the collapse of the FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) project.

Infantino sent a letter to FIFA Council members and the organisation’s 211 member associations on Monday, outlining proposals for an external assessment ahead of the next FIFA Council meeting on October 15.

The move comes after the FFE plan faced opposition from several football bodies and prompted calls for greater scrutiny of FIFA’s governance.

“I will ask the Council whether it wishes to commission an external, independent assessment of FIFA’s current governance framework for major strategic initiatives and to recommend potential improvements,” Infantino stated in his letter, which was seen by The Associated Press.

“I will propose that the Council establish a direct, structured, and time-bound consultation with the confederations and member associations on how to further strengthen FIFA’s decision-making processes,” he added.

The FFE concept involved private investors acquiring a stake in FIFA’s commercial rights, including those linked to the World Cup and other competitions. The proposal was withdrawn in July following opposition from UEFA and other confederations.

FIFA Forward Enterprise plan sparks backlash

The FFE proposal became public before FIFA’s planned institutional process had been completed, according to Infantino, who acknowledged that this created concerns among member associations.

“The proposal entered the public domain before FIFA’s planned institutional process had been completed and before it could be presented in full to the Council and the member associations. I recognize that, without full context, this caused concern and created the impression that decisions had already been taken. They had not,” Infantino said in the letter.

The fallout has led to demands for greater transparency and independent scrutiny from within the football community. UEFA and CONCACAF presidents Aleksander Ceferin and Victor Montagliani recently called for an independent review of FIFA’s financial reserves, while several football associations have questioned the organisation’s handling of the FFE proposal.

UEFA has also sought documents and testimony from FIFA entities in the United States as part of its consideration of potential criminal proceedings in Switzerland relating to the FFE plan.

UEFA has alleged that the proposal was developed without adequate consultation with FIFA’s governing bodies, claims that FIFA has disputed.

Infantino remains committed to increasing FIFA revenue

Despite withdrawing the FFE proposal, Infantino said FIFA would continue looking for ways to increase its resources and invest more money into football.

“Withdrawing this proposal does not diminish our ambition or our responsibility to reinvest a greater share of the fruits of FIFA’s success into football. We will continue to explore sustainable ways to increase FIFA’s resources,” Infantino added.

“What changes is not the ambition, but the strength of the process.”

articles.title: Manchester United is now a soulless football club and Ratcliffe, Carrick and Fernandes must shoulder the blame
articles.summary: Sunday's draw with Fulham typified the apathy at Manchester United - a club at which the passion has long since drained away...
articles.content:
Manchester United is now a soulless football club and Ratcliffe, Carrick and Fernandes must shoulder the blame

Sunday's draw with Fulham typified the apathy at Manchester United - a club at which the passion has long since drained away...

Last Update:

There are few clubs in English football that stir the emotions quite like Manchester United.

Those last-minute winners in Fergie time, Roy Keane thundering into a challenge, or berating a match official with his veins popping, those battles with Arsene Wenger’s Arsenal, memorable nights in Europe and the ultimate success in Barcelona.

There was always a sense of occasion when Manchester United came to town, a ring around the date in the calendar.

And yet, watch them now and the overriding sense is apathy, of indifference.

The brutal truth is United have lost their sense of being. No longer are they the standard bearer, no longer do they command respect and admiration from neutrals. From top to bottom, they are a shell of what they used to be.

The disconnect between majority owners, the Glazers, and the fanbase is well known and continues to rumble on with no end in sight. There was hope the partial buyout by Sir Jim Ratcliffe – a self-confessed United fan – would improve the dynamic but, if anything, it has gone the other way.

The redundancies, the penny-pinching towards staff that dodged the cuts, the awful treatment of loyal fans, the lack of love afforded to Old Trafford, the list goes on.

Added to that are a series of catastrophic managerial decisions; needlessly prolonging Erik ten Hag’s stay before sacking him and bringing in Ruben Amorim, before ditching the affable yet hapless Portuguese. It is now looking increasingly like Michael Carrick’s tenure will be short-lived as well.

Carrick worked wonders after replacing Amorim in January, guiding the club to a place in the Champions League. But his success meant United had no choice but to give him the role on a full-time basis. And that, as we have seen countless times, rarely works.

Carrick appears a good man. He’s just a bad fit.

And so here we are, heading into the international break with United in 12th place and Carrick presiding over the club’s worst start to a Premier League season in 13 years.

United are static, on and off the field

Much of the focus has been on the players’ lack of intensity, an issue that really came to the fore in the weekend draw at lowly Fulham.

This season in the Premier League, Carrick’s team are: last in sprints made, last in distance covered at high intensity, last in the amount of time spent at high intensity and last in the amount of time sprinting.

At Craven Cottage, standard-bearer, captain and best player Bruno Fernandes sprinted for 35.2 yards across the 90+ minutes. 35.2 yards… let that sink in.

Can you imagine Keane sprinting for 35.2 yards at his pomp? And can you imagine what Keane would have done to Fernandes in the dressing room after finding out his team-mate had sprinted for 35.2 yards?

Sir Alex Ferguson would not have tolerated this lack of effort or intensity.

Carrick is a very different character, and that’s absolutely fine. In some ways, it is refreshing to have an element of calm on the touchline and in post-match interviews. Surely everyone is sick and tired of the new wave of ‘Jack-in-the-box’ coaches like Mikel Arteta, Andoni Iraola and Matthias Jaissle?

But it’s hard to imagine Carrick stirring the inner feelings of players, pushing them to the limit in the way Ferguson did. An unfair comparison? Quite possibly. More modern equivalents are Pep Guardiola and Jurgen Klopp. They inspire, Carrick’s dead-pan approach flatlines the emotions.

Carrick will go but the problems at United will remain

So, where does this leave United?

They have players who don’t sprint, don’t press, don’t seemingly care.

They have a manager who fails to inspire, whose tactics are questionable, and is clearly on borrowed time.

And they have owners the fans despise.

The owners aren’t going anywhere, bar perhaps Ratcliffe to his overseas mansion. He will continue to talk about business practices and a lack of confidence in the UK while presiding over the failure of one of its great sporting institutions.

That leaves Carrick as the inevitable fall guy. He will slip into the history books alongside Ten Hag and Amorim and few will bat an eyelid.

Fernandes will continue to wander around, focusing more on his personal numbers than the greater good, huge sums will be spent on good, not great, players and United will finish well behind Arsenal and Manchester City. It would be a surprise if they finished above the likes of Brentford and Brighton.

Manchester United is now a cold football club. The fans provide the heart and soul but there is little else to cling to.

The 2026/27 Nations League gets underway this week, with some huge fixtures taking place across League A. There are also plenty of intriguing […]
articles.content:
England face the world champions as Klopp, Xavi and Zidane make bows: Five Nations League games to look out for

Last Update:

The new-look, three-week international break is here and while Premier League fans will be counting down the days until club football returns, there is plenty to keep an eye on across Europe.

The 2026/27 Nations League gets underway this week, with some huge fixtures taking place across League A. There are also plenty of intriguing storylines, from new managers taking charge to some heavyweight nations meeting early in the competition.

Here, 101 Great Goals are five games that should be firmly on the radar.

Netherlands vs Germany – September 24

The Nations League gets off to a flying start with one of European football’s biggest rivalries, as the Netherlands welcome Germany to Amsterdam.

It will also be the first competitive game in charge for both managers, with Jurgen Klopp beginning his Germany reign and Xavi Hernández taking charge of the Netherlands.

That alone makes this one impossible to ignore, particularly when you consider that neither nation have exactly thrived on the pitch in recent years, so there is plenty of pressure on both bosses to claim an early win.

Germany reached the semi-finals of the previous Nations League, while the Netherlands made it to the quarter-finals, and both will be looking to make a fast start this time around.

Portugal vs Wales – September 24

Portugal begin their title defence against Wales in Lisbon, with Jorge Jesus’ first task since becoming Selecao boss being to defend their Nations League crown.

Cristiano Ronaldo remains the obvious headline, but Portugal have an abundance of attacking talent around him and will expect to control proceedings at the Estadio Jose Alvalade.

Wales, meanwhile, will be hoping to spoil the party and make a statement against the reigning Nations League champions, with Craig Bellamy hoping to eventually get Wales back at a major tournament once again.

It is a difficult opening assignment, but these are exactly the sort of fixtures that can provide a team with a huge boost if they can produce a result.

Italy vs Belgium – September 25

A day later, Italy face Belgium in what should be another fascinating League A encounter.

Italy missed out on the 2026 World Cup, so there is plenty of attention on returning boss Roberto Mancini as he begins his second spell in charge of the Azzurri.

Belgium, meanwhile, arrive after reaching the quarter-finals of the World Cup and will be looking to carry that momentum into the Nations League.

With both sides looking to establish themselves in a new cycle, this feels like an important early test rather than simply another group-stage fixture.

England vs Spain – September 26

England get their Nations League campaign underway with arguably the biggest fixture of the lot, as Spain visit Wembley.

The game will bring together two of Europe’s heavyweight nations and provides England with an immediate test against the reigning world champions.

It also gives Thomas Tuchel’s side the chance to begin to win over fans once again, with plenty of questions still hanging over the Three Lions’ semi-final capitulation against Argentina in the United States.

There will be no shortage of quality on show, either, with a chance to see Real Madrid and Barcelona stars Jude Bellingham and Lamine Yamal go head-to-head, while Trent Alexander-Arnold, Morgan Gibbs-White and Rio Ngumoha will hope to impress after being added to the squad since the World Cup.

Belgium vs France – September 28

And just when the first batch of fixtures appears to be winding down, Belgium and France go head-to-head in Brussels.

France will be starting a new era under Zinédine Zidane, who takes charge of his first competitive match against Turkey earlier in the break, before facing Belgium three days later.

Belgium, meanwhile, could have already faced Italy by this point, meaning their opening Nations League schedule is anything but gentle.

It could be an early indicator of where both sides stand in League A, with two heavyweight squads going up against each other in what should be another cracking contest.
