articles.title: Five England players to watch during the international break
articles.summary: Tuchel's England squad has a number of new and returning faces
articles.content:
Five England players to watch during the international break

Tuchel's England squad has a number of new and returning faces

Last Update:

The Premier League may be on hold for now, but there is certainly no shortage of intrigue around England during the international break.

Thomas Tuchel’s side return to action this week for the first time since reaching the semi-finals of the World Cup with a packed four-game window, beginning with a mouthwatering meeting with world champions Spain at Wembley.

The England boss has also had to shuffle his pack from the original squad he named, with Declan Rice, Cole Palmer, Kobbie Mainoo, Marcus Rashford and Tino Livramento all withdrawing through injury.

James Garner and Morgan Gibbs-White have been drafted in, while several members of the squad have a golden opportunity to make their mark.

Here are five names worth keeping a particularly close eye on over the next few weeks.

Trent Alexander-Arnold

Few England players generate as much conversation and intrigue as Trent Alexander-Arnold.

The Real Madrid star has been handed a way back into the international picture after being left out of England’s World Cup squad, with Tuchel impressed by his performances in Spain at the start of the season.

Now comes the hard part: turning that recall into a regular place in the team.

Alexander-Arnold offers something few defenders can match with his range of passing and ability to dictate play from deep.

With four matches on the schedule, he should have plenty of opportunities to remind Tuchel exactly what he can do.

Morgan Gibbs-White

Gibbs-White was not initially part of Tuchel’s squad, but Cole Palmer’s injury has opened the door for the Nottingham Forest midfielder.

The timing could hardly be better for Gibbs-White, who has started the season in excellent form and already has six England caps under his belt.

His ability to carry the ball, create chances and operate between the lines gives Tuchel an interesting option in an attacking midfield role.

Having been handed a late reprieve, Gibbs-White will be desperate to make sure this is more than just a short-term call-up.

Rio Ngumoha

At only 18 years old, Rio Ngumoha is one of the most exciting prospects in the England squad.

The Liverpool winger has already tasted senior international football, but this could be a much bigger opportunity to show Tuchel that he can be trusted at the highest level.

Ngumoha plays with the sort of fearlessness that can make young attackers so dangerous. Tuchel has previously praised his courage and adventurous approach, and England fans will be hoping to see plenty of both.

Four games in a single international window could provide the teenager with a valuable chance to gain experience alongside England’s established stars.

Alex Scott

Alex Scott’s call-up is a reward for a seriously impressive start to the season with Bournemouth.

Tuchel singled out the midfielder when explaining his squad selection, highlighting Scott’s performances in the Premier League.

The timing is particularly interesting given the absences of Declan Rice and Kobbie Mainoo. Scott now has a chance to show that he can handle the demands of international football and compete for a place in an increasingly competitive midfield.

The 22-year-old is still waiting for his senior England debut, so this could be a defining few weeks in his development.

Jarrad Branthwaite

Jarrad Branthwaite has been waiting patiently for another opportunity in an England shirt, and he now has one.

The Everton centre-back has only one senior cap to his name, but his physical attributes have long made him an intriguing option for the Three Lions.

Branthwaite combines considerable size with pace and an ability to play out from the back, qualities that Tuchel clearly values.

With four matches to navigate and a number of players unavailable, the 24-year-old has a chance to make a serious impression and strengthen his case for a more permanent role in the squad.

England’s international break fixtures

England’s first test comes against Spain at Wembley on Saturday, September 26, before Tuchel’s side travel to Prague to face Czechia four days later.

Croatia await in Rijeka on October 3, with England then hosting Czechia at Wembley on October 7.

articles.title: The sack race: Which Premier League managers are already at risk after five games?
articles.summary: Roberto De Zerbi and Michael Carrick are feeling the heat just five games in
articles.content:
The sack race: Which Premier League managers are already at risk after five games?

Roberto De Zerbi and Michael Carrick are feeling the heat just five games in

Last Update:

We may only be five games into the Premier League season, but a host of managers may already at risk of the sack after poor starts to the season.

The international break is so often a time when clubs opt to change managers and the new extended three-week break from action could leave a number of vulnerable bosses looking over their shoulders.

101 Great Goals takes a look at the five managers most at risk of the sack.

Roberto De Zerbi

Roberto De Zerbi is arguably the manager under the most pressure heading into the international break, with Tottenham sitting bottom of the Premier League after five games.

Spurs have picked up just two points and their 3-2 defeat at home to a previously winless Aston Villa on Saturday means they are still searching for their first win of the campaign.

Their lack of goals is particularly concerning, with De Zerbi’s side finding the net just twice in their opening five league games despite considerable investment over the summer.

The international break gives him time to work with his squad, but another poor result when Tottenham return could leave his position in serious doubt.

Michael Carrick

Michael Carrick’s Manchester United have endured another frustrating start, with Sunday’s 1-1 draw at Fulham leaving them with just five points from their opening five matches.

Having led United to Champions League qualification last season, Carrick would have expected a much better beginning to the new campaign, but performances have been inconsistent and Sunday’s late equaliser only rescued a point.

United’s huge expectations mean pressure can build quickly, particularly when results aren’t coming. Their first game back after the international break is against Tottenham, making it a potentially huge fixture for both Carrick and De Zerbi.

Alvaro Arbeloa

Alvaro Arbeloa has also found himself under some early pressure after Fulham’s winless start to the Premier League campaign.

Sunday’s 1-1 draw with Manchester United was another frustrating result, particularly after Fulham had taken the lead and looked on course for all three points.

The former Real Madrid defender has not yet reached the kind of crisis point facing De Zerbi, but Fulham need to start converting promising performances into victories.

The international break could provide Arbeloa with valuable time to work with his squad before a crucial run of fixtures.

Pierre Sage

Pierre Sage is another manager worth keeping an eye on, although the pressure around the Crystal Palace boss is nowhere near as intense as it is at Tottenham or Manchester United.

Palace have made a mixed start to the campaign and Sunday’s goalless draw at Leeds means they are still searching for the consistency needed to push towards the top half of the table.

Sage will have time on his side, but a prolonged run without victories would inevitably increase the scrutiny. For now, he remains one to watch rather than an immediate candidate to lose his job.

Frank Lampard

Frank Lampard may have given himself some breathing room with Coventry’s first Premier League victory of the season on Saturday.

The 1-0 win away at Nottingham Forest was particularly important after a difficult opening to the campaign and will allow Lampard to head into the international break with some much-needed positivity.

Coventry will still need to improve significantly if they are to avoid being dragged into a relegation battle, but the victory has eased some of the immediate pressure.

A poor run after the break, however, could quickly see Lampard back in the sack-race conversation.

articles.title: ‘Stop referee harassment now’: Atletico take swipe at Mourinho after fiery Madrid derby
articles.summary: Mouringo printed out sheets showing two Atletico challenges he thought were red cards
articles.content:
‘Stop referee harassment now’: Atletico take swipe at Mourinho after fiery Madrid derby

Mouringo printed out sheets showing two Atletico challenges he thought were red cards

Last Update:

Atletico Madrid have hit back at Jose Mourinho after the Real Madrid manager brought printouts of two controversial refereeing decisions in the Madrid derby to his post-match press conference.

Mourinho accused officials of missing two red cards decisions in Real’s 2-1 defeat at the Wanda Metropolitano on Sunday.

Atletico have responded in typical style, posting a series of times on their X account, the first being a video showing a sheet of paper coming out of a printer with the words #StopAcosoArbitralYA, meaning “stop referee harassment now”.

The second then showed a picture of Mourinho at the press conference with the same message, posting for a third time with the message: “This year they have a new challenge. Three weeks without League. This season they start very early.”

It is not the first time Atletico have used their social media account to poke fun at their rivals, with the club repeatedly mocking Barcelona following their failed pursuit of striker Julian Alvarez.

Alongside Mourinho’s post‑match claims, the match report published on Real’s website said that the derby loss was decided because of the dreadful refereeing” of Ortiz Arias.

Despite Mourinho feeling that the hosts should have seen two red cards, it was a Real player who was actually dismissed, with Dean Huijsen sent his marching orders for denying Guiliano Simeone a goalscoring opportunity.

Alejandro Grimaldo scored from the resulting penalty before Jonathan David made it 2-0 only six minutes later to put Atleti in command.

Antonio Rudiger reduced the deficit in the 89th minute but it did not stop Los Blancos suffering defeat for the second time in LaLiga this season, with Mourinho’s side already six points behind leaders Barcelona in the table.

Mourinho: The story of the match is right here

“We can skip the press conference because the story of the match is right here,” Mourinho said as he showed media the printed images on sheets of A4 paper on Sunday.

“Those were two clear red cards. Given the difficulties we faced afterwards playing 11 against 10, we can only imagine what 50 minutes of 11 against nine would have been like.

“So I’ll just have to limit myself to hugging my players, who gave it their all and played a first half, showed great class and character, setting us up perfectly to win the second half.”

Simeone, when asked to respond to Mourinho’s refereeing rant, said he was always respectful of everyone else’s opinions.

“I understand that we’re in a privileged position with a lot of public scrutiny, as coaches, and whether it’s Mourinho, [Barcelona manager Hansi] Flick, [Real Betis boss Manuel] Pellegrini, me, or anyone else, we need to be careful about what we say,” he said.

“We have to know how to respect others, the referees, our colleagues. And when someone crosses that line of respect, it’s not right – you can’t cross that line.”

Man United striker Sesko set for tests after withdrawing from Slovenia squad

Sesko scored 12 goals last season after joining from RB Leipzig, helping United finish third in the Premier League.

But he has struggled for fitness to start the 2026-27 campaign, in which he has scored two goals so far.

articles.title: Premier League: 5 key talking points as City steal early march in title race and Carrick comes under fire
articles.summary: Manchester City go into the international break top of the Premier League, while Tottenham sit at the foot of the table.
articles.content:
Premier League: 5 key talking points as City steal early march in title race and Carrick comes under fire

Manchester City go into the international break top of the Premier League, while Tottenham sit at the foot of the table.

Last Update:

The Premier League season takes an extended pause for three weeks as international football reassumes control of the football calendar, and Manchester City will doubtless be the happiest team in the division going into the break.

City, hoping to wrest the title back from Arsenal, have taken maximum points from their five league games this term, despite a somewhat unconvincing performance against Sunderland on Sunday.

The mood among City fans will be in stark contrast to those of a Manchester United persuasion, following another difficult result for Michael Carrick’s side.

For Tottenham fans, the break at least brings a temporary halt to the disappointment after their latest defeat, which will make the break an especially difficult one for Roberto De Zerbi following a winless start to the new campaign.

Here we look at five of the biggest talking points from the fifth round of Premier League fixtures.

Title rivals both show their frailties

The title race looks destined to be a two-horse race, with City taking a three-point lead over defending champions Arsenal into the break after their thrilling 5-3 win over Sunderland.

That followed the Gunners slipping up with a 3-0 defeat at Brighton and Hove Albion but, even with the difference in results, both City boss Enzo Maresca and Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta have problems to ponder during the season’s first interlude.

For all their obvious prowess going forward, City were far too easy to break down against Sunderland. Brian Brobbey became the first Premier League player to score a hat-trick and end on the losing side since 2007, and the Netherlands striker had a simple finish for all three goals as the Black Cats cut City open with little difficulty each time.

Maresca may point to City’s clean sheets in the four games prior — only two of those matches were in the Premier League — but there is still a clear vulnerability about his side that was obvious in their narrow opening-day win over Bournemouth. The good news for him is that Arsenal have obvious issues too.

The complete breakdown of Arsenal’s typical defensive solidity at Brighton may ultimately just be a blip, but the lack of cohesion in midfield between Declan Rice, Bruno Guimaraes and Martin Odegaard represents a potentially bigger problem.

It is further forward where Arsenal may have their greatest concern after a game in which Kai Havertz failed to fire. With Viktor Gyokeres clearly second choice to the German, the Gunners need Havertz to consistently deliver. If he cannot, then it’s hard to see Arsenal having the firepower to compete with a City side that has so much in the way of ammunition.

Jacquet impresses again, but Iraola faces Wirtz pressure

It’s often said that a mark of a great side is winning when you don’t play well, and  Liverpool’s efforts in their 1-0 victory at still winless Bournemouth on Sunday could at best be described as uninspiring, with Alexander Isak’s fourth goal of the season proving the difference.

The standout performer for the Reds was centre-back Jérémy Jacquet, who continues to impress following his £60million move from Rennes.

Jacquet, per FotMob, was credited with three tackles, a block, two clearances, two interceptions and six recoveries. He also won three of his four duels, with the Frenchman’s partnership with Virgil van Dijk blossoming as Liverpool have kept three successive clean sheets in the league.

While there is reason for optimism at the back, there is mounting concern over the performances of Florian Wirtz, who was criticised heavily by Jamie Carragher after the win at the Vitality Stadium.

Carragher urged Iraola to consider dropping Wirtz ahead of Liverpool’s clash with City after the break. Should Iraola heed that advice, it will be a significant setback for Wirtz’s hopes of ever justifying his £100m fee.

Can Seagulls or Bees gatecrash the Champions League places?

Brighton’s demolition of Arsenal came under 24 hours after Brentford dispatched another team viewed as a potential title contender in empathic fashion, brushing aside Chelsea 3-0.

With the Blues strong start under Xabi Alonso stalling, Manchester United, Aston Villa and Tottenham all struggling in the opening weeks and Newcastle United transitioning to a new era under Matthias Jaissle, the performances of Brighton and Brentford naturally raise the question of whether either of them can break their way into the Champions League places.

Both sit in the top four after five games and have displayed defensive solidity while getting goal contributions from several areas. Indeed, Brighton (16) and Brentford (10) are among just four teams to have hit double figures in the league so far this term.

But the underlying numbers suggest Brighton, who have a xG against of 8.7, should have conceded more than the five goals they have allowed. The big test for Fabian Hurzeler’s men will be maintaining the momentum as their Conference League fixtures pile up after the break, while a testing run of games upon the resumption that sees the Bees face Villa, Liverpool and surprise package Hull City will reveal a lot about Brentford.

Early evidence suggests there could be a top-five opening for one of these teams, and their meeting on the south coast on November 7 will have a great deal of intrigue if they are both still in the upper reaches of the table.

Is it time for Carrick to go?

The prolonged honeymoon for Michael Carrick is well and truly over.

After his outstanding spell as interim Manchester United manager last season, Carrick has endured an extremely difficult start to his tenure as permanent boss, and there are likely to be calls for that stint to end following an underwhelming display in a 1-1 draw at Fulham on Sunday.

Former defender Gary Neville hit out at United’s effort off the ball in scathing remarks made while working as the co-commentator for Sky Sports.

“I’ve watched Manchester United since the age of five and that’s the worst 15 minutes I’ve ever seen,” Neville said after Fulham took the lead through a Lisandro Martinez own goal. “Absolutely pathetic.

“I’ve never seen such a lack of effort. What must [Michael] Carrick be thinking?”

Though Neville’s comments will be written off by many as bizarre hyperbole on the part of a United legend, his words speak to a significant issue for the Red Devils in a league that demands high energy from teams hoping to be successful.

Sky Sports said on Monday that GeniusIQ data ranked United last in the Premier League for distance covered at high intensity, time occupied at high ​intensity, total sprints and time spent sprinting.

With United sitting a lowly 12th in the table after a summer in which they only added to the midfield, the anger at the club’s hierarchy will persist over the international break. However, it’s clear the finger is also starting to be pointed at Carrick and, unless he can get his side producing high-intensity and match-winning performances, time may soon run out on his managerial career at Old Trafford.

Are Spurs set for relegation battle?

It was another miserable weekend for Tottenham, who will now spend three weeks propping up the Premier League following their latest defeat to Villa and Fulham’s draw with United.

Tottenham did at least finally end their wait for a Premier League goal this season, but the damage had been done by the time Conor Gallagher and Jan Paul van Hecke found the net to make the scoreline more respectable.

Van Hecke, a £52m signing from Brighton, is part of Spurs’ many problems. The Dutchman is performing poorly at the heart of a defence that remains far too easy for teams to breach, with Johan Manzambi, Nicolas Jackson and Emi Buendia profiting in Villa’s 3-2 victory.

The midfield has energy, but there is a distinct lack of creativity in a side on which over £300m was spent in the summer. Tottenham have an xG of 5.0 this season, the third-worst in the Premier League.

With Roberto De Zerbi given that kind of backing, the hope was Tottenham would be well clear of danger after two 17th-place finishes in the last two seasons. Instead, Spurs are a team that look destined for another scrap. Tottenham don’t create enough opportunities and they are leaky at the back. It’s a recipe for disaster, and De Zerbi must find a way to fix it over the course of the break.

articles.title: Who has impressed across the first five weeks? Our Team of the Premier League season so far…
articles.summary:
There have been some stand-out performers across the first five weeks of Premier League action. 
Here's our best XI.
articles.content:
Who has impressed across the first five weeks? Our Team of the Premier League season so far…

There have been some stand-out performers across the first five weeks of Premier League action.

Here's our best XI.

Last Update:

The Premier League is on an extended international break and does not return until October 10.

It is, therefore, a good time for a little reflection and to look back across the first five matchdays and identify the players that have stood out in August and September.

Only one team has two players in the best XI and, unsurprisingly, that is leaders Manchester City.

GOALKEEPER

James Trafford (Leeds)This was always going to be a big season for Trafford after joining Leeds from Manchester City. The England international moved to Elland Road in the summer and started a top-flight campaign as a club number one for the first time. He has not disappointed, conceding just three times, and making a league-best 20 saves, as part of a strong start from Daniel Farke’s side.

DEFENCE

Anan Khalaili (Crystal Palace)Khalaili had the difficult job of replacing Daniel Munoz down the right side of the Palace defence but has done a sterling job. It has not been a seamless transition from Oliver Glasner to Pierre Sage at Selhurst Park but 22-year-old has been one of the shining lights with a series of strong displays. Khalaili has made a league-best 21 tackles and added 15 clearances and, at the other end, also got on the scoresheet in the defeat to Ipswich.

Semi Ajayi (Hull)Few pundits foresaw Hull’s fine start to the season with the Tigers heading into the hiatus in eighth place. Ajayi has been a mainstay of a defence that has conceded just four goals in five games and also got the season up and running with the opening goal in their 2-0 victory over Manchester United on the opening day.

Jeremy Jacquet (Liverpool)Jacquet has had fans purring with a string of fine performances at the heart of the Liverpool defence. The 21-year-old missed the bulk of last season due to a shoulder injury but has already formed a strong partnership with Virgil van Dijk. It remains early days but Jacquet already looks the natural heir to Van Dijk as the leader of the Reds’ back four.

Lewis Hall (Newcastle)Hall suffered the disappointment of being snubbed by Thomas Tuchel for a place in England’s World Cup squad. It was a decision that appeared mystifying at the time and even more baffling now given his strong start to the season. Newcastle managed to retain Hall when other big-name players departed over the summer and the left-back has responded with a series of impressive displays defensively and he also grabbed a goal in the win over Hull on Saturday.

MIDFIELD

Elliot Anderson (Manchester City)Trying to replace Rodri in the Manchester City midfield is a thankless task but Anderson has been a huge contributor for Enzo Maresca over the first five weeks of the season. The pressure was on Anderson following his big-money move from Nottingham Forest but he has been a key driver in City winning their first five games and sitting top of the tree.

Martin Odegaard (Arsenal)After a difficult couple of seasons. Odegaard has sparkled in the opening weeks. Prior to Saturday’s dismal display at Brighton, Arsenal looked firm favourites to retain their Premier League trophy with Odegaard providing the creative spark in midfield.  The Norway international scored matchwinning goals against Chelsea and Napoli and also notched in the opening night victory over Coventry.

Pascal Gross (Brighton)The veteran German has been a revelation in Brighton’s strong start. Now 35, he has lost none of his creativity and has excelled in a youthful Seagulls midfield with his nous and the energy around him moulding together to form a formidable unit. Gross ran the show against Arsenal on Saturday, scoring the opener and supplying the corner from which Chema Andres also netted. His weekend display came on the back of a goal and two assists against Coventry and another goal against Manchester United in the EFL Cup.

ATTACK

Cole Palmer (Chelsea)Xavi Alonso has made a mixed start to life at Chelsea but his problems lie in defence. Palmer has shone at the other end, striking up a strong working relationship with Joao Pedro and Morgan Rogers. His form saw him recalled to the England squad only for him to pull out due to injury. Palmer has four goals and two assists in all competitions and there will be plenty more to come.

Kevin Schade (Brentford)Germany international Schade is one of the most underrated forwards in the top flight. Pacy, direct and with an eye for the spectacular, the 24-year-old already has three goals to his name – two against Bournemouth in a 2-2 draw and the equaliser as the Bees drew at Leeds. Those three goals came from an xG of just 1.52.

Erling Haaland (Manchester City)There is no other number nine in world football who can match Haaland’s numbers. He already has seven goals in all competitions from five appearances. He also completed the set of scoring against all the other Premier League teams after notching against Sunderland at the weekend. The big Norwegian is firmly on course to win the Golden Boot for the fourth time in five seasons.

England: Rice, Rashford, Mainoo and Livramento join Palmer in withdrawing from Nations League squad

Morgan Gibbs-White and James Garner will come into the squad.

Last Update:

Arsenal star Declan Rice has withdrawn from the England squad for their upcoming UEFA Nations League matches, with Manchester United pair Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo and Newcastle United’s Tino Livramento also joining Chelsea’s Cole Palmer pulling out through injury.

Palmer’s withdrawal was reported earlier on Monday, and the Football Association confirmed he will be replaced in the squad by Nottingham Forest’s Morgan Gibbs-White.

Midfielder Rice played the full game on Saturday as Arsenal suffered their first loss of the new season, a 3-0 defeat at Brighton and Hove Albion.

Rashford and Mainoo came off late in United’s 1-1 draw at Fulham and are being assessed by their club.

Newcastle full-back Livramento has consistently struggled with injuries in recent times, with a hamstring problem preventing him from featuring at the World Cup after he was selected for the tournament in North America.

Having recovered from that issue, Livramento missed Newcastle’s 2-1 win over Hull City on Saturday through his latest setback, the nature of which has not been confirmed.

England face Spain at Wembley on Saturday before two games with Czechia, which take place either side of a trip to Croatia.

articles.title: ‘He wouldn’t be in my Liverpool team’ – Carragher urges Iraola to make Wirtz decision after ‘poorest’ display
articles.summary: The Reds legend was highly critical of the Germany international.
articles.content:
‘He wouldn’t be in my Liverpool team’ – Carragher urges Iraola to make Wirtz decision after ‘poorest’ display

The Reds legend was highly critical of the Germany international.

Last Update:

Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola has been urged to make a decision on dropping Florian Wirtz by Jamie Carragher, who described the Germany forward’s performance against Bournemouth as his poorest for the club.

Wirtz has struggled to live up to the hype following his £100million move from Bayer Leverkusen last summer, with his displays attracting consistent criticism.

The 23-year-old has seven goals and nine assists in 55 games for the Reds, his only official goal involvement this season coming in a 2-2 draw with Nottingham Forest.

Per FotMob, Wirtz created three chances in Sunday’s 1-0 win at Bournemouth, which was secured by a second-half strike by Alexander Isak.

Wirtz was a part of the build-up play for that goal as he failed to get on the end of Cody Gakpo’s right-wing cross to the near post before it was tucked home by Isak.

He is credited with nine chances created in the Premier League, with only Dominik Szobszlai and Gakpo ahead of him among Liverpool players in that regard.

But Carragher was far from impressed with Wirtz, and believes it is time for Iraola to seriously think about his position in the team.

“That was one of the poorest I’ve ever seen him in a Liverpool shirt,” Carragher said on ‘The Jamie Carragher podcast’.

“I’ve been critical of the fact that he hasn’t got the numbers. But normally when you watch Wirtz, he’s neat and tidy, he keeps possession, there’s things that you like. He gets out of a tight situation where you’re normally expecting your player to lose the ball.

“But the reason I worry is, I don’t think Wirtz is in poor form since he came to Liverpool. I actually think what we’re seeing is what he is.

“And I was worried for Wirtz probably 12 months ago. And maybe that was a little bit early to say that, but I didn’t say it. It was just in the back of my head.

“I commentated on Liverpool away at Burnley and Liverpool won with a late penalty from Mo Salah. And when I was watching that game it was what I’ve seen for the last 12 months: I don’t see how he’s going to hurt you. It’s just neat and tidy. And in some way, the price tag for that type of player should be half of what Liverpool have paid.

“The worry for Wirtz now is that his performances so far, or what he’s given Liverpool, is so low. Where we were expecting him was to take Liverpool to another league title, to take Liverpool to a Champions League.

“The gap he’s got to get to almost justify what people were expecting, I almost think is too big. You can’t get there. Even if he improves a bit and gets there, it’s still not what Liverpool thought they were getting.”

Carragher: Iraola has a decision to make

Carragher went on to make a series of damning comparisons to similar players at other clubs, with the former Liverpool centre-back adamant Wirtz is not playing at a high enough level to justify selection when they face Manchester City on October 11 after the three-week international break.

“I think going forward Iraola’s got a decision to make here. Wirtz would not be in my Liverpool team,” added Carragher.

“I thought this Bournemouth game was a big game for Wirtz. Because if he doesn’t produce [against Bournemouth], he’s then going to have a three-week break. By the time we come back, we’re into October. Before you know it, it’ll be Christmas in six to eight weeks, or it’ll feel like we’re getting to Christmas. He has to do something!

“If you go through the Premier League and think of players in his position – not just for the top teams, forget the top teams who we should be judging him against, I’m talking about normal Premier League players in the middle of the table – who have done more for their clubs.

“I think of Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall at Everton. No one out there would say Dewsbury-Hall is a better player than Wirtz, or would go for more money than Wirtz, or would cost £120m. But every three or four weeks he scores a goal.

“I watched Morgan Gibbs-White for Nottingham Forest last week at Aston Villa, and in the second half he put in a performance in 45 minutes that Florian Wirtz has never done before for Liverpool.

“I’ve seen a goal Emiliano Buendia scored for Aston Villa at Tottenham. Again, these players aren’t going to get over £100m, or £120m, but they’re still giving their clubs bits every few weeks.

“Wirtz wouldn’t be in my Liverpool team. Manchester City at home, for me, he can’t be in the team.”

Carragher has been impressed with the ruthlessness Iraola has shown in his brief tenure at Liverpool in dropping other big-name players, and indicated he wants him to replicate that with Wirtz.

“The things I’ve liked so far about Iraola, he’s had the courage to make big decisions,” Carragher explained. “Ryan Gravenberch has just signed a hefty contract on a five-year deal on massive money, because they thought him and Szoboszlai were going to be the future of the midfield going forward. He’s not playing.

“Now, I can imagine the guys at the top of the club looking at that, thinking we’ve just given him a hefty contract. But no, he’s not playing.

“The full-back situation, he keeps changing the full-backs, he’s dropped Jeremie Frimpong straight away. Milos Kerkez has been in and out. So he’s made decisions.

“But sooner or later he’s going to have to make a decision on Florian Wirtz, and, for me, I hope it’s sooner. Not because I don’t like Florian Wirtz, I’m desperate for the kid to do well. I just want Liverpool to win. That’s it, basically.”

Can Klopp sprinkle stardust on Wirtz?

However, Carragher sees potential salvation for Wirtz during the international window, when he will work with former Liverpool boss and new Germany coach Jurgen Klopp.

“The one hope for Liverpool supporters now is Jurgen Klopp is the Germany manager,” said Carragher.

“Wirtz goes away with the Germany team for three weeks, and he’s obviously one of the best players in Germany, that’s how they see him. Can Jurgen Klopp sprinkle a bit of stardust on him in that position?

“Jurgen is one of the greatest managers in the world, we know that. And what he gets out of players is probably more than most managers because of the nature of his personality, and fingers crossed something can happen for him.

“There’s a scenario there that Jurgen Klopp and Germany have a great international window, he gets loads of goals, assists and comes back on a high. Manchester City’s the next game, he impacts that, all is forgotten, all is forgiven. There’s a potential turnaround there.

“I would love that to happen, I’d love him to be the match-winner against Manchester City.”

articles.content:
Gibbs-White to be called up to England squad as injured Palmer withdraws

Palmer reportedly has a minor injury.

Last Update:

Morgan Gibbs-White is set to be called up to the England squad for their upcoming UEFA Nations League fixtures as a replacement for the injured Cole Palmer.

Both Palmer and Gibbs-White missed out on the England squad for this summer’s World Cup, which saw the Three Lions finish third after a dramatic semi-final defeat to Argentina.

Chelsea forward Palmer was picked by Thomas Tuchel as England start their Nations League campaign with four games over the course of an elongated international break. Tuchel said Palmer, who has four goals and two assists for the Blues so far this season, needed to “justify the nomination”.

But it seems a minor injury will prevent him from doing so, with Nottingham Forest star Gibbs-White set to take his place, according to multiple reports.

Gibbs-White, who has one goal and two assists for Forest this term, last played for England in a friendly against Wales last October.

The 26-year-old has never started for England, with his six caps all coming as a substitute.

It is also anticipated that Manchester United pair Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo will drop out of the squad, with both players being assessed after coming off in the closing stages of the Red Devils’ 1-1 draw with Fulham on Sunday.

England face world champions Spain in their Nations League opener at Wembley on Saturday.

This international window will also see Tuchel’s men face Czechia twice, either side of a trip to Rijeka to take on familiar foes Croatia.

articles.title: Xhaka released from Switzerland squad after admitting obtaining a fraudulent Covid certificate
articles.summary: Granit Xhaka will not play for Switzerland during this international break after confirming he deceived authorities over his Covid status
articles.content:
Xhaka released from Switzerland squad after admitting obtaining a fraudulent Covid certificate

Granit Xhaka will not play for Switzerland during this international break after confirming he deceived authorities over his Covid status

Last Update:

Granit Xhaka will not play for Switzerland in their upcoming Nations League games after admitting to obtaining a fraudulent Covid certificate in 2022.

The Sunderland midfielder, who was then playing for Arsenal, has admitted he broke the rules due to “great reservations” about the vaccine.

He could face a criminal investigation in Switzerland and has, therefore, been released from the national team squad for the home and away games with North Macedonia either side of clashes with Scotland and Slovenia.

Xhaka wrote on Instagram: “At the time, I was personally very uncertain and had serious reservations. I felt a deep distrust of the vaccine and was plagued by fears and uncertainty.

“In that emotional state, I obtained a vaccination certificate instead of clarifying my unanswered questions through the proper channels. Today, I clearly see that this was not the right course of action. It was a mistake. I’m sorry.

“I take responsibility for this decision, will deal with the processing of the facts and co-operate fully with the relevant authorities.”

Swiss FA looking to ‘bring peace’ to Xhaka row

The Swiss FA will now tackle their Nations League games without the experienced midfielder.

A statement read: “After his personal statement, Granit Xhaka will not participate in the upcoming gathering of the men’s national team. This decision was made jointly in a conversation between Xhaka and the SFA management.”

SFA president Peter Knäbel added: “Granit Xhaka informed us about the facts last night and at the same time told us that he would speak out publicly and take responsibility.

“We welcome the fact that Granit is taking this step. At the same time, we have come to the conclusion together that it is in the team’s interest to dispute these games without him. For us, it is now a matter of bringing peace to the situation and focusing fully on the team and the upcoming challenges in the Nations League.

“At the conclusion of this international match window, we will reassess the situation together with Granit and discuss further procedures.”

Xhaka played the full 90 minutes as Sunderland lost 5-3 at Manchester City yesterday and is widely credited as being a hugely instrumental figure in the Wearsiders’ impressive return to the Premier League following promotion in May 2025.

The 33-year-old joined Sunderland from Bayer Leverkusen last summer having also played for Basle, Borussia Monchengladbach and Arsenal.

articles.title: Messi scores again but Dreyer double sees Inter Miami’s run of MLS draws stretch to four games
articles.summary: Lionel Messi was unable to drag Inter Miami to victory over San Diego as they were held to a fourth successive draw
articles.content:
Messi scores again but Dreyer double sees Inter Miami’s run of MLS draws stretch to four games

Lionel Messi was unable to drag Inter Miami to victory over San Diego as they were held to a fourth successive draw

Last Update:

Lionel Messi was on target but he could not help new Inter Miami coach Kily Gonzalez record a debut MLS victory as San Diego claimed a deserved 2-2 draw at Nu Stadium.

Messi netted his 101st Miami goal but was overshadowed by San Diego’s Anders Dreyer, who opened the scoring in the 12th-minute and then grabbed an 82nd-minute equaliser after Luis Suarez had put the hosts in front.

It was a disappointing outcome for Gonzalez, who was finally able to sit in the dugout for a league game after an issue with a work visa was resolved.

“We’ve been here for four days and haven’t been able to train properly. Defensively, we really need to be much stronger,” González said.

“We can’t commit these defensive horrors, they come at a high cost. That final situation shouldn’t have happened. It’s surreal to be in a position to win the game, yet nearly lose it.

“We only avoided defeat because our goalkeeper saved us.”

Gonzalez claims Inter Miami were complacent

Gonzalez’s first match in charge was the midweek win over Mexican side Cruz Azul in the Campeones Cup and the Argentine felt his side were still feeling riding the wave of that encounter.

“I think the Campeones Cup might have had an unconscious effect, especially in the first half, leading to a bit of complacency,” González added. “These are factors that are part of football. At a club where we are obliged to win every match we play, we have to rise to the occasion. We made significant adjustments at halftime to get the team flowing and ensure we stayed compact, keeping the lines tight so we wouldn’t suffer the way we did in the first half.”

Messi’s goal came via a 24th-minute free-kick that drifted past everyone in the box and flew into the far corner. It was his 20th league goal of the season but it was not enough to prevent Miami from recording a fourth successive draw.

The Floridian club are now third in the Eastern Conference, 11 points behind Nashville who have clinched a play-off spot.

articles.title: Jose Mourinho rants about referees again after Real Madrid defeat
articles.summary: Atleti beat Madrid to leapfrog their rivals in La Liga
articles.content:
Jose Mourinho rants about referees again after Real Madrid defeat

Atleti beat Madrid to leapfrog their rivals in La Liga

Last Update:

Jose Mourinho has strongly criticised referee Miguel Angel Ortiz Arias, Video Assistant Referee (VAR) Daniel Jesus Trujillo Suarez and the Liga refereeing committee after his side’s combustible 2-1 defeat at Atletico Madrid on Sunday.

After holding up photos of challenges between Madrid’s Jude Bellingham and Federico Valverde and Atleti’s Cristian Romero and Lee Kang-in, Mourinho said he had not reviewed Dean Huijsen’s second-half red card for pulling back Giuliano Simeone, which resulted in Alejandro Grimaldo scoring a penalty before Jonathan David added the hosts’ second in their 2-0 win.

Mourinho alleged that the circumstances surrounding the referee’s appointment had been wrong and suggested the VAR official had a history of poor decisions against Madrid.

Arias is in his seventh season as a Liga official and is the first from Madrid to have overseen the game, according to Marca. The outlet, who named him as their best referee of the 2021/22 season, said he is a PE teacher.

What Jose Mourinho said about referees after Atleti vs Madrid

“It was all very strange,” Mourinho said (via Madrid). “The first thing is that a week before the match, it was already known who the referee would be when, as I’ve been told, it should be announced 24 hours before.

“A week before, it was already known who the referee was. Then, it’s a 41-year-old referee who isn’t even international, and it’s not because he’s a great referee.

“The poor guy came here and couldn’t handle the pressure, which I call the pressure of the ’80s – something you rarely see today.

“Then there’s Mr Trujillo, who was on VAR… he has a very complete history as a VAR in Real Madrid matches.

“Last season alone, there was the Real Sociedad match in the Copa del Rey, and then there [were games against] Osasuna and Girona.

“This is a VAR with a lot of history. This combination: a poor referee who has only officiated small games and a VAR official with a long history.

“Congratulations to the referee appointment committee.”

Atletico vs Real Madrid: Mourinho wants ‘peace’

Madrid’s second defeat of Mourinho’s second spell in charge – both of which have come across their last three away matches in La Liga – has left them fourth after seven league games, six points behind leaders Barcelona.

“If they leave us alone, in peace and let us compete on equal terms with everyone, there’s still a long way to go,” Mourinho said of his complaints in the context of a potential title challenge.

“I don’t want to go too far and say this was prepared. I don’t want to think that. I want to think they simply made mistakes. Just as a coach or a player can make mistakes, I want to think the referee committee made mistakes.

“Poor people – they made mistakes, sending someone who’s 41 years old and has never been in a situation like this, alongside someone else with a very rich history against Real Madrid.”

articles.title: Carrick hails Manchester United response after another poor performance
articles.summary: Michael Carrick was not impressed with his side's performance in the 1-1 draw with Fulham.
articles.content:
Carrick hails Manchester United response after another poor performance

Michael Carrick was not impressed with his side's performance in the 1-1 draw with Fulham.

Last Update:

Manchester United manager Michael Carrick believes his side did enough to beat Fulham despite being held to a 1-1 draw in the Premier League.

United created a number of chances but were unable to find the winning goal, but Carrick was happy by the reaction of his players after Fulham took the lead.

“I thought we should have won the game, I thought we created enough to win the game,” Carrick told Sky Sports.

“The goal we did concede is one of them goals. The boys could have thought it is one of those days but I really like the reaction.

“We nearly won it in the end. We came to get the win of course, the way it panned out and the way we finished is the positive we take from it.”

Fulham goalkeeper frustrates United

Carrick believes Fulham’s Bernd Leno was the main reason United were unable to take all three points.

The visitors struck the woodwork twice and created several other opportunities, but the goalkeeper produced a number of important saves to keep the scores level.

“I think probably their goalkeeper really. The saves that he made today – he has probably made three top saves,” Carrick said.

“We have hit the post twice and had a load of opportunities. Of course we are not happy about not winning the game but there are things to take from it for sure.

“Football is a difficult game. We controlled a lot of the first half. It’s the Premier League and you will have spells where you don’t have it all your own way.

“To expect total dominance for the whole game, I don’t think anyone gets that in this league.”

Carrick sees positives despite dropped points

Despite United’s failure to claim all three points, Carrick was pleased with the energy shown by his players and believes there are plenty of positives to take from the performance.

“Yes,” Carrick said when asked if he was happy with the team’s energy.

“I think we can take a lot from today. I think we can learn a lot as well.

“We can be better at certain things, that is pretty clear, but there were some good signs today.”

articles.title: Lampard: Coventry players have ‘shown they can do it’ in Premier League after Forest victory
articles.summary: It was a memorable evening for the Sky Blues at the City Ground
articles.content:
Lampard: Coventry players have ‘shown they can do it’ in Premier League after Forest victory

It was a memorable evening for the Sky Blues at the City Ground

Last Update:

Coventry City boss Frank Lampard said his players have “shown they can do it” after picking up their first Premier League victory of the season.

Jay Dasilva scored the only goal of the game in a narrow 1-0 win over Nottingham Forest as the Sky Blues recorded their first top-flight win – and goal – in 25 years.

Igor Jesus saw what he thought was a late equaliser ruled out for a foul in the build-up as Coventry held on for a famous win at the City Ground.

Speaking after the game, Lampard could not hide his delight with the result.

The Coventry manager told Sky Sports: “I feel great, I feel amazing. The way the players worked for it. [It is a] tough place to come we knew that having lost our first four games all in different circumstances it’s easy to think negatively and think where is the goal and where it the win coming from?

“The reality in football is you have to fight for it, you have to work for it, you have to have organisation.

“I can go through so many players today and how they worked. You make your own luck in terms of VAR, I think it was a foul but when you work that hard I think the boys deserve it. It’s huge mentally for the team.”

Nottingham Forest

Coventry

‘Not everyone is Wayne Rooney’

Lampard said many of his players are experiencing Premier League football for the first time, and he hopes the win can help improve morale after a difficult start.

“Not everyone is a Wayne Rooney or a superstar that can just own it,” Lampard said.

“This can now hopefully give us confidence. The boys today have shown they can do it.”

Next up for Coventry after the lengthy international break is the visit of Newcastle, followed by a trip to Tottenham.

articles.title: Arteta laments ‘extremely poor’ Arsenal after Brighton defeat
articles.summary: It was a first loss of the season for the Gunners
articles.content:
Arteta laments ‘extremely poor’ Arsenal after Brighton defeat

It was a first loss of the season for the Gunners

Last Update:

Mikel Arteta admitted his Arsenal side were “extremely poor” after the Premier League champions fell to a 3-0 defeat to Brighton.

Pascal Gross, Charalampos Kostoulas and Chema Andres all found the net to give the Seagulls a famous – and thoroughly deserved – win over the Gunners, who endured a miserable afternoon on the south coast.

Arteta’s men were put under pressure from the opening stages, and found themselves two goals down before half-time.

Stunned, last season’s Champions League runners-up fell further behind after the break, and failed to muster any kind of comeback against a hugely impressive Brighton side.

The result marked a first defeat of the campaign for the north Londoners, with Arteta unable to hide his frustration at full-time.

“[It was] a really disappointing result and performance,” the Gunners boss told Sky Sports.

“Brighton were another gear up from us. We were extremely poor technically and not respecting the game.”

Brighton

Arsenal

‘This can happen again’

Despite his disappointment, Arteta was quick to praise the performance of the hosts, and insisted his players must learn from the experience.

The Arsenal manager added: “Credit to Brighton. They went up another gear. It’s a big lesson to learn. It doesn’t take away from what the team has done the last few weeks.

“But now we have to make sure we learn the lesson because this can happen again.”

Next up for Arsenal after the extended international break is the visit of Leeds United at the Emirates on 10 October, before welcoming French side Lille in the Champions League three days later.

articles.title: Premier League Review: Arsenal hammered, more misery for Tottenham and Hull lose unbeaten record
articles.summary: Arsenal were hammered at Brighton while there were wins for Aston Villa, Everton and Newcastle this afternoon. All the details are in our Premier League review.
articles.content:
Premier League Review: Arsenal hammered, more misery for Tottenham and Hull lose unbeaten record

Arsenal were hammered at Brighton while there were wins for Aston Villa, Everton and Newcastle this afternoon. All the details are in our Premier League review.

Last Update:

Arsenal’s winning machine suffered a rare malfunction as Mikel Arteta’s defending champions were thrashed 3-0 by in-form Brighton this afternoon.

The Gunners went into the contest having registered six victories from six games in all competitions to start the season but were a distant second best on the South Coast as Brighton completed a brilliant week with another superb display.

Pascal Gross was again at the heart of the Seagulls’ best moments, opening the scoring with a shot that eluded David Raya at his near post after 31minutes.

It was 2-0 on the stroke of half-time with Charalampos Kostoulas firing in from 25 yards after a swift counter-attack from the hosts.

Arsenal continued to look all at sea and it was no surprise when Chema Andrés marked his first Premier League start with a third, heading in Gross’ cross.

The defeat saw Arsenal slip to second behind Manchester City, who play Sunderland tomorrow.

Arsenal’s neighbours Tottenham also lose

It was a miserable afternoon for the North London clubs with Tottenham also losing, 3-2 at home to Aston Villa.

Johan Manzambi prodded in just before the break to give Villa, for whom it was a first win, the lead.

Spurs thought they had equalised in the second half but Mohammed Kudus’s effort was disallowed for offside against Andy Robertson.

It was cruel but Villa showed no mercy with Nicolas Jackson and Emi Buendia scoring to increase the visitors’ advantage.

Conor Gallagher did net Tottenham’s first league goal of the season with four minutes to go, and there was still time for Jan Paul van Hecke to add a second, but it was scant consolation.

Promoted teams Hull and Ipswich both beaten

Hull’s unbeaten start is over after they failed to come back from a nightmare opening seven minutes at Newcastle.

The hosts, who were thrashed at Leeds on Monday night, bounced back with early goals from Joe Willock and Lewis Hall putting them in command.

They could have had a third but Yoane Wissa saw his spot-kick saved by Hull goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis on the stroke of half-time after Jacob Murphy went down easily under the challenge of Sorba Thomas.

Mohamed-Ali Cho’s neat finish brought Hull back into the game but, despite plenty of late pressure, the Tigers could not find an equaliser.

Everton moved up to fifth with a hard-fought 1-0 win over 10-man Ipswich at the Hill Dickinson.

Thierno Barry’s 11th-minute goal put the Toffees ahead and their position was strengthened when Abdul Fatawu was sent off midway through the second half for a second yellow card after going down theatrically under minimal contact from James Garner.

The Tractor Boys still carried plenty of threat going forward and England goalkeeper Jordan Pickford had to make fine saves to deny Emersonn, Julio Enciso and Abdoul Ouattara.

Arsenal stunned by brilliant Brighton as champions trail on the south coast

The Premier League champions have it all to do in the second half at the Amex.

Last Update:

Premier League champions Arsenal were dealt an early blow on their visit to the south coast as Brighton took the lead at the Amex Stadium.

After a bright start, Fabian Hurzeler’s side put the visitors under immense pressure and deservedly broke the deadlock when Pascal Gross let fly from 20 yards to beat the outstretched hand of David Raya.

Brighton’s Charalampos Kostoulas had earlier forced a good save from Raya following Bruno Guimaraes’ error, as Mikel Arteta’s men struggled to establish a foothold in the game.

Kostoulas added further misery to Arsenal’s afternoon when he drilled home a second for Brighton after being afforded too much time and space on the edge of the box on the stroke of half time.

It meant the Gunners went into the break two goals down with a mountain to climb in the second half if the north Londoners have any hope of salvaging something from the game and preserving their unbeaten start to the campaign.

For Brighton, meanwhile, victory could see them rise to as high as third in the table.

articles.title: Tottenham are ‘fragile’ admits under-pressure boss De Zerbi after defeat to Aston Villa
articles.summary: Roberto De Zerbi bemoaned another defeat for his Tottenham side this afternoon as Aston Villa won the early kick-off 3-2
articles.content:
Tottenham are ‘fragile’ admits under-pressure boss De Zerbi after defeat to Aston Villa

Roberto De Zerbi bemoaned another defeat for his Tottenham side this afternoon as Aston Villa won the early kick-off 3-2

Last Update:

Roberto De Zerbi admitted his Tottenham side looked “fragile” after they slipped to another defeat this lunchtime.

Spurs were beaten 3-2 by Aston Villa to maintain their winless run and, although they did manage their first league goal of the season, it was scant consolation for De Zerbi, who is starting to come under increased pressure after a summer of heavy spending.

The hosts started superbly but were frustrated by the brilliance of Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki. And there was a sense of inevitability that they would be caught out at the other end.

And that’s exactly what happened as Johan Manzambi prodded in just before the break.

Spurs thought they had equalised in the second half but Mohammed Kudus’s effort was disallowed for offside against Andy Robertson.

It was cruel but Villa showed no mercy with Nicolas Jackson and Emi Buendia scoring to increase the visitors’ advantage.

Conor Gallagher did net Tottenham’s first league goal of the season with four minutes to go, and there was still time for Jan Paul van Hecke to add a second, but it was scant consolation.

We need to stay more focused – Tottenham boss De Zerbi

“I think we could score in the first half many, many times,” De Zerbi told TNT Sports. “We conceded the goal with 10 players [with Van de Ven off the pitch due to injury] but we had to stay more focused to defending that situation in extra time in the first half.

“In the second half we conceded a goal from the goal kick directly. Before then we scored but it’s offside. The third goal, a great goal of Buendia. But I have to say, we played well in the first half, we didn’t score but [we were] too fragile.”

Tottenham

Aston Villa

Spurs are struggling to score at one end and giving away too many goals at the other – a recipe for disappointment.

De Zerbi added: “Stronger, when we have 10 players, [for] one minute, we have to stay like a family in the goal area to defend. Not so easy, like the goal kick in the second half when we concede the second goal. It’s too little to concede a goal. To score one goal we have to create 20 chances and the others, just one half [chance], not one, because the goal kick is not a chance. Too easy for them to score.”

The final whistle was met with muted boos from the home fans that had remained and De Zerbi told them to direct their frustration at him.

“If we didn’t score it’s my responsibility,” he said. “I take the responsibility. We’re going to work harder, but football is like life. You are strong or you lose.”

Villa skipper McGinn delighted with first win

Spurs’ despair was matched in equal measure by Villa’s relief. Unai Emery’s men had also not won in the league this season and this victory will come as a huge boost heading into the international break.

Captain John McGinn told TNT Sports: “Leading up to the international break, you don’t want to be in the bottom three.

“I thought we were really poor first half, we showed nothing going forward, but the second half we stood tall and deserved the win.”

articles.title: Xabi Alonso admits ‘we must do better’ after dismal Chelsea thrashed by Brentford
articles.summary: Xabi Alonso looked shellshocked after his Chelsea side collapsed in the second half to lose 3-0 at Brentford
articles.content:
Xabi Alonso admits ‘we must do better’ after dismal Chelsea thrashed by Brentford

Xabi Alonso looked shellshocked after his Chelsea side collapsed in the second half to lose 3-0 at Brentford

Last Update:

Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso conceded “everything was disappointing” after his side suffered a 3-0 defeat at Brentford tonight.

Chelsea were arguably the better side in the first half but capitulated once Jaidon Anthony nodded the home side ahead from a corner just after the hour mark.

Igor Thiago scored his first goal of the season late on to make it 2-0 and Fabio Carvalho tapped in a third in injury time to complete an awful night for Alonso at the Gtech Community Stadium.

He told BBC Match of the Day: “Everything was disappointing, especially the result, but we can do better. We must do better. For 45 minutes we were competing well, but in the second half we dropped, and conceded the three goals. You need to be very focused, and once you concede from set-pieces, it gives them an advantage and control because once you concede the second goal it becomes much harder and we lost a little bit of our discipline when we were close to the box. We have to correct our mistakes.”

Chelsea offered little going forward while also looking defensively weak.

“First half we were around [the box] but not creating big chances,” said former Real Madrid boss Alonso. “We missed the last pass, the last dribble to get shots in clear positions, but that’s one part. The other part is when you need to hold, when you need to be tight, [the opponent] is trying to attack you and you need to know how to defend and stick together. Win duels and be consistent in that part.”

Lacking spark going forward and weak defensively – Chelsea’s issues laid bare

Chelsea have now shipped 12 goals in five Premier League games, the most in the top flight.

Alonso said: “It’s everything but for sure individual and collective details will have to be better, but it’s not only defensively, with the ball there are parts where we need to do better.”

Set-pieces remain a huge issue for Chelsea and England international Levi Colwill admitted they had to improve in that area for the club to move forward.

He told Sky Sports: “Not been good enough. At times we have been bullied in the box, we need to definitely improve with that. We have all got trust in our set-piece coach and still adjusting to new things. We do need to improve as a team.

“I don’t think spirit went down. It hurt and we tried to push for the equaliser and we got hit on the counter attack. I don’t think our spirit dropped.

“We still need to improve a lot. We can’t rely on our front three to pull us out of danger. The rest of us have to help as much as possible. We definitely have a lot of room to improve.”

Brilliant Brentford enjoy taste of victory

While it was a dismal night for Chelsea, it was one of celebration for Brentford, who lapped up the adulation of their supporters at the final whistle.

Boss Keith Andrews said: “I felt like there was something bubbling towards tonight and I have this unbelievable calm around our team because I trust them. I see a humility and hunger within the group and we can challenge each other.

“We have to continue to get better in this league, the money teams are spending on players but that’s just on paper, what we do every day in training is pushing boundaries, be open with each other and continue to go on this journey and I’m loving the journey.”

The win moved Brentford up to third ahead of the rest of the weekend games.

articles.title: King Kane nets 100th Bundesliga goal in record time as Bayern Munich rout Union Berlin
articles.summary: Harry Kane netted twice - including a landmark goal - as Bayern hammered sorry Union Berlin
articles.content:
King Kane nets 100th Bundesliga goal in record time as Bayern Munich rout Union Berlin

Harry Kane netted twice - including a landmark goal - as Bayern hammered sorry Union Berlin

Last Update:

Harry Kane became the quickest player to hit 100 Bundesliga goals as Bayern Munich crushed Union Berlin 7-0 on Friday.

The England captain reached the landmark with the first of two goals on the night, slotting home from the penalty spot after 39 minutes.

Kane got to three figures in just 98 games, 31 games faster than anyone else.

Strangely, he wasn’t the star of the show as Michael Olise scored a hat-trick to take his tally for the season to eight in all competitions. The France international netted his first with a superb shot from outside the area, skipped round the goalkeeper to add a second and then netted another curling effort to complete his treble.

Jamal Musiala had earlier opened the scoring for Bayern with summer signing Ismael Saibari also getting on the scoresheet.

The win moved Bayern to the top the Bundesliga but they could be overtaken by both Freiburg and Borussia Dortmund this weekend.

Monaco surge to the Ligue 1 summit

Monaco are top of Ligue 1 after edging out Lens 2-1.

Jonathan Gradit’s 84th-minute own goal proved decisive after Lens’ Matthieu Udol had cancelled out Paris Brunner’s opener.

In La Liga, Elche enjoyed their first win of the season with a remarkable 3-1 victory at Espanyol.

The visitors started the night at the foot of the table and even the most ardent Elche fan would have been fearing the worst when they had Federico Redondo sent off after just six minutes.

But two first-half goals from Fer Nino put them in charge. Victor Chust put through his own goal to give Espanyol hope but German Valera completed a wonderful night for Elche with their third with 12 minutes to go.

articles.content:
Zidane names five newcomers in first France squad, including Liverpool defender Jacquet

Zidane Zidane has not been shy in bringing new faces into his first France squad for upcoming games in the Nations League.

Last Update:

Zinedine Zidane has included uncapped quintet Guillaume Restes, Andy Diouf, Jeremy Jacquet, Lucas Da Cunha and Esteban Lepaul in his first France squad.

Zidane, who took over after Didier Deschamps retired following the World Cup, selected 20 outfield players and three goalkeepers for four Nations League games between September 25 and October 5.

Jacquet has been rewarded for a promising start to his Liverpool career while Da Cunha has been a prominent member of the Como side that has gone from Serie B to the Champions League over the past four years.

Zidane said: “It’s a first selection, a first gathering. The ideas were quite clear. You may have one or two players who are not there due to lack of playing time or a small injury, but there has been a lot of work since my appointment on July 28.

“This break is good with 15 days together, four matches to play. We will play every three days, so everyone will be involved. My way of seeing football? You will see it. I am excited by the games. I want to see this team play. We have the players.”

Zidane also confirmed Real Madrid striker Kylian Mbappe would retain the captaincy but there was no place for veteran midfielder N’Golo Kante, who went to the World Cup but did not play a single minute.

“It’s a choice, but I think there are players to develop this team,” added the former Real Madrid boss. “It has nothing to do with his [Kante’s] qualities. He is an extraordinary player in the French team. I congratulate him for what he did.”

articles.summary: Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca has eased expectations on his side.
articles.content:
Enzo Maresca warns Manchester City pressure can quickly mount

Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca has eased expectations on his side.

Last Update:

Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca is refusing to get carried away by his side’s impressive start to the season, insisting pressure can quickly increase if results begin to go against them.

City continued their winning run with a 5-0 win over Championship side Norwich in the Carabao Cup on Thursday.

The result was their sixth consecutive win in all competitions since losing to Arsenal in the Community Shield, giving Maresca a strong start after taking over from Pep Guardiola.

However, the former Chelsea boss knows expectations at City are high.

“I’m really happy. I said in the first press conference, for me to be in this club is a privilege and to be in this club after a legend like Pep is a privilege,” Maresca said.

“I know if I don’t win it’s a disaster, and it’s normal, but I don’t spend my day thinking who was here before and for how many years.

“I’m just here to focus on what we can do better, improve the team and trying to win games.”

City already planning for Sunday

Maresca was pleased to rest players who had featured heavily in recent matches, with City having beaten Porto and Manchester United before the Carabao Cup tie.

“It was very important we gave rest to the ones that played back-to-back 90 minutes against Porto and United,” he said.

“Hopefully they can be full of energy for Sunday’s game that will be a strong game.”

Maresca also suggested Samba could provide another option in attack, despite normally operating as a midfielder.

“We have Antoine [Semenyo] there, we can use Phil [Foden] and Rayan Cherki as a false nine. It depends on the gameplan,” he added.

“But Floyd played here, he was good and hopefully we can give him more chances.”

articles.title: Iraola ‘pushing’ Liverpool player over issue: ‘I suppose it will take some time’
articles.summary: Andoni Iraola will face former side Bournemouth on Sunday
articles.content:
Iraola ‘pushing’ Liverpool player over issue: ‘I suppose it will take some time’

Andoni Iraola will face former side Bournemouth on Sunday

Last Update:

Andoni Iraola says Ronald Araujo “needed” to join Liverpool on loan from Barcelona – and the Reds boss has identified one area he wants the defender to improve after his impressive start to his season-long spell at Anfield.

Uruguay international Araujo has been at Barca since 2018 but made a surprise switch to Liverpool on August 10 and has started their last four games in all competitions, comprising three wins, a draw and a total of two goals conceded.

“We knew each other because we played against each other, but not personally,” reflected Iraola, adding that the 27-year-old has adapted well to the physical demands of sometimes being asked to move from centre-back to right-back.

“Sometimes you talk to a player and you can feel it straight away: everything was positive. He needed this kind of change. He has come with humility from a big club.

“He’s probably played more minutes than we expected so early in the season. He’s finishing games in a good place and not cramping. I like his spirit.”

Ronald Araujo: How Liverpool loanee could improve

Each of the Liverpool defences Araujo has been a part of have featured four players of different nationalities and Iraola believes the three-time Liga winner would be even more effective if he spoke English.

“Now I’m pushing him to learn the language,” explained Iraola. “A good way for us to use his experience is if he could communicate better with teammates and use all of the experience he has. I suppose it will take time.”

Araujo is likely to feature again when Liverpool seek successive league away wins by visiting Iraola’s former club, Bournemouth, on Sunday.

Liverpool have won one and drawn three of their first four top-flight matches of the season, while Marco Rose’s Cherries, who qualified for Europe for the first time in their history by reaching the Europa League under Iraola last season, are on three points.

“It’s going to be a tricky one because they obviously know very well what we try to do, on the ball and without the ball,” said the Spaniard.

“I also have this advantage – I know their strengths, their weaknesses. It’s going to be strange for me. I don’t know if it’s a big advantage or a disadvantage, but it’s going to be different.”

articles.title: Carrick claims sacking is ‘not on radar’: ‘What do you want me to show?’
articles.summary: United have matched their worst start in the modern Premier League
articles.content:
Carrick claims sacking is ‘not on radar’: ‘What do you want me to show?’

United have matched their worst start in the modern Premier League

Last Update:

Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick says he is not close to losing his job and side’s poor form is not a “catastrophe or a disaster” or “the end of the world”.

In Carrick’s first full season in charge, United have lost three and won one of their first five domestic matches, including a 1-0 home defeat against 10-player Manchester City on Sunday and a 3-2 loss to Brighton & Hove Albion at Old Trafford in the EFL Cup on Wednesday.

“We don’t like losing matches,” said Carrick, reacting to what he perceived as a reporter suggesting he had not been sufficiently moved by audible supporter disgruntlement.

“It’s not like I don’t feel the emotion, but it doesn’t affect what we do next. I need to show more emotion? In what way? What do you want me to show?”

Manchester United results: Carrick takes blame

United spurned a 2-0 lead against Brighton, ending their 145-game unbeaten home run – including 143 wins – in matches in which they had been two goals ahead.

“We live in a world of instant reaction and judgement, which is fine,” said Carrick, who made United the form team in the Premier League after being appointed on an initial temporary basis in January, including securing Champions League qualification.

“It is what it is, but it’s not in my world. Being realistic and understanding this would come and learning about each other is really important.

“That’s why I’m here. It’s my responsibility, I’m fine with that. It’s not a blame game. We always search for things to look at and find the blame; sometimes it gets too much [a case] of wanting to find the blame.

“Blame me. It’s no problem, but it’s not about blaming people. It’s about finding solutions. It’s a whole collective thing. It’s about what you focus on, really.

“I’m totally happy taking responsibility – no problem with that. I know where we want to get to and we want to get there fast.”

Michael Carrick: United future ‘not on radar’

United are already eight points off the top of the table and three shy of the likely Champions League qualification places. “I think it will be a lot longer than one or two games of results,” Carrick said of the prospect of losing the backing of his bosses.

“Taking away all of that, it’s irrelevant for me. I know the club, I know the role, I know what’s expected here in terms of playing at a certain standard.

“In terms of future and ownership and how long I’ve got… it’s ridiculous to think that way in the position I’m in. It’s just not on the radar.

“I understand where we need to be and what the owners expect. I get all that. It is just two or three games [in which] we haven’t had certain results. We’ve got to perform and we’ve got a lot of games to plan for.

“I wouldn’t want to be anywhere else. It’s the best place for me to be. Sometimes when it’s not going to plan, the best way is to work through it and come out stronger.

“It’s a period of time when small things can become big things for other people. The key for us is to stay focused, stay on track. It can happen, as much as we don’t like it.

“The fact it’s happened in the first cluster of the season… if it happened in November, it’s maybe seen a little bit differently. But I was expecting a spell we had to work through.”

articles.summary: Lowly Spurs and Villa meet in the Premier League on Saturday
articles.content:
De Zerbi gives Spurs players message: ‘They have to understand’

Lowly Spurs and Villa meet in the Premier League on Saturday

Last Update:

Tottenham head coach Roberto De Zerbi says Tottenham’s players have his “full confidence” but “have to work” to match the physical demands of the Premier League in pursuit of their first league goal and win of the season.

Spurs host Aston Villa on Saturday with the clubs among the five not to have won any of their first four top-flight games of the campaign alongside Coventry City, Fulham and Bournemouth.

“We have to improve in everything,” said De Zerbi, whose team suffered their third defeat of the season in all competitions with a 3-1 defeat at Liverpool in the EFL Cup on Tuesday.

“You have to stay calm and be confident in what you’re doing. We conceded the first goal [at Liverpool] in a bad way… one long ball to [Cody] Gakpo [should not] be enough to concede.

“For the second, we could have closed Gakpo down [in a] better and stronger [way]. The third goal is individual quality from [Dominik] Szoboszlai.”

Tottenham vs Aston Villa: De Zerbi on Spurs fitness

De Zerbi, who took over on March 31, reiterated his suggestion that Tottenham are less fit than their rivals. “We started pre-season without a great physical condition,” said the Italian, discussing the three-week gap in their schedule after Saturday because of internationals.

“The players have to understand the intensity of the Premier League. They can’t lose all their physical condition [during the international break].

“They have to work and we have prepared a plan for individual training because, when the group comes back, we have to [restart] immediately.”

Dejan Kulusevski is still recovering from a knee injury that has kept the Sweden winger out since May 2025. “We have to manage Deki in the best way we can,” said De Zerbi.

“[His potential return] is a great thing for us because he is a good player and a good guy. He deserves to play again and we have to work day by day.

“For Deki, the international break is important because when he is at top condition and over the injury, he will be like another new signing.”
