articles.title: Arsenal boss Arteta warns referees over Sunderland row
articles.summary: Mikel Arteta expects Arsenal's game at Brighton to be 'beautiful'
articles.content:
Arsenal boss Arteta warns referees over Sunderland row

Mikel Arteta expects Arsenal's game at Brighton to be 'beautiful'

Last Update:

Arsenal head coach Mikel Arteta says his conversations with refereeing bosses will “remain private” but he wants officiating to “improve” following the row over the penalty his side conceded at Sunderland in the Premier League.

Arteta claimed the “game was unprotected” when John Brooks and Video Assistant Referee Stuart Attwell awarded a second-half spot kick following a tussle between Gunners defender Ezri Konsa and Sunderland counterpart Dan Ballard at the Stadium of Light last Saturday.

Visiting goalkeeper David Raya saved Enzo Le Fee’s spot kick, with Arsenal proceeding to win 2-0 – helped by Bukayo Saka’s added-time penalty – to stay perfect this season.

“I’m here to try to give my opinion, defend my club and give the very best to our players,” said Arteta. “I will make mistakes sometimes but I will try to be as fair as possible.

“It’s not about [a potential] apology; it’s just agreeing whether the decision should have been different or not. Maybe [refereeing leaders] have a different opinion. Let’s try to improve and move forward together.”

Brighton vs Arsenal: Arteta ‘respect’ for Hurzeler

Arteta said his conflict with Brighton & Hove Albion counterpart Fabian Hurzeler last season is “all done” and “all in the past”.

Arsenal visit the Seagulls on Saturday for the first time since their controversial win at the Amex Stadium in March, when Bukayo Saka’s ninth-minute strike proved the only goal and Hurzeler questioned their tactics afterwards.

“I have huge respect for Fabian, what he’s done and what Brighton have done as a club,” said Arteta. “It’s just remarkable. [This] is going to be a beautiful game to watch, I’m sure.”

After four league games, Arsenal are level on points with Manchester City at the top of the table. Brighton have seven points after winning 5-0 at Coventry City last Sunday, as well as recovering from 2-0 behind to beat Manchester United at Old Trafford in the EFL Cup on Wednesday.

Mikel Arteta: What did Hurzeler say?

“If they win… no-one will ask how they win,” said Hurzeler, discussing Arsenal’s approach to slowing down play. “They deserve to win it.

“But in the end, we have to make limits – or the Premier League has to make the limits. Where will this go in the future? That’s my question.

“In one game you play 60 minutes, and then when you play against Arsenal [it’s] only 50 minutes… is this what the supporters are paying for? Do you get my point?

“Everyone here in the room, did you really enjoy this football game? I’m sure maybe one raises his arm because he’s a big Arsenal fan, but besides that, no chance.

“[Referees] just try to do their job the best they can do, but they have to stick to some things and I think the Premier League definitely have to help them more.

“At the moment, I have the feeling Arsenal are [using] their own rules, no matter how they are playing. That’s why I think it’s difficult to judge.

“I will never be that kind of manager who tries to win in that way… every team will manage and waste time, but there has to be a limit and the limit has to be set by the Premier League [and] referees. At the moment, they just can do what they want.

“I ask one question: [have] you [ever seen], in a Premier League game, a goalkeeper going down three times? No? So I think we shouldn’t waste too many words about [Raya doing that] tonight.

“We should focus on us, we should focus on our performance. We can’t control these kinds of things. The Premier League has to find the rules and it’s not my business.”

Mikel Arteta: Arsenal boss’s response

When he was asked about Arteta’s remarks at the time, Arteta sarcastically called them a “surprise”. “You go back to [our] previous games and you’ll find a lot of comments like this, always,” he added.

“I think they [critics] love our players. I mean, every time they talk about our players, I think they are the most loved ones in the country.

“[Do I] care? Yeah. Depends. On the comments. And the purpose of that.”

Hurzeler praised Arsenal on Friday. “Last season was last season,” he said. “Opinions are very important and I will definitely always share mine if I get asked.

“I congratulate Arsenal for being deserved champions. They’ve started very impressively and are maybe the best team in England, with their squad.

“It’s our challenge to welcome them in our stadium with a special atmosphere.”

articles.title: Rio Ngumoha: Why the Liverpool forward will ‘save club £130 million’… and has a ‘really big chance’ this season
articles.summary: The versatile forward was at Chelsea for eight years
articles.content:
Rio Ngumoha: Why the Liverpool forward will ‘save club £130 million’… and has a ‘really big chance’ this season

The versatile forward was at Chelsea for eight years

Last Update:

By the time Rio Ngumoha struck with a solo effort in Liverpool’s 3-1 win at Yokohama during pre-season, the 16-year-old’s dazzling runs and productive delivery had made a goal seem inevitable.

England Under-17 youth international Ngumoha had also shone four days earlier against Milan in Singapore, including an assist for Dominik Szoboszlai’s equaliser in the 4-2 defeat.

Reds manager Arne Slot has been cautious in his praise of Ngumoha and warned him about his occasional pass selection, but others have been more effusive in their predictions.

Here’s what winger Ngumoha has had to say about his latest spell in the first team and why team-mate Harvey Elliott and two ex-Liverpool regulars believe he has a huge future.

Best NFL Betting Promos | NFL Preseason GW1 Bonus Bets

Rio Ngumoha: Liverpool’s Lamine Yamal?

Former Chelesa prospect Ngumoha joined Liverpool’s academy in September 2024, scoring two goals in eight assists in the Premier League 2 last season and making six Uefa Youth League appearances.

Jason McAteer, who made 139 appearances for Liverpool between 1995 and 1999, believes Ngumoha could solve a future transfer headache.

“When you look at the way the transfer windows are going for this type of player, we spent [up to] £116m on [Florian] Wirtz,” former right-back McAteer told LFC TV.

“As the seasons go on, that’s only going to increase and you’ll be looking at 120, 130, 140. In two or three seasons’ time, when he’s 19, and probably before that, when he’s ready to go in as a first-team regular, that’s going to save them 130 million.

pic.twitter.com/qBo70eOAkd

“It can be daunting when you move into a first-team environment, but he’s flourishing. I’m not putting him up there with [Barcelona’s Lamine] Yamal – certainly not – but if you’re good enough, you’re old enough.

“It’s vitally important that Liverpool are producing academy talent season after season. The pathway for the academy talent is there if they’re given the opportunity. He’s a very, very special boy.”

Harvey Elliott: Ngumoha ‘incredible’

Harvey Elliott, who knows about expectations during a Liverpool career that began with the winger starting an EFL Cup match as a 16-year-old in 2019, called Ngumoha “fearless”.

“He showed that against AC Milan, one of Europe’s big teams,” said Elliott. “He looked like a kid in a park, although he is a kid. He just needs to carry on like this.

“We’re trying as much as we can to help him out. If he keeps on performing the way he is and working hard, the kid’s got an amazing future.

“I’m really excited to see where things go. Myself and the younger lads are closer to him in age. There aren’t many 16 or 17-year-olds in the team. He’s in because he’s incredible at his age and able to handle to himself.”

“It’s important the younger lads are around him and look after him, which is what we’ve been doing. Not leave him out – bring him into the squad and make him feel really part of it.”

Ngumoha: Andy Robertson an inspiration

Ngumoha, who started Liverpool’s 4-0 home win over Accrington Stanley in the FA Cup on January 11, called his display against Yokahama “a very big night” and “just the first of many.”

“I’ll keep on working hard and show the manager what I can do,” he vowed, crediting Andy Robertson with “really helping me a lot”.

“He’s so experienced and one of the best left-backs in the world. I feel like having him behind me, you can’t really ask for anything more.

“He teaches me a lot. [For the goal] I think they lost the ball and then Robbo passed it to me. In my mind, I was thinking ‘can I score?’, because I had a chance last time.

“My brother is the biggest person in my life – him and my mum – and he’s definitely buzzing. I’m not trying to rush because I’m still only young.

“At the same time, I want to show the manager what I can do and not get too complacent, because I want bigger and better things for me and the club.”

Staying sharp ⚡️ Quick feet from Rio ✨ pic.twitter.com/fPeEs8kJrf

Rio Ngumoha loan move: ‘You can get lost’

Neil Mellor was prolific for Liverpool at youth level but did not establish himself as a first-choice striker during his time at the club between 1999 and 2006.

“Decisions have to be made with these young players, whether it’s training with the under-21s or the first team,” said Mellor.

“Where’s his game time going to be? It’s not going to be in the reserves, like it was for us. Does he get enough in the under-21 or under-19 games?”

Mellor feels Ngumoha should not go out on loan. “I’m a big believer that somebody who’s as talented as that needs to learn the standards for what’s expected at Liverpool Football Club,” he explained.

“To train every day with the best players in the world would be massive for his development. If he went on loan to someone like, I don’t know, West Brom in the Championship or Southampton, you can get lost or go backwards a little bit. It doesn’t suit everybody.

“I think he’s in the right place and right environment, with where this football club is at, to be in a position to say ‘I might be needed, in a year or two years, to play in the first team’.”

Conor’s touch 🪄Rio’s finish 😮‍💨 pic.twitter.com/Wc4nyI1m4l

Wirtz and Salah make team-mates ‘better’

Ngumoha was a month younger than Elliott when he featured against Accrington, although he is second to Jerome Sinclair – who was 16 years and six days of age against West Brom in the EFL Cup in 2012 – as the club’s youngest ever player.

“There are some 16-year-olds coming through who do well and are adaptable to their surroundings,” suggested McAteer.

“He’s one of them, I think. It’s a hard one because he’s a very, very talented player, but he’s 16. When I speak about ‘if you’re good enough, you’re old enough’ – that’s in a football maturity world.

“In life, there’s an immaturity about him because he’s 16. That’s not being critical. There’s a lot to learn – we’ve all been 16.”

McAteer also believes Ngumoha should stay put. “He needs protecting, in that sense, in staying at the club rather than going on loan,” he said.

“If he was 19… I’d put him out on loan at Blackburn or somewhere like that. Liverpool will be thinking whether he’s old enough to go out on loan or be kept hold of and develop.

“With the likes of Wirtz and [Mohamed] Salah, he’s only going to get better and mature quicker this season where he is.”

An incredible team move for the first 👏Rio Ngumoha with a brace for #LFCU21s against Aston Villa ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/sV8uH0pXNC

Will Ngumoha play in the Premier League this season?

Elliott is backing Ngumoha to continue breaking through in 2025/26. “He’s going to have a massive shot this season,” said the Under-21 Euro winner.

“We can all see his quality and I think he has a really, really big chance. In the upcoming years, hopefully he can show the world and everyone at Liverpool why he’s so highly rated.”

articles.title: Isak claims move from Newcastle to Liverpool was no-brainer
articles.summary: Alexander Isak has opened up on his move to Liverpool from Newcastle.
articles.content:
Isak claims move from Newcastle to Liverpool was no-brainer

Alexander Isak has opened up on his move to Liverpool from Newcastle.

Last Update:

Alexander Isak says joining Liverpool from Newcastle last summer was an “easy decision” despite the difficult circumstances surrounding his transfer.

The Sweden striker completed a British-record £125m move to Anfield on deadline day in September 2025 after missing pre-season.

Isak had previously claimed promises made to him at Newcastle had been “broken”, but he insists he never regretted his decision to leave the club.

“Liverpool is a massive club, and everything about the club made it pretty clear,” Isak told BBC Sport.

“And the club’s ambition and the club’s will to get me in as well. It was a big part of it.”

The 26-year-old struggled for goals during his first season at Liverpool and suffered a leg break that kept him out from December until April.

Asked whether he ever regretted the move during that period, Isak said: “No, never. I would never think like that.”

Isak looking forward after injury

Isak made only 22 appearances for Liverpool last season, playing 1,032 minutes in total, but has already matched his previous Premier League tally of three goals after just four matches this season.

He says the experience of dealing with his long-term injury has helped him focus on the future rather than dwelling on what happened.

“[The leg break] was tough. Anyone who had a long injury would know,” Isak said.

“But on the other hand, when you’re in a good place and when you feel good, you don’t really tend to look back because it doesn’t really benefit you.

“So I’m just looking forward and feel really optimistic and excited about the season, and what it can bring to us.”

World Cup gave Isak timely boost

Isak scored once and provided three assists as Sweden reached the last 32 of the World Cup before being eliminated by France.

The tournament also gave him the chance to build his fitness and regain his rhythm after a frustrating campaign at club level.

“Playing for your country in a World Cup is a dream of most people,” Isak said.

“With the injuries last season, the World Cup was perfect. I had that period where I could play and gain rhythm and form.

“And, on top of that, it was a massive experience, so that was perfect to do and come back here for pre-season and to start the season.”

articles.title: Samba says Man City debut was ‘mind blowing’
articles.summary: 17-year-old is star of the show in big win for the holders
articles.content:
Samba says Man City debut was ‘mind blowing’

17-year-old is star of the show in big win for the holders

Last Update:

Manchester City youngster Floyd Samba described his senior debut as “mind-blowing” after netting a brace in the 5–0 EFL Cup third-round demolition of Norwich City at the Etihad Stadium.

The 17-year-old forward – son of former Blackburn Rovers and QPR defender Chris Samba – took centre stage as Enzo Maresca’s heavily rotated side easily swept aside Championship opposition to set up a fourth-round tie against Brighton & Hove Albion.

Samba set the holders on their way early on, rising to guide home a clever header following fine work down the right flank by fellow full debutant Allan. Rayan Cherki quickly doubled City’s advantage just three minutes later, latching onto a pinpoint Ayyoub Bouaddi pass to break Norwich’s high defensive line.

Allan made it 3–0 shortly after the interval with a sharp solo strike, cutting inside from the left before angling a finish across goal. Samba then capped his dream evening with City’s fourth before the hour mark, curling an exquisite effort into the net from a similar angle with his proud father watching on from the stands. Fellow academy talent Ryan McAidoo added a fifth in the final minute to complete the rout.

Speaking after the game, Samba reflected on learning he was in line for minutes against the Canaries.

He said: “Right before the game yesterday, the day before – I knew there would be an opportunity to get some minutes for the first time with the first team. To get a debut like that is mind blowing. I couldn’t believe it myself – but that’s just the beginning, I’ve got a big career ahead of me. It was a great debut.”

The teenager, who has been part of City’s academy since Under-9 level, also admitted the step up from youth football to senior level was a major test physically and tactically.

He said: “I couldn’t be happier right now, being my first senior debut, you have to expect everything to go well, the intensity, the level of players, everything goes up and you have to be able to match it and cope with it, and I think I did well with that.”

articles.title: Jaissle: Newcastle to use mounting injury worries as ‘opportunity’
articles.summary: Matthias Jaissle sees opportunity for members of squad amid Newcastle's injury woes, and remains fully committed to their youth movement.
articles.content:
Jaissle: Newcastle to use mounting injury worries as ‘opportunity’

Matthias Jaissle sees opportunity for members of squad amid Newcastle's injury woes, and remains fully committed to their youth movement.

Last Update:

Matthias Jaissle is keeping a positive mindset amid Newcastle United‘s mounting injury worries, with the Magpies boss viewing the long list of absentees as an “opportunity” for other members of his squad.

Newcastle suffered their first defeat under Jaissle on Monday as they were emphatically beaten 4-1 by Leeds United at Elland Road.

Winger Anthony Elanga missed the game due a hamstring injury sustained in training, while Jacob Ramsey suffered a thigh injury in the warm-up. Newcastle were hit with another injury during the game, as midfielder Nico Gonzalez was forced off with a concussion.

The severity of Elanga’s injury is still not confirmed, though he is reportedly set to spend at least six weeks on the sideline.

As such, the upcoming extended international break comes at a good time for Newcastle, but they will be without that trio, as well as right-back Amar Dedic, for the visit of unbeaten Hull City on Saturday, which will be the Magpies’ last before a break that for them will stretch to the October 12 trip to Coventry City.

Captain Dan Burn, midfielder Joelinton and forward Will Osula are also all unavailable, leaving Jaissle with a thin squad as Newcastle aim to get back to winning ways.

But the German sees a positive in the injury issues impacting his team.

He told a pre-match press conference: “It is really important to show the right reaction after the Leeds United match. We are fully aligned and fully committed to showing a reaction in front of our fans.

“It would be nice to finish this block of fixtures before the international break with a good result.”

“[We have] no new players coming back for the Hull game. We have some injured players missing, but we use that as an opportunity for others.

“Anthony and Amar will not be able to play on Saturday. JJ [Ramsey] is injured. Hopefully after the international break our injury list is shorter.”

On Elanga, who scored in each of Newcastle’s opening two matches, Jaissle added: “No real update on Anthony. I’ve spoken with him now, he is heading for an MRI scan. We will get more clarity after that, and hope it’s not too serious.

“It is sad after the great start he had. He is a key strength in our squad and we want to stay positive.”

Jaissle retains belief in Newcastle youth movement

The injuries in midfield will leave Jaissle to select between 20-year-old Lewis Miley, 18-year-old Sean Steur and 20-year-old Aladji Bamba in the engine room.

But Jaissle is undaunted by that prospect and remains committed to the approach of sticking by young players despite their struggles against Leeds.

“It will be a young midfield. We trust them. This is our approach,” Jaissle said.

“I said that, four, five weeks ago, it’s a brave journey the club is going [on]. I’m fully committed in that, so now if there’s one setback we shouldn’t delete our journey or our mission.

“We’re fully committed, we’re fully aligned. We anticipated that something like that against Leeds happened, or is happening also in the next weeks and months. It’s just on us to respond, but still believing, we don’t change that.”

articles.title: Klopp wants Germany to reclaim national pride after far-right election result
articles.summary: Jurgen Klopp has called for a rally to restore Germany's national pride.
articles.content:
Klopp wants Germany to reclaim national pride after far-right election result

Jurgen Klopp has called for a rally to restore Germany's national pride.

Last Update:

New Germany coach Jurgen Klopp says his team can help ensure that “national pride is not entrusted to the wrong people” following a recent far-right election victory.

The Alternative for Germany (AfD) party won 43.8% of the vote in Saxony-Anhalt, narrowly missing out on an absolute majority in the eastern state’s regional parliament.

The anti-immigration party is also expecting strong results in elections in Berlin and Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania on Sunday.

Speaking after announcing his first Germany squad, Klopp stressed that he was not a political “expert”, but said football could help change how national identity is viewed.

“We had an election where some people may have thought it was OK, while others were saying, ‘my God, what is happening here?'” Klopp said.

“From my perspective as a sportsman, I can say that I would very much like to reclaim the flag for myself, for all of us.

“I want it so that when someone waves it, no one thinks: ‘What is wrong with you?’ Instead, I want people to understand: You are happy and realise how lucky you were to be born, grow up, or move to this wonderful country.”

Germany coach wants football to unite people

No far-right party has controlled a German state since the Second World War, when the ruling Nazi party carried out the Holocaust.

“I do not want to entrust national pride to the wrong people,” Klopp added.

“I can be proud to be German while also being open-minded and diverse, and kind and friendly.

“Football can foster a sense of community, so that people can truly feel the power of sport,” he said.

Klopp names 44-man Germany squad

Klopp selected 16 uncapped players in a 44-man squad for four Nations League matches across a two-week period.

A group of 24 players will face the Netherlands in Amsterdam on September 24 before hosting Greece in Augsburg three days later.

Most of those players will then return to their clubs, with the remaining 20 joining the squad for matches against Serbia in Munich on October 1 and Greece in Thessaloniki on October 4.

The first group includes Premier League trio Kai Havertz, Kevin Schade and Anton Stach. Bayern Munich midfielder Jamal Musiala has also been included after twice collapsing during pre-season matches.

Brentford midfielder Vitaly Janelt has received his first international call-up in the second group, which also features Liverpool’s Florian Wirtz and Newcastle defender Malick Thiaw.

Goalkeeper Manuel Neuer and defender Antonio Rudiger retired from international football after Germany’s second-round World Cup exit against Paraguay.

articles.title: Hutchison backs Moyes to deliver at Everton but claims Toffees need to ‘find the next Semenyo’
articles.summary: A Merseyside legend is backing David Moyes to deliver at Everton.
articles.content:
Hutchison backs Moyes to deliver at Everton but claims Toffees need to ‘find the next Semenyo’

A Merseyside legend is backing David Moyes to deliver at Everton.

Last Update:

Don Hutchison has backed David Moyes to take Everton to the next level but insists the club must overhaul their recruitment approach if they are to return to European football.

Hutchison dismissed the scepticism surrounding Moyes among sections of the Everton fanbase, pointing to the manager’s record at West Ham as evidence that he is more than capable of delivering success in the right environment.

“I think he can get them to the next level. I know some Evertonians are a little doom-and-gloom about Moyes, but I do not understand it,” he said, speaking to betTOM.

“Look at the job he did at West Ham. He took them into Europe for three consecutive seasons and won the Europa Conference League. Everton have the right manager, but they need investment.

“They either have to sign £60 million or £75 million players, or recruit more intelligently. Clubs such as Bournemouth, Brentford and Brighton have shown that you do not always need to buy famous names.

“You need a strong scouting network to find the next Justin Kluivert, Antoine Semenyo or players who can outperform their price tag. If Everton want to get back into Europe, that is the route: keep Moyes and improve the recruitment.”

‘They are playing with an elite player’

Hutchinson believes Jack Grealish’s presence will be a huge factor in the club’s success this season, after the Manchester City man rejoined the Toffees on loan for another year.

“I think he will be great. I don’t think the club needed to persuade him to join – he actively wanted to be there.

“He has a great football brain. He can slow games down, bring other players into play and control the tempo. You can see why Pep Guardiola valued him.

“It is now up to David Moyes to get the best out of him, but the other Everton players need to use their football intelligence too.

“They are playing with an elite player, and they need to make runs and read the game at the same level as him.”

articles.title: ‘We move on together’ – Alonso happy to have clarity after Chelsea ownership change
articles.summary: Xabi Alonso welcomed the clarity in Chelsea's ownership situation, and re-stated the ambition to return to challenging for major honours.
articles.content:
‘We move on together’ – Alonso happy to have clarity after Chelsea ownership change

Xabi Alonso welcomed the clarity in Chelsea's ownership situation, and re-stated the ambition to return to challenging for major honours.

Last Update:

Xabi Alonso is pleased to have clarity around Chelsea‘s ownership structure after Todd Boehly and fellow co-owner Mark Walter sold their stakes, allowing Clearlake Capital to take full control.

Clearlake previously held a 61.5% stake in Chelsea, with Boehly and Walter each owning 12.83%. Swiss philanthropist Hansjorg Wyss, who also held a 12.83% share, will remain part of the ownership group.

The BlueCo consortium, fronted by Boehly, completed its purchase of Chelsea in 2022 for £2.5 billion, with a further £1.75 billion committed to investment in the club following the sanctions placed on former owner Roman Abramovich.

The Financial Times reported that Boehly and Walter will receive £950 million for their combined stake, with the deal valuing Chelsea at £5 billion including debt.

With Boehly stepping down as chairman following the sale, Behdad Eghbali is set to be the man in sole charge at Stamford Bridge.

And that is a situation that suits Alonso, who was persuaded to take over as head coach by Eghbali.

“I think it is an important day for the club when there is an important change in the structure of the club, new ownership,” Alonso told a press conference ahead of Chelsea’s Premier League clash with Brentford.

“Thanks to the former owners for what they have done. I was not here but I know that they played an important role. And now that Behdad is taking more control, or almost full control, I think it is good that the main one is clear.

“I have a very good relationship with Behdad; he was the one who came to Madrid to explain the project to convince me and we are working well together. As I have mentioned, this is phase one we have completed in project of the squad. It is good and now we move on together.”

Chelsea have stuttered in their last two league matches, losing at Arsenal and drawing with Hull City, with those results dampening talk they could challenge for the title in Alonso’s first season.

But Alonso is confident his side can contend for major honours.

“That is why we are here,” he added. “To work to get into that position, knowing that the competition that we have but for sure the ambition of the club, the potential of the club, the dimensions of the players, of where we are.

“We know where we want to be. We know everything takes time but the ambition for that is very clear.”

articles.title: Barca president calls for 2030 World Cup final to be held at Camp Nou
articles.summary: The Blaugrana chief is set to put the idea to FIFA.
articles.content:
Barca president calls for 2030 World Cup final to be held at Camp Nou

The Blaugrana chief is set to put the idea to FIFA.

Last Update:

Barcelona president Joan Laporta wants the 2030 World Cup final to be held at Camp Nou rather than in Madrid or Casablanca.

The 2030 tournament will be hosted in Spain, Portugal and Morocco, with games to mark the centenary of the tournament to be staged in Argentina, Paraguay and Uruguay.

But the venue for the final has still to be confirmed, with Spain and Morocco in dispute about where it should be staged.

Both countries have claimed they will host the final, with Real Madrid’s Santiago Bernabeu likely the frontrunner for Spain, while the 115,000-seater Grand Hassan II is being built east of Casablanca. It will become the largest football stadium in the world.

However, Laporta believes Camp Nou, which is still being redeveloped, is a better option.

When work is completed, Barcelona’s iconic stadium will hold 105,000 fans, with Laporta viewing it as the ideal venue for the final.

“The World Cup final shouldn’t be in Casablanca nor Madrid, it should be at the Spotify Camp Nou,” Laporta told Cadena SER.

“I say this for a reason: 105,000 fans.

“I think that FIFA will take this into account. And besides, we already had a World Cup final at the Santiago Bernabeu in 1982.

“With all respect to Morocco, the 2030 World Cup final should be played in the Spanish state. Besides, Spain are the world champions.”

Laporta added that he will put the idea to world football’s governing body, FIFA.

“The 2030 World Cup final in the Spotify Camp Nou would mean the international recognition that we want, and we will propose it,” he explained.

“We will argue these reasons and others that we are sure will occur to us.”

articles.title: Hutchison issues Wirtz ultimatum after claims he ‘never really considered Liverpool title contenders’
articles.summary: Former Liverpool man Don Hutchinson has had his say on Florian Wirtz's future at the club.
articles.content:
Hutchison issues Wirtz ultimatum after claims he ‘never really considered Liverpool title contenders’

Former Liverpool man Don Hutchinson has had his say on Florian Wirtz's future at the club.

Last Update:

Former Liverpool midfielder Don Hutchison has warned the club to resolve the Florian Wirtz situation by January, insisting the German international has already had more than enough time to settle and must start producing at the level his ability demands.

Hutchison, speaking on behalf of betTOM, was full of praise about Andoni Iraola’s start at Anfield, but suggested the midfield could be a problem area deeper into the season.

The 55-year-old’s criticism centred on their £116.5million signing, who he believes has not done enough to prove his worth at Anfield so far.

“He can only really play as a No.10, but that creates an issue because it moves Dominik Szoboszlai away from his best position,” Hutchison said.

“Liverpool could eventually bring in a proper No.6 and play two holding midfielders, allowing Szoboszlai to be the No.10. Then Wirtz has to prove he deserves to stay in the side.

“I would wait until January. By then, he will have had around 18 months at the club, which is ample time. I do not believe it should take a player with a good football brain more than a few weeks to settle, never mind a year and a half.

“When you watch old clips of Philippe Coutinho at Liverpool, you see the level Wirtz should be reaching.”

Arsenal to pull away in title race

Hutchinson is not convinced Liverpool can compete for the Premier League crown they won in 2025. Instead, he is expecting Arsenal to pull away further down the line.

“I never really considered Liverpool title contenders this season because Arsenal were so good last year, and Manchester City have had a very strong transfer window,” he said.

“Arsenal look the best side by far. They are strong all over the pitch, rarely allow opponents a shot, do not concede many goals and score freely. David Raya, Gabriel and Declan Rice are perhaps their three most important players, but Arsenal have quality replacements across the team. I can see Arsenal pulling away, although City’s summer business has narrowed the gap.”

For Liverpool, Hutchison pointed to the Champions League as the more meaningful measure of progress this term.

“A trophy, a top-four or top-five finish, Champions League qualification and a competitive European run would represent a good season.

“They need to show they can beat teams such as Atletico Madrid and perhaps Real Madrid, but if they go out to PSG or another elite side, it would not be a disaster.”

articles.title: Beckham backs Messi over Kane for Ballon d’Or after inspiring Inter Miami to Campeones Cup
articles.summary: Inter Miami owner David Beckham is backing Lionel Messi to win the Ballon d'Or over Harry Kane.
articles.content:
Beckham backs Messi over Kane for Ballon d’Or after inspiring Inter Miami to Campeones Cup

Inter Miami owner David Beckham is backing Lionel Messi to win the Ballon d'Or over Harry Kane.

Last Update:

Inter Miami co-owner David Beckham believes Lionel Messi should win his ninth Ballon d’Or after another outstanding year for club and country.

Harry Kane is reportedly the bookmakers’ favourite for the award after scoring 73 goals in 61 appearances for Bayern Munich and England last season.

However, Beckham has backed his fellow Inter Miami figurehead Messi, pointing to the Argentina captain’s performances at this summer’s World Cup.

Messi scored eight goals during the tournament and also helped Inter Miami win their first MLS Cup last year. He then played a key role as Miami won their first Campeones Cup on Wednesday night.

‘He should win it’

Speaking to Apple TV, Beckham said Messi’s form at the World Cup showed why he should be considered the leading candidate.

“I think when you see him do things like this tonight, when you see him have the World Cup that he’s had, it’s not luck that he’s being considered for the Ballon d’Or again,” Beckham said.

“It’s not luck because he was probably the best player in the tournament. He had an incredible year last year.

“He came into that tournament in the World Cup, and like you’ve just said, 39 years old, to affect a World Cup and every game the way he did. That’s special. There’s no one at 39 that’s doing that and doing it at that level. So he deserves to be considered for the Ballon d’Or. He, in my opinion, he should win it.

“You’ve got great players there like Harry Kane, like Kylian Mbappe, like Jude Bellingham and other players there, but you know when you’re talking about Leo, I’m his biggest supporter,” he added.

Messi makes history for Miami

Messi opened the scoring in Wednesday’s Campeones Cup clash at Miami’s Nu Stadium, heading in a Luis Suarez cross in the 24th minute.

The 39-year-old thought he had doubled his advantage after racing clear and slotting the ball into the net, but the effort was ruled out for offside.

Messi still had another major contribution to make, delivering the corner from which former Real Madrid and Manchester United midfielder Casemiro headed home in the 81st minute.

The 2-0 win secured Miami their first Campeones Cup, with Messi having also scored his 100th goal for the club in the match.

Messi has previously won the award eight times, in 2009, 2011, 2012, 2013, 2016, 2019, 2021 and 2023.

articles.content:
Chelsea ownership changes as Clearlake Capital takes full control

Todd Boehly has departed Chelsea after selling his shares in the club.

Last Update:

Todd Boehly and fellow co-owner Mark Walter have sold their stakes in Chelsea, handing full control of the Premier League club to private equity firm Clearlake Capital.

Clearlake previously held a 61.5% share in Chelsea, with Boehly and Walter each owning 12.83%. Swiss philanthropist Hansjorg Wyss, who also held a 12.83% stake, will remain part of the ownership group.

The consortium completed its purchase of Chelsea in 2022 for £2.5 billion, with a further £1.75 billion committed to investment in the club following the sanctions placed on former owner Roman Abramovich.

The Financial Times reported that Boehly and Walter will receive £950 million for their combined stake, with the deal valuing Chelsea at £5 billion including debt.

Boehly steps down as chairman

As part of the ownership changes, Boehly will relinquish his position as Chelsea chairman.

The club praised his “unwavering commitment” to the ownership group’s belief that supporters should remain at the heart of Chelsea.

“It has been an honour to serve as Chairman of Chelsea Football Club,” Boehly said in a club statement.

“I would like to thank the many who helped secure a bright future for the Club, including the English Premier League, the coaches and players, the talented leadership and staff at Chelsea, and the legions of dedicated fans.

“I have valued my partnership with Clearlake and the wider ownership group, and the collective decisions and investment we have made to support the immediate and long-term success of the Club. I am confident that Chelsea is well positioned for continued success under Clearlake’s leadership.”

Chelsea insist there will be no major changes

Walter recently completed the sale of the Los Angeles Lakers to a group led by venture capitalist Joshua Kushner and former Disney chief executive Bob Iger, in a deal that valued the NBA franchise at $12.5 billion.

He remains the owner of the Los Angeles Dodgers and is also under federal investigation relating to insurance companies he owns.

Chelsea appointed Xabi Alonso as manager during the summer and currently sit sixth in the Premier League.

articles.title: ‘That’s on me’ – Carrick pulls no punches after Man Utd’s EFL Cup collapse
articles.summary: United were beaten despite being 2-0 up at home
articles.content:
‘That’s on me’ – Carrick pulls no punches after Man Utd’s EFL Cup collapse

United were beaten despite being 2-0 up at home

Last Update:

Michael Carrick shouldered full responsibility after Manchester United surrendered a commanding two-goal advantage to crash out of the EFL Cup in a stunning 3-2 defeat to Brighton at Old Trafford.

Fresh from the bitter disappointment of their weekend derby defeat to Manchester City, United looked poised for a cruise into the fourth round after an explosive opening.

Nineteen-year-old winger Shea Lacey illuminated the contest, cutting inside onto his left foot to lash home a fine opener at Jason Steele’s near post. Just 46 seconds later, Mason Mount bundled home a rebound to double the advantage with his first goal of 2026.

However, Charalampos Kostoulas poked past Karl Darlow in first-half stoppage time to hand the Seagulls a lifeline, before quick-fire strikes from Pascal Gross and substitute Maxim De Cuyper turned the tie on its head. The defeat marked the first time United had lost at Old Trafford having led by two goals since November 1976.

Speaking to BBC Radio 5 Live at full-time, Carrick admitted that the early euphoria around Lacey’s breakthrough was quickly eclipsed by the manner in which his rotated side lost control.

“It seems a long time ago now but the start of the game was fantastic,” he said.

“It was everything we hoped for, even more really, in some ways with Shea [Lacey] getting his goal. The night’s gone in a different direction but I think for Shea and everyone who’s been connected with his journey, to have a moment like that was great,

“He should be celebrating and enjoying it a little bit more really. Then we let the game get away from us with the longer the game went.

“We ended up with a pretty disappointing night. It’s obvious for me to say that. We accept that. We can’t be in a position like that and lose the game in that manner.

“I’ll understand the disappointments and frustrations. I accept that. That’s on me. It’ll need to be better than that.”

Questioned on whether he had already addressed the collapse with his squad in the dressing room, Carrick conceded that recent late setbacks are beginning to take a psychological toll.

“We can’t change that. It’s done,” he said.

“We’ve got to keep evolving as a group. We have to keep learning and dealing with situations. Sometimes they come a bit easier than others. Tonight was a tough one.

“We didn’t find a way out of it. That’s up to me and the staff to help the players and guide them through it. I think we all know that in the end tonight feels like a big disappointment.

“We’ve had small, little things that have gone against us in the last week or two and then it accumulates to feel that it’s a lot bigger. I think we have to be honest and say that. The late goal against Everton from outside the box. The [Manchester] City goal the other day. It can all of a sudden roll into something a bit greater but I understand the disappointment because we shouldn’t finish the game in that manner with the position we were in and we have to be humble and take that.”

Carrick demanded an instant response from his players with the domestic calendar offering no respite with a trip to Fulham at the weekend.

“We have to find the answers for Sunday,” he said.

articles.content:
Europa League: Sunderland make winning return to European competition

Enzo Le Fee's penalty proves decisive on historic night for the Black Cats

Last Update:

Sunderland marked their first European game in 53 years with a 1-0 win against AZ Alkmaar in a historic Europa League clash on Wearside.

The Black Cats had not played in Europe since a 2-0 defeat in Lisbon to Sporting in the Cup Winner’s Cup of 1973.

Micky Horswill was the last Sunderland player to score in Europe before Enzo le Fee’s penalty served up a deserved and gutsy win for the side which finished seventh in the Premier League last season.

The key moment came when teh lively Le Fee was hauled down following a devastating counter-attack, and picked himself up and coolly slotted his spot-kick into the bottom corner.

Backed by a deafening home crowd, Regis Le Bris’ side dominated the opening 45 minutes with wasteful finishing prevented a more commanding lead.

Le Fee hit the woodwork with a rasping drive before the interval before Sunderland were forced to weather substantial pressure and appeared to be clinging on into the closing stages before AZ’s intensity finally waned.

The Black Cats missed late opportunities to make the scoreline emphatic.

Elsewhere there were wins for Benfica, Lyon and Bayer Leverkusen, with the competition continuing on Thursday night.

EFL Cup review: Wins for Everton and Aston Villa as United crash out

Fleetwood Town pull off an upset

Last Update:

Everton and Aston Villa powered into round four of the EFL Cup with wins on Wednesday night.

Everton saw off the challenge of recently relegated Wolves at home thanks to a late goal from Charly Alcaraz with Prime Minister Andy Burnham among the crowd.

And Villa needed two goals from Tammy Abraham to see off Coventry and continue their poor start to the season.

Fleetwood Town, of League Two, soldier on after a fine home win over Sheffield United.

Abraham on song

Abraham issued a timely reminder of his quality to boss Unai Emery with a decisive double for Villa.

Having rejected summer loan moves following Nicolas Jackson’s £65m arrival, Abraham opened the scoring after seven minutes. Though Victor Torp briefly levelled with a sublime 25-yard free-kick, Coventry’s defensive frailties resurfaced. Ross Barkley glanced home an unmarked header before the break, and Abraham sealed progression just before the hour mark by turning in John McGinn’s corner, condemning the struggling Sky Blues to a fifth defeat in six matches.

At the Hill Dickinson Stadium, David Moyes’ Everton were repeatedly thwarted by former Toffees goalkeeper Joao Virginia, who brilliantly denied Thierno Barry. However, the breakthrough arrived in the 80th minute when substitute Alcaraz jinked into the box and slotted home his first goal for the club in 13 months.

The shock of the round came at a wet and windy Highbury Stadium, where Fleetwood made club history when Rhys Norrington-Davies inadvertently headed Danny Andrew’s cross into his own net.

articles.summary: Tottenham have been handed another financial boost through their owners.

Tottenham receive further £120m injection from Lewis Family

Tottenham have been handed another financial boost through their owners.

Last Update:

The Lewis family have provided a further £120 million in capital to Tottenham, according to reports.

The latest investment takes the amount supplied to the club by the family to around £320m over the past 12 months. It follows a £100m injection during the summer from the family, who run Spurs’ majority owner ENIC.

The additional funding comes as the Lewis family take on a more prominent role in Tottenham’s decision-making following Daniel Levy’s departure as executive chairman last September.

The summer investment increased the Lewis family’s shareholding in Tottenham to approximately 88%.

Levy was given the opportunity to invest a proportionate amount to prevent his stake from being diluted, but he did not take up the option before the deadline.

As a result, his holding fell from 29.88% to around 27%.

The Lewis family have now committed another substantial sum, although it remains unclear whether Levy will be offered the chance to participate in this latest investment.

If Levy does not take up a further opportunity to invest, his shareholding could be diluted again.

His stake would potentially fall to around 25% following the latest capital injection.

The investment also provides Tottenham head coach Roberto De Zerbi with further financial backing after the club spent heavily during the summer transfer window.

articles.summary: The nature or severity of the injury have yet to be confirmed.
articles.content:
Elanga out of Sweden squad amid concern over Newcastle winger’s injury

The nature or severity of the injury have yet to be confirmed.

Last Update:

Anthony Elanga has been left out of Sweden’s squad for their upcoming UEFA Nations League matches with an injury Newcastle United boss Matthias Jaissle conceded could be long-term.

Winger Elanga missed Newcastle’s first defeat under Jaissle, a 4-1 loss at Leeds United on Monday, having suffered an injury in training.

Jaissle did not confirm the nature or the severity of the problem, indicating it needs further assessment.

“The injury doesn’t look good,” Jaissle said after the loss at Elland Road.

“We need to investigate how serious it is. Elanga is struggling with injury but at the moment it does not look that good. Unfortunately, he is injured. We need to investigate further and in more detail to find out how long he will be out.

“We will miss him and hope he is back to play quickly. It could be [long-term]. We hope not. He will get another MRI next week, and we will see.”

A statement from the Swedish Football Association announcing the squad read in part: “Anthony Elanga has suffered an injury in the past week and will therefore miss the meeting.”

Speaking to reporters about Elanga, Sweden boss Graham Potter said: “My experience is that it’s better if the communication takes place between the medical staff, because otherwise things can easily get lost along the way.”

Asked how long he could be out for, Potter replied: “No, it’s too early to say.”

Elanga had made an impressive start to the season, scoring two goals in three Premier League games.

That followed a strong World Cup for the 24-year-old, who scored twice as Sweden reached the round of 32 before losing to France.

He will miss Newcastle’s final game before the international break as they look to get back to winning ways against surprise package Hull City.

In an expanded international window, Elanga will be out of action for a pair of games with Romania, which come either side of meetings with Poland and Bosnia-Herzegovina, with Sweden drawn into a difficult group in Nations League B as they look to secure promotion to League A.

articles.content:
Al-Taawoun ordered to play two games behind closed doors after Jota chants in Al-Hilal game

The Saudi governing body has handed down a severe punishment.

Last Update:

Al-Taawoun have been ordered to play their next two home Saudi Pro League matches behind closed doors after fans taunted Al-Hilal’s Ruben Neves over the death of Diogo Jota.

The Saudi Arabian Football Federation handed down the punishment while also fining Al-Taawoun  100,000 riyals ($26,660 / £19,796).

Fans of the club were videoed repeatedly chanting Jota’s name in the direction of Neves during Al-Hilal’s 6-0 win over Al-Taawoun last Saturday.

Jota, a former Portugal team-mate of Neves and Al-Nassr star Cristiano Ronaldo, was killed in a car crash in Northern Spain in July 2025. Neves was Jota’s best friend and a pallbearer at his funeral.

In response to the chanting, Ronaldo took to social media to demand action be taken.

He wrote: “The league must take action and punish this kind of fan behaviour. This is no longer football, and there have to be limits. People who behave like this should never be allowed to enter a stadium again.”

Neves showed his disgust during the game, indicating that ‘God is watching’ by pointing at the sky, his eyes and then the fans during the game.

Afterwards, he was asked about the incidents, and said: “I hope they [the fans] don’t go to prayer later.”

articles.content:
Tuchel regrets not ‘eating grass’ after England’s World Cup win over Mexico

Thomas Tuchel has opened up on England's win over Mexico at the World Cup.

Last Update:

Thomas Tuchel has revealed he wished he had eaten some of the grass after England’s 3-2 World Cup win over Mexico.

England defeated the host nation with 10 men in Mexico City in a last-16 tie last summer, producing one of the finest overseas performances in the country’s history.

“I texted a friend after the match and I just wrote, ‘I regret that I didn’t eat some grass after the match to keep something from this in my body forever.’ That was the feeling. That was the moment,” Tuchel said.

England prepare for next challenge

England return to action later this month against world champions Spain in the Nations League.

They will also face Croatia and Czechia during the upcoming international break, with Tuchel expected to announce his squad on Friday.

The England manager believes the Nations League provides an important opportunity to prepare for Euro 2028.

“It’s very difficult to prepare for a World Cup in the US, but I think it’s possible to prepare for a Euros and we prepare in Nations League Tier One,” he said.

“The target is to have another 10 matches. We had 10 matches in the US — eight wins, one draw, one painful loss. That is something to build on.

“We all have the right to hold our heads high and go with courage and positivity into the next challenges. We have four matches in Nations League coming up, and that’s where the focus is.”

articles.content:
Bologna sack Tedesco after four games and appoint Palladino

Palladino will take charge of his first game on Saturday.

Last Update:

Bologna have sacked Dominic Tedesco after just four games in charge and replaced him with Raffaele Palladino.

Tedesco, the former Schalke, Spartak Moscow, RB Leipzig and Belgium boss, was appointed in June following the exit of Vincenzo Italiano, having seen his spell with Fenerbahce come to an end in April.

But Bologna have endured a disappointing winless start to the new season.

They have taken just one point from a possible 12 in Serie A, with last weekend’s 1-0 defeat to Napoli proving Tedesco’s last of a very brief tenure.

Palladino will now look to turn their fortunes following a short spell in charge of Atalanta last term.

He replaced Ivan Juric last November and won 18 of his 39 games in all competitions, drawing nine and losing 12.

His efforts were good enough to see Atalanta finish seventh and qualify for the Conference League, but Palladino was relieved of his duties at the end of the season.

Palladino’s first game in charge comes on Saturday, when Bologna host Torino.

articles.title: Focus on Manchester derby VAR mistake is ‘poor’, says City boss Maresca
articles.summary: Maresca feels more should have been made of his side's performance with 10 men.
articles.content:
Focus on Manchester derby VAR mistake is ‘poor’, says City boss Maresca

Maresca feels more should have been made of his side's performance with 10 men.

Last Update:

Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca is disappointed with the focus on the VAR error that settled last Sunday’s derby in their favour.

City claimed a 1-0 win over rivals Manchester United at Old Trafford thanks to a controversial Erling Haaland winner in the 60th minute, which maintained a perfect start to the new Premier League season for Maresca’s men.

Haaland’s goal was initially ruled out for offside, only for that decision to be overturned following a VAR check.

The Norwegian was being played onside by Patrick Dorgu, with the goal allowed to stand despite Enzo Fernandez attacking Josko Gvardiol’s cross from an offside position prior to Haaland tucking it home a the far post.

Referees body ProRef subsequently acknowledged that an “error of judgement” had been made in not disallowing the goal for Fernandez interfering with play from an offside position.

Maresca: City are still waiting for an apology

The VAR officials who came to the decision, Matt Donohue and Blake Antrobus, have been stood down in the wake of the controversy.

Maresca, though, has been irritated by the continued fallout from the decision, which has overshadowed his side’s efforts in claiming all three points despite being reduced to 10 men in the 23rd minute when Phil Foden was shown red for kicking Bruno Fernandes in the stomach in an off-the-ball incident.

Speaking ahead of Thursday’s EFL Cup tie with Norwich City, Maresca said: “To talk about one moment after that game when we played for 70, 75 minutes with 10 players is quite poor. I think the performance was unbelievable and I’m pleased.

“Tomorrow night, it’s another competition but the ambition is the same. There is no VAR but we don’t plan the game in a different way.”

Referencing a similarly controversial decision in January 2023, when Maresca was an assistant at City for a derby defeat that saw a Fernandes equaliser allowed to stand despite Marcus Rashford being stood in an offside position, the Italian added: “There is knowledge that there was a mistake and that’s all. Sometimes it goes for you sometimes against you.

“Three years ago it when I was here happened the exact same against Manchester United. The goal was not a regular goal and no one apologised. We are still waiting for the apology for that.

“Sometimes it happens for you, sometimes against you. It’s football.

“It’s not easy for the VAR and the people in front of the screen. To make a decision in 10, 20 seconds is not easy for them. Sometimes they make mistakes. I make mistakes, players make mistakes. It’s part of our job.

“It’s also complicated for them.”

Asked about Foden’s dismissal and the three-match suspension his straight red incurs, Maresca told his pre-match press conference: “At half-time he was upset and sad because he knew it was something wrong. After the game he was a bit more relieved and happy.

“Yesterday he was very good. He knows that the reaction was probably not a good one but it is finished and we move on.”

“It’s a big one [blow]. He was doing well with us. He started quite well [before his red card]. Now he is out tomorrow and for Sunderland and Liverpool. Then he is back again.”

articles.title: Arteta hails ‘unbelievable’ Dowman after Arsenal star bags brace in EFL Cup
articles.summary: Mikel Arteta was full of praise for Arsenal youngster Max Dowman after his performance against Ipswich on Tuesday.
articles.content:
Arteta hails ‘unbelievable’ Dowman after Arsenal star bags brace in EFL Cup

Mikel Arteta was full of praise for Arsenal youngster Max Dowman after his performance against Ipswich on Tuesday.

Last Update:

Max Dowman scored twice as Arsenal defeated Ipswich 4-2 in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday night, but Mikel Arteta has warned that the teenager’s development must be managed carefully.

The 16-year-old had made 13 appearances last season but had been restricted to substitute duties during the opening weeks of this campaign.

He made his opportunity count at Portman Road, scoring two impressive goals to strengthen his case for further Premier League involvement.

Dowman’s first was a superb solo effort, as he drove through the Ipswich defence before finishing past the goalkeeper. His second showed his composure, with the youngster placing the ball into the bottom corner.

“Unbelievable, he’s unpredictable, he can go either way, so fluid, so nice to watch,” Arteta said.

Despite Dowman’s performance, Arteta stressed that Arsenal must not allow the excitement surrounding the youngster to dictate his development.

“He is 16 years old and we have to be really cautious,” the Arsenal manager said.

“We don’t want to stop him, we don’t want to put the brakes on him, we need to develop him and we are fully aware what he needs. He will have opportunities.”

Arteta added that Dowman was handling the demands of senior football increasingly well, while emphasising the importance of ensuring he is properly prepared whenever he is selected.

“He’s an unbelievable player because of the character that he has and how much he loves to play at the biggest stage,” he said.

“It’s not easy [to contain the hype], I understand, but what we have to do is look after him. He’s 16 years old. You don’t see that in this league.”

articles.title: Mourinho ‘risked everything’ as Real Madrid leave it late in latest win
articles.summary: Jose Mourinho says he risked everything for Real Madrid to win their latest La Liga outing.
articles.content:
Mourinho ‘risked everything’ as Real Madrid leave it late in latest win

Jose Mourinho says he risked everything for Real Madrid to win their latest La Liga outing.

Last Update:

Jose Mourinho admitted Real Madrid “risked everything” during their 3-2 LaLiga win at Elche, with substitute Carlos Espi scoring a 91st-minute winner.

Madrid looked comfortable after taking a 2-0 lead in the first half. Arda Guler’s free kick was turned into his own net by Elche goalkeeper Matias Dituro before Kylian Mbappe doubled the advantage after being found by Yan Diomande.

However, Elche scored twice late on to level the match and put Madrid’s strong start under serious pressure.

Mourinho responded by sending on forwards Espi and Endrick, leaving Madrid with six attack-minded players on the pitch. T

he move paid off when Jude Bellingham found Mbappe, who crossed for Espi to score the winning goal.

“With the changes at the end, I risked everything,” Mourinho said.

“We won, but we could have lost. We had to do it, because a draw isn’t enough.”

Espi making an impact

Espi has now scored late winners in two matches this season, having also struck away at Espanyol.

The youngster also had an overhead-kick equaliser ruled out at Real Betis, underlining his growing influence despite competing for minutes alongside Mbappe.

“[Espi] is doing well, making an important contribution to the team,” Mourinho said.

“He has a problem in front of him, which is a player who isn’t a normal player [Mbappe], and playing with both together isn’t easy.”

Madrid go level with Barcelona

Mourinho admitted Real Madrid had made life difficult for themselves after failing to finish off Elche when they were in control.

“In games that seem like they’re done, we have three, four, five chances to kill it, and we don’t,” he said.

“We didn’t score, we didn’t finish it with the 3 or 4-0. When it seems easy, you leave things like that, away from home at these stadiums.

“They get a goal and it’s an open game. The good thing is that in difficulty, the team reacts and wins.”

The result moved Madrid level on points with Barcelona at the top of LaLiga, ahead of Barcelona’s match against Racing Santander.

articles.title: EXCLUSIVE: JJ Gabriel to join Real Madrid on his 16th birthday in huge blow to Manchester United
articles.summary: Man United's JJ Gabriel is set to join Real Madrid
articles.content:
EXCLUSIVE: JJ Gabriel to join Real Madrid on his 16th birthday in huge blow to Manchester United

Man United's JJ Gabriel is set to join Real Madrid

Last Update:

JJ Gabriel is to join Real Madrid in October after asking to leave Manchester United, a source has told 101 Great Goals.

The 15-year-old’s request to cancel his contract with immediate effect was reported by the Telegraph on Tuesday.

It is believed Gabriel has made the decision because of an approach from Madrid.

The Premier League club are not obliged to accept the request and have to sanction Gabriel’s departure for the move to proceed.

But United’s hands are somewhat tied because they cannot sign Gabriel on professional terms until he is 17 years of age or make him a scholar until his 16th birthday on October 6.

That has opened the door for Madrid to make their move and exploit a loophole allowing them to sign players aged between 16 and 18 from a fellow European Union country. Gabriel holds an Irish passport, making him eligible.

The shock development will come as a huge blow to United, who saw Gabriel as the crown jewel in their youth set-up.

The supremely gifted forward, who can play across the front three, made his first appearance for United’s Under-18 side aged 14 and went on to score 23 goals last season and become the youngest-ever winner of the club’s Jimmy Murphy young player of the year award.

Gabriel had been expected to make his first-team debut this season and was thought to be in contention to play against Brighton & Hove Albion at Old Trafford in the EFL Cup third round on Wednesday.

With talks with Madrid accelerating over the past week, that is not now a possibility.

Instead, London-born Gabriel, whose full name is Joseph Junior Andreou Gabriel, will move to Spain and further his development at Madrid’s training complex, Valdebebas.

Manchester United fail to follow Arsenal’s lead

It is not known what has prompted Gabriel’s desire to pursue a deal with Madrid but a lack of clarity around his prospects at United could be a reason.

Gabriel has trained with United’s senior squad Under-21 squads this season but was not included in the club’s A list for the Champions League.

Clubs in the competition can call up youth players from a B list at short notice, but Gabriel would not have been eligible for that until he turned 16, meaning he was unable to featuring in the home win against Azerbaijani minnows Sabah on Thursday.

Instead, Gabriel played against Sabah in the UEFA Youth League on the same day, scoring a brilliant hat-trick in a one-sided win.

He deleted all mentions of United on his social media accounts after that game.

United’s treatment of Gabriel is in stark contrast to how Arsenal have looked after Max Dowman.

Dowman was 15 when he played for Arsenal in their 3-0 Champions League win over Slavia Prague last season.

Among his significant contributions as the Gunners won last season’s Premier League, Dowman scored a goal at home to Everton in May to become the Premier League’s youngest-ever scorer at 16 years and 73 days of age.

Giggs hails Gabriel as a ‘generational talent’

Gabriel’s reputation has spiralled after he joined United as an 11-year-old.

Ryan Giggs, who went from precocious teenager to 13-time Premier League winner under Sir Alex Ferguson, spoke about the attacker in glowing terms on Rio Ferdinand’s podcast on Wednesday.

“He’s a generational talent,” said Giggs. “There’s no point in going out on loan because he’s at the best place and he’d be dipping in and out of the first team, so that experience is invaluable.

“[It’s] not only the games and the training, but actually travelling with the team, seeing the expectation of Manchester United… the focus is so huge on United. You need to get used to that.”

When Manchester City tried to lure Gabriel last summer, he opted to remain at United. But the appeal of Madrid has prompted a change of heart.

articles.content:
Iraola hails Szoboszlai after rocket seals Liverpool’s win over Tottenham

Andoni Iraola was full of praise for midfielder Dominik Szoboszlai on Tuesday night.

Last Update:

Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola praised Dominik Szoboszlai after the midfielder scored a spectacular goal in the Reds’ 3-1 Carabao Cup win over Tottenham.

Szoboszlai came off the bench to settle the tie with a long-range effort from around 30 yards. His strike restored Liverpool’s two-goal advantage after Conor Gallagher had pulled one back for Spurs.

Alexis Mac Allister and Cody Gakpo had put Liverpool ahead before Tottenham threatened a comeback, but Szoboszlai’s finish ended any doubt and secured Liverpool’s place in the fourth round.

“The three goals we scored were very good goals,” Iraola said.

“The origin of the first and second goals are also very important for us but the third goal is a worldie, it is outstanding. The thing with Dom is that before shooting, you are trusting he might score.

“With another player you are thinking it’s maybe too far but with Dom everyone is thinking he might score.”

Liverpool’s young players impress

Iraola made 10 changes to the side that drew 0-0 with Fulham at the weekend, with the decision paying off as several younger players delivered energetic performances.

The Liverpool boss explained that the changes were necessary after his team appeared short of energy in their previous match.

“It’s true that I made a lot of changes but I think I needed to do it because we could see the other day that we lacked a bit of energy the other day and we needed fresh legs,” he said.

“I am happy because all the players have given us intensity and aggressiveness.”

Iraola praises commitment

Iraola was particularly pleased with the effort shown by Trey Nyoni, Rio Ngumoha and James McConnell, who all pushed themselves physically before being substituted.

“I was happy for [the young players]. Different positions, different demands. But I think the best thing is they were dead when I subbed them,” he said.

“Trey [Nyoni] was cramping, Rio [Ngumoha] couldn’t have run a lot more. [James] McConnell the same. When this happens, it’s because you’ve given us what you’ve got.

“They have been very athletic, willingness to win their duels, making their presence felt. I was happy for them.”

BREAKING: JJ Gabriel stuns Manchester United by asking for Old Trafford exit

JJ Gabriel has requested his contract at Manchester United is cancelled in another massive blow to the Old Trafford club

Last Update:

JJ Gabriel, the hugely gifted 15-year-old, has asked to leave Manchester United following a breakdown in relations between his family and the club, according to reports.

Gabriel has been dubbed “Kid Messi” after a series of sparkling displays for United’s youth teams and was expected to make his senior debut in Wednesday night’s EFL Cup clash with Brighton at Old Trafford.

But the Enfield-born youngster won’t now be considered after informing the club of his desire to cancel his contract that was due to expire at the end of the season.

United are believed to retain hope that the situation can be rectified and aren’t obliged to accept Gabriel’s request. However, the ball is firmly in the youngster’s court.

Premier League rules state that: “During your child’s registration period, their registration may only be cancelled if everyone agrees (the club, player and their parent/carer).”

The rules add: “If the parties don’t agree, then any person involved can also ask the Premier League to provide a binding decision on a termination request.”

Clubs can’t sign players on a professional contract until they turn 17 years of age or a scholarship until they are 16. Gabriel is not 16 until October 6.

Manchester United fail to follow Arsenal’s lead

It is not known what has prompted the breakdown in the family’s relationship with United but a lack of clarity around his first-team prospects may be one possible reason.

Gabriel has trained with the senior squad and the Under-21s at various points this season but was not included in the club’s A list for the Champions League, denying him the chance to make an appearance in European competition.

Gabriel was therefore ineligible to play against Azerbaijani minnows Sabah last week. Instead he played against the same club in the UEFA Youth League, scoring a brilliant hat-trick in a one-sided win.

He deleted all mentions of United on his social media accounts after that game.

United’s treatment of Gabriel is in stark contrast to how Arsenal have looked after Max Dowman.

Dowman was 15 when he played for Arsenal in their 3-0 Champions League win over Slavia Prague last season. The winger has also played Premier League football and made a difference at various points last season as the Gunners secured the title.

Giggs hails Gabriel as a ‘generational talent’

Gabriel’s reputation has spiralled after he joined United as an 11-year-old.

Ryan Giggs, who also emerged as a first-teamer at Old Trafford as a precocious teenager, spoke about the attacker in glowing terms in a podcast with Rio Ferdinand last week.

Giggs said: “He’s sort of a generational talent. There’s no point in going out on loan because he’s at the best place and he’d be dipping in and out of the first team. So that experience is invaluable. You know, not only the games and the training, but actually travelling with the team, seeing the expectation of Manchester United, you’re seeing all sort of, the focus is so huge on United. You need to get used to that.”

The news he wants out will spark a huge scramble for his signature. Manchester City tried to lure him across town last year and will no doubt he interested, along with Arsenal and a host of European giants.

articles.title: Three things we learned from Hansi Flick’s press conference ahead of Barcelona’s game with Racing Santander
articles.summary: Barcelona boss Hansi Flick spoke on a number of subjects during his press conference to preview Wednesday's La Liga game against Racing Santander. Here are the highlights...
articles.content:
Three things we learned from Hansi Flick’s press conference ahead of Barcelona’s game with Racing Santander

Barcelona boss Hansi Flick spoke on a number of subjects during his press conference to preview Wednesday's La Liga game against Racing Santander. Here are the highlights...

Last Update:

Barcelona boss Hansi Flick held his press conference this afternoon ahead of tomorrow’s clash with Racing Santander.

The German was asked his thoughts on the Ballon d’Or – and Lamine Yamal’s chances of winning the award – as well as Gavi’s current exclusion from the team and the fact the 2029 Champions League will be held at the revamped Camp Nou.

Here, we analyse his responses…

FLICK WARY OF BALLON D’OR DISTRACTION

With the Ballon d’Or due to be awarded next month, the race is on to succeed Ousmane Dembele as the winner of the game’s most prestigious individual award. But Flick admitted his weariness at the current period of campaigning and expressed his eagerness for it to end.

Yamal is among the three leading contenders, along with Real Madrid’s Kylian Mbappe and Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane, to lift the trophy in London. As seen with Mbappe’s clumsy use of words, in which he offended France team-mate Dembele by describing himself as “the chosen one”, the race can divide dressing rooms and distract players from team matters.

Yamal has outlined why he believes he should win it and, while Flick is happy to back the teenage winger, he hinted he felt it was an unnecessary hindrance.

He said: “He’s young. I’ve said it before. He is honest, he has self-confidence and I like him. And for him this is something important. I will support him because it is impressive to have a player like that; and everyone wants to see him in the stadium, and they murmur when he goes one against one, or one against three.

“He has the opinion that he deserves it. I know that there are a huge number of top players and that it is not easy. They [the Ballon d’Or jury] will decide and I will be happy when they finish deciding it.”

FLICK BACKS GAVI TO PLAY A KEY ROLE FOR BARCELONA

Flick was spotted deep in conversation with midfielder Gavi prior to Tuesday morning’s training session.

The Spain international has played just seven minutes since coming off at half-time in the season opener against Elche due to a right knee injury.

Gavi has suffered with terrible injury problems in recent seasons – he played just 13 times last season because of surgery to repair a meniscus in that knee. He also missed more than 300 days after an ACL tear in late 2023, again in the right knee.

The recent arrival of international team-mate Rodri has added more competition in the centre of the field but Flick insisted Gavi remained a key part of his plans.

He said: “Of course, every player is important to us. We need each of them. Gavi is ambitious, he wants to play. He started against Elche, then he was injured but now the team is playing well and he must accept it. You have to manage the minutes. I don’t know what will happen during the season, but we need them all and with a positive mentality.”

FLICK WILL ATTEND 2029 CHAMPIONS LEAGUE FINAL – BUT IN WHAT CAPACITY?

Barcelona’s home stadium – Camp Nou – was this morning awarded the 2029 Champions League final.

Flick, who has a contract with the Catalan club until 2028, was asked if he thought Barca would be playing in the game, and if he would still be in his current role.

He replied: “I will be 100% be at the final in 2029 [if Barca get there] as a coach or as a Barça fan. In football you never know. I’m enjoying it, this club and this team are fantastic, but you never know.”

articles.title: Rodri reveals Mourinho phone call after joining Barcelona
articles.summary: Rodri says he contacted Jose Mourinho after rejecting a move to Real Madrid
articles.content:
Rodri reveals Mourinho phone call after joining Barcelona

Rodri says he contacted Jose Mourinho after rejecting a move to Real Madrid

Last Update:

Barcelona midfielder Rodri has revealed he called Jose Mourinho after deciding to reject Real Madrid and join their Clasico rivals in August.

Spain international Rodri joined Barcelona from Manchester City in a deal worth an initial £65 million after seven years in England.

Madrid were also interested in signing the 30-year-old, who held talks with both Mourinho and Barcelona head coach Hansi Flick before making his decision.

Rodri admitted the choice was difficult, particularly given the way Madrid handled their interest.

“I had to analyse a lot of things and make a big decision between two of the best clubs in the world,” Rodri told Mundo Deportivo.

“In the end, I was guided by sporting aspects, by what excited me a little more and picking where I felt I could win and grow most as a player.

“It wasn’t easy at all. Saying no to Madrid is not easy, above all when their behaviour with me was exemplary. In the end, Deco and Hansi convinced me.”

Rodri thanks Mourinho for interest

Rodri explained that Mourinho made it clear how much he wanted him to move to the Santiago Bernabeu and outlined the role he could play in his team.

The midfielder chose not to disclose the details of their private conversation but confirmed he contacted the Portuguese coach after agreeing to join Barcelona.

“I don’t want to reveal a private conversation, but evidently he expressed his desire for me to go there and explained what he felt I would bring to the team,” Rodri said.

“He was very good with me. When I made the decision, I also called him to thank him for the interest and the way he was with me.

“He is a great coach, he has demonstrated it across many years, and Real Madrid are going to be a tough rival in the league this season.”

articles.summary: Max Dowman has barely featured for Arsenal so far this season
articles.content:
Arteta challenges Dowman to earn minutes after quiet start to new campaign

Max Dowman has barely featured for Arsenal so far this season

Last Update:

Mikel Arteta has promised Arsenal youngster Max Dowman will get minutes this season but warned the 16-year-old must earn his opportunities.

Dowman has been an unused substitute in four matches so far this campaign, including last Wednesday’s 1-0 win at Napoli in the Champions League.

The 16-year-old made history last season by becoming the youngest player to start a Premier League match when he was selected against Crystal Palace.

Arteta was unable to guarantee that Dowman would start Tuesday’s Carabao Cup fourth-round tie at Ipswich, despite Arsenal’s busy schedule.

“Max will have his chance. He will have his minutes and he will have to earn them like anybody else,” Arteta said.

“You know the talent that we have, the players that we have there, we need to help him and find a way to make sure he continues to develop.”

Arsenal targeting another win

Arsenal travel to Ipswich looking to make it five victories from five matches at the start of the new campaign.

The Gunners reached the Carabao Cup final last season but lost to Manchester City at Wembley. Although defending their Premier League title and pursuing a first Champions League triumph are likely to be bigger priorities, Arteta expects his squad to be motivated by the chance to progress.

“It’s the next game ahead and the next competition,” he said.

“We will look at the players eyes, they will say they want to play, they want to win the game, they want to improve and they want to review the [Sunderland] game and they will be willing for me, because I know the boys.”

Saka praises Arsenal’s recent efforts

Arsenal’s latest win came at Sunderland on Saturday, when Bukayo Saka scored late to secure a hard-fought three points.

That result followed a narrow win over Napoli and a close contest against London rivals Chelsea, with Tuesday’s match at Ipswich representing the club’s third consecutive away fixture.

Saka admitted the demanding run had tested the squad but praised the way Arsenal had handled the travel and workload.

“It’s been a massive week for us,” Saka told the official club website.

“There has been a lot of travelling. People don’t understand behind the scenes how it’s been, but I’m really happy with how we’ve managed this.

“It’s amazing for us, so credit to the team, the staff, all of us. We need to keep going – it doesn’t stop.”
