articles.title: Leeds ‘not getting carried away’ after rising to third with Newcastle thrashing
articles.summary: Leeds have won two and drawn two this season
articles.content:
Leeds ‘not getting carried away’ after rising to third with Newcastle thrashing

Leeds have won two and drawn two this season

Last Update:

Jayden Bogle insisted Leeds are “not getting carried away” despite rising to third in the Premier League with a dominant 4-1 win over Newcastle.

Leeds ran riot at Elland Road, with Bogle credited with the second goals after a header by Dominic Calvert-Lewin, who scored a goal of his own for the third, with a Sean Steur own goal and a Noah Okafor completing the scorers.

Daniel Farke’s men remain unbeaten in the top flight this season and are now third in the top flight, while they also handed Newcastle their first defeat of the season.

On Leeds’ ambitions, Bogle told Sky Sports: “At the moment, we’re taking it game by game, we’re not to get to carried away.

“Everyone is ambitious in their own ways but as a group, we’ll stay focused and focus on the next game.”

Leeds continue to impress in 2026

Leeds’ success this season actually stretches back to the start of the year, with few teams bettering their form in 2026.

Only Arsenal (52), Manchester City (50), Manchester United (45) and Bournemouth (37) have won more Premier League points in 2026 than Leeds United (35), with the Whites suffering just a single defeat across their last 13 league games (won six, drawn six).

Bogle added: “It’s about working and having an understanding of the players and playing with them.

“Dom [Calvert-Lewin] is in the middle competing for everything, getting players next to and under him is massive for us. It paid off well tonight.

“We worked on rotation, JJ [James Justin] was going a bit higher and wider sometimes which leaves the pocket open for me to get into.

“Dom [Calvert-Lewin] occupies two centre-backs. It’s about getting into an area where the ball might go. We tried some different patterns and movements we’ve worked on in training to make space.”

“We wanted to start well today, get the fans on board and get them going. We did that to start with, it was about maintaining that and keeping the energy high.

“It was a tough game, a lot of running, it was tough physically. They [Newcastle] are a top side, they can hurt you at any point.”

articles.title: Manchester United legend slams ‘worst VAR decision I have ever seen’ as Red Devils told they have ‘a lot’ to do in pursuit of Arsenal
articles.summary: Manchester United legend Gary Pallister has had his say on the VAR controversy from Sunday's loss to City.
articles.content:
Manchester United legend slams ‘worst VAR decision I have ever seen’ as Red Devils told they have ‘a lot’ to do in pursuit of Arsenal

Manchester United legend Gary Pallister has had his say on the VAR controversy from Sunday's loss to City.

Last Update:

Former Manchester United defender Gary Pallister has delivered a scathing assessment of the VAR decision that allowed Erling Haaland’s goal to stand in Sunday’s Manchester Derby, while also warning that Michael Carrick’s side remain some way off Premier League champions Arsenal’s level.

United suffered a controversial 1-0 defeat to Manchester City at Old Trafford on Sunday, with Haaland’s goal sparking debate over whether Lisandro Martinez had been impeded by an offside Enzo Fernandez in the build-up.

The moment forced an apology from Pro Ref, who admitted a lapse in judgement that allowed City’s goal to stand.

Pallister, speaking to Gambler Media, did not hold back when asked for his assessment of the decision, describing it as the worst VAR call he has ever witnessed.

“There have been some beauties in the past, but I’d probably have to say that is the worst VAR decision I have ever seen,” Pallister said.

“Anyone watching the game with any knowledge of the offside law knows that Lisandro Martinez is impeded in getting to the ball by Enzo Fernandez but then they give the goal anyway. You’re left scratching your head.

“Whoever is in the VAR room responsible for making that decision doesn’t know anything about football. An absolutely incredulous decision.”

Pallister calls for VAR officials to face sanctions

Although critical of the decision at Old Trafford, Pallister stressed that he remains a supporter of VAR and believes the technology has an important role to play in the Premier League.

However, the former United centre-back argued that officials must face consequences when serious mistakes cost team points in high-stakes matches.

“I’ve stood behind VAR for a long time because they do get a lot of decisions right, but with what happened at Old Trafford yesterday, they just can’t be getting that wrong,” he said.

“I don’t know who is behind VAR, but whoever was in the room there yesterday clearly got it wrong, and that is an embarrassment for VAR and the whole process.

“It puts people like Michael Carrick under pressure for losing a derby game, which shouldn’t have happened. I think referees and VAR officials need potential sanctions for making such errors.”

Manchester United have a long way to go to match Arsenal

Despite the setback on Sunday, Pallister believes United’s rebuild will require patience, pointing to Arsenal’s lengthy process of developing a competitive squad under Mikel Arteta.

Asked what needs to improve for United to reach Arsenal’s level, he suggested the difference between the two teams could take years to achieve.

“To get to Arsenal’s level? Oh, wow, I don’t know. I know you’ve got to build that team up over a period of time. Michael’s only at the start of his managerial career at United, so he’s trying to find the right fits for the team that are going to help us improve,” he said.

“Arsenal are, what, four or five years ahead in terms of building a team and getting to where they want to be? So, you know, it could take that long.”

For United, he believes the immediate priority must be to develop a side capable of controlling matches rather than simply relying on individual moments.

“At the moment, I don’t think we can dominate games, and I think we’ve got to find a way to do that,” Pallister said.

“Whether that’s personality, character, the quality of the players, or a team ethic, you’ve got to find all that in your side and give them the confidence that they can go out, dominate games, and win games.

“At the moment, the start of the season has lacked a little bit of that, I would suggest. So we kind of have to bring that to the party, I guess.”

Kobbie Mainoo singled out for praise

Despite the disappointment of the derby defeat, Pallister identified Kobbie Mainoo as United’s standout performer so far this season.

The midfielder impressed during Sunday’s match and came close to scoring with a strike that hit the post, as well as competing with £116million man Elliot Anderson for 90 minutes.

“Kobbie had a real purple patch yesterday in the game. I think he’s a clever player. I don’t know what his best role is still in that midfield area, but he looks after the ball well. He sees a pass, he can score a goal, and he hit the post yesterday with a great strike,” Pallister said.

“It just leaves you scratching your head as to why he was put out in the cold last year by United and never got a sniff at the World Cup, because he’s got some terrific qualities.”

Pallister also praised Bruno Fernandes, who had a quiet game against City but has remained the architect of any impressive Manchester United moments.

“Kobbie and, yeah, probably at the start of this season, Bruno as well, because he’s an eight-out-of-ten player most games,” he said.

“But after that, you’d probably look at Kobbie as the outstanding player so far this season.”

Bruno Fernandes remains United’s key player

Fernandes has already produced a hat-trick against Ipswich this season, but United’s reliance on their captain has raised questions about whether the team can perform when he is not at his best.

Pallister acknowledged that concern while making clear that he considers the Portugal international one of the finest players in world football.

“Yeah, I mean, the only way we got through yesterday was that ball through to Mbeumo, which they probably should have scored from,” he said.

“But, yeah, I think Roy Keane spoke yesterday about what Bruno brings to the team in terms of assists, energy, goals, and quality. Wow, he’s up there with the best in the world for me.

“Where we’d be without him, God only knows, because season after season, he’s proved to be the go-to player. He’s in the form of his life and he plays every game. Whether that carries on into his thirties, we’ll wait and see.

“But he’s been a joy to watch as a footballer, and as an ambassador for Manchester United as well. There was a lot of talk about him leaving for a lot of money last year, and he nailed his colours to the mast and said, ‘No, I’m a United player.'”

articles.title: Alan Shearer goes in two-footed on Bruno Fernandes, labelling Manchester United captain ‘pathetic’
articles.summary: Bruno Fernandes has come in for criticism following Phil Foden's red card in the Manchester derby. Alan Shearer was particularly vocal in his condemnation of the United skipper.
articles.content:
Alan Shearer goes in two-footed on Bruno Fernandes, labelling Manchester United captain ‘pathetic’

Bruno Fernandes has come in for criticism following Phil Foden's red card in the Manchester derby. Alan Shearer was particularly vocal in his condemnation of the United skipper.

Last Update:

Former England captain Alan Shearer has branded Bruno Fernandes “pathetic” following his part in Phil Foden’s red card on Sunday.

Manchester United captain Fernandes was involved in the first-half fracas, initially kicking Foden before falling to the ground theatrically when the Manchester City midfielder reacted by poking both feet into the Portuguese’s midriff.

It was hard to distinguish between the two acts of petulance but only Foden received a red card from referee Michael Oliver.

Shearer told The Rest Is Football podcast: “The way Bruno Fernandes went down was pathetic. He helped get Foden off and, yes, he’s kicked out at him a little bit but Bruno Fernandes has also kicked Phil Foden.

“If Phil Foden reacts in the same way as Bruno Fernandes do they both get red cards? So, for me, either both are red or neither of them are.”

Agbonlahor brands Fernandes a “cheat”

United failed to make the most of their man advantage with Erling Haaland’s controversial winner – a goal Pro Ref later admitted should not have stood – proving decisive.

It was a game short of quality but high on talking points with talkSPORT presenter Gabby Agbonlahor also hitting out at Fernandes.

The former Aston Villa striker said: “At the end of the day, Bruno Fernandes is a cheat. He’s an outstanding player, but he’s a cheat.

“You’ve kicked Foden twice on the floor, which should have been a red card to you. Then Foden’s lashed out a tiny little bit and you’re rolling around when you’re not hurt.

“A proper referee goes over and says: ‘You two, cut it out, a yellow each, play on.’ It’s never a red card.

“That’s why you get your karma. Maybe the goal that should’ve been disallowed on Haaland, is the karma you sometimes get in football for the red card to Phil Foden.”

Keane disappointed by lack of solidarity among players

Speaking as one of Sky Sports’ pundits on Sunday, former United midfielder Roy Keane also felt Fernandes had got contributed to Foden’s dismissal.

The Irishman said: “Bruno goes in, tackles him, clearly fouls him and gives him a little boot on the floor. Foden gets up, does react, and he’s now sent off.

“I’m guessing it’s classed as violent conduct, but to me Bruno’s the one who’s violent here. I have to call it out. I don’t think that’s a red card for Foden, I really don’t.

“The players are all in the PFA [Professional Footballers’ Association], everyone’s in a union – you’ve got to try and look out for each other; you can’t be rolling around.”

articles.title: Arsenal boss Arteta let football down with weekend rant and damaged the game he claims to want to protect
articles.summary: Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta has a duty to speak with more care after another weekend tirade against refereeing standards...
articles.content:
Arsenal boss Arteta let football down with weekend rant and damaged the game he claims to want to protect

Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta has a duty to speak with more care after another weekend tirade against refereeing standards...

Last Update:

It’s becoming a familiar scenario: a decision goes against Arsenal and Mikel Arteta cuts a furious figure in his post-match media commitments.

The Spaniard’s brow is furrowed and he glares at his inquisitor with anger seemingly seeping out of every pore.

It was the same script at the Stadium of Light on Saturday night following Arsenal’s gutsy 2-0 win against Sunderland. Arteta’s team were hugely impressive, staring down the hosts’ blood and thunder approach and a partisan crowd to emerge with a victory that once again reinforced the belief it will take something special for the reigning champions to be dethroned.

They were a long way from their fluent best, in part due to a draining week that included wins at home to Chelsea and at Napoli and in part due to a Sunderland performance that would have overwhelmed most teams in the Premier League.

But they found a way and boarded the flight south having maintained their 100% record.

Arteta ought to have been thrilled but, instead of heaping praise on his players, opted to use his media duties to talk about the penalty awarded to the hosts after referee John Brooks and VAR Stuart Attwell deemed Ezri Konsa had fouled Dan Ballard inside the box.

According to Arteta, the foul ought to have been given the other way round, accusing former Gunner Ballard of performing a “judo roll” on the England international. Enzo Le Fee saw his spot-kick brilliantly saved by David Raya before Bruno Guimaraes and Bukayo Saka netted to sink the Wearsiders.

“Today the game was unprotected and it could have cost us the game and the momentum which is a really, really serious thing,” he fumed.

“It’s not a penalty in any case, in any game, in any context, in any league” 😳Mikel Arteta reflects on Arsenal’s 2-0 win over Sunderland 👀@jules_breach | 📺 Stream with TNT Sports on HBO Max pic.twitter.com/2BUZILexk3

Arteta’s Arsenal not used to seeing decisions go against them

Cry me a river, Mikel.

Does Arteta care about the protection of the game? Of course not.

Was he concerned when Arsenal were found to have been, along with Chelsea, the biggest beneficiaries of refereeing and VAR errors last season, according to the Premier League’s key match incidents (KMI) panel? Of course not.

Was he concerned when his side became the first in Premier League history not to receive a red card or concede a penalty in a single season last term? Of course not.

You could feasibly argue inconsistencies in refereeing are matched by inconsistencies in Arteta’s care for the game.

This was a pre-planned attack by the Arsenal boss, no doubt mindful that at some point a key decision would go against his side, especially given the clampdown on wrestling inside the penalty area, a transgression made into an art form by the North London side in their title-winning season.

Is it just Arteta who could benefit from a lesson in humility and integrity? Absolutely not. Too often managers are using their media interactions as an opportunity to manipulate the narrative, to apply pressure and to alter perceptions.

If it wasn’t so transparent it’d be genius. And yet, turn on any TV channel or radio station over the past two days and your ears would have been subjected to a talking head discussing the merits of Arteta’s argument.

Does that mean Arteta was wrong in his judgement of the penalty call? No, on reflection, he had a valid point. But where does it end? It simply cannot be that every single decision is correct – even with VAR as a fallback. The VAR is still a human being and most decisions require an element of subjectivity.

It cannot be that every perceived human error is met with outrage, whether it is faux or genuine.

Arteta has duty to protect the game, not just Arsenal

Arteta talks about protecting the game. As someone in his lofty position, he has greater leverage to do exactly that and Saturday was the perfect opportunity.

His team played well and won. Why not come out, acknowledge he felt the penalty call was a mistake, but then throw his support behind referees, the VAR, and offer an appreciation of the difficulties of a job that will never, ever produce results that satisfy everyone?

Idealistic? Perhaps.

But, had he done that, Arteta would have enhanced a reputation that is frequently tarnished by his touchline antics and perhaps even swung popular opinion in his, and his team’s, favour.

As it is, he didn’t and it was another bruising weekend for the Premier League and its referees.

Arteta did get one thing right; the game does need protecting. Unfortunately, it is from the likes of him.

articles.title: Mourinho claims he is ‘tired’ of press conferences and reveals reason for Diomande’s lack of minutes
articles.summary: Jose Mourinho says he is tired of press conferences.
articles.content:
Mourinho claims he is ‘tired’ of press conferences and reveals reason for Diomande’s lack of minutes

Jose Mourinho says he is tired of press conferences.

Last Update:

Jose Mourinho has never been short of things to say. Six press conferences in a week, however, are even testing his limits.

The Real Madrid manager appeared ahead of Tuesday’s La Liga clash with Elche, where he was in vintage form.

“I’d like to win, I’d like to play well and win, nothing more,” he said. “I hope that in three months we are better than we are today, but I have nothing magical to say that in three months we will be at an incredible level. In every match and training session, the goal is always to improve.

“The more time a coach has to work with a team, the greater the chances of becoming stronger.”

Asked about Real Madrid’s high-pressing approach, Mourinho added: “I don’t think it’s possible to press high for 90 minutes. I don’t think so, and it’s not our profile, nor are there many teams in the world capable of doing it for 90 minutes.

“If you ask me if I like a low block, I don’t. But what I don’t want are contradictions between what I like most and the qualities of my players. For me, that something is this ability to press high, this ability to kill in three or four seconds of transition.

“But I also don’t want to suffer in the sense that when we are deep, the opponent gets two or three shots that force the goalkeeper to make big saves and endure three, four or five corners.”

Diomande’s lack of starts & press conference fatigue

Mourinho was characteristically blunt in defending the squad rotation that has kept summer signing Yan Diomande on the bench for most of the season so far.

“He’s not missing anything. If he were in another team with fewer high-potential players instead of being at Madrid with this squad, he would probably be a starter playing 90 minutes every game.

“But when I say this about Diomande, I say it about everyone. A coach who only focuses on 10 players and forgets the rest runs out of fuel in the engine over the season and also loses motivation and internal competitiveness. This idea of an undisputed starter, as you all love to use that term, is difficult.”

And finally, the quote of the day, delivered in true Mourinho fashion.

“Six press conferences in one week. In other countries, they allowed me to skip one. But six press conferences in one week – I’m tired of you, and you’re tired of me.

“I always say the same thing and you don’t have any more questions to ask me, but here we are because it’s our job, mine and yours. If you tell me next week that we can skip one of these six, I’ll bring some snacks here and we’ll have some fun.”

articles.title: Kane scores winner as Bayern end fairytale start, PSG claim first win, Atletico bounce back and Juventus stunned
articles.summary: The England captain ensured the newly promoted side suffered their first loss.
articles.content:
Kane scores winner as Bayern end fairytale start, PSG claim first win, Atletico bounce back and Juventus stunned

The England captain ensured the newly promoted side suffered their first loss.

Last Update:

Bayern Munich were made to work hard to see off newly promoted Elversberg in the Bundesliga, with Harry Kane’s second-half strike proving decisive in a 2-1 win.

Elversberg have enjoyed a fairytale start to their debut campaign in the Bundesliga, beating Bayer Leverkusen and Borussia Monchengladbach, but they fell behind in the 26th minute as Lennart Karl slammed home at the far post from Ismael Saibari’s left-wing cross.

Elversberg’s Cole Campbell looked to have levelled shortly before half-time, only to see his goal ruled out for offside, but the hosts did equalise in spectacular fashion just after the hour, when former Bayern man Maurice Krattenmacher curled into the top-right corner from the edge of the area.

Michael Olise struck the crossbar before Bayern restored their slim advantage with Kane’s ultimately decisive effort, the England striker rifling home from Aleksandar Pavlovic’s lay-off.

The day’s other game in the Bundesliga saw RB Leipzig claim a thumping 5-0 victory over winless Hamburg, who are now bottom.

PSG end winless start

Paris Saint-Germain finally ended their surprising wait for a Ligue 1 win, the defending champions winning 1-0 at Brest.

Luis Enrique’s side had taken just two points from their opening three games, but Ferran Torres’ first-half strike proved enough for them to get off the mark with a first league victory.

The former Manchester City and Barcelona forward slotted home from the edge of the area after a sublime flicked lay-off from Ousmane Dembele.

Lille are in a group of three teams at the top on 10 points following their 2-0 win over Troyes.

Les Dogues had two goals disallowed for offside in the first half, but Tiago Santos’ 18th-minute effort and a late Ethan Mbappe goal secured the points.

Lille are top on goal difference, but last year’s runners-up Lens continued their stuttering start as they were forced to come from behind to draw 2-2 at Le Mans.

Atletico back to winning ways

Atletico Madrid bounced back from their defeats to Athletic Bilbao and Liverpool as they left it late to claim a 3-0 win at Real Sociedad.

Sociedad beat Atletico on penalties in last season’s Copa del Rey final, but Diego Simeone’s men gained a measure of revenge at the Anoeta.

Alejandro Grimaldo broke the deadlock from the penalty spot six minutes from time, coolly converting from 12 yards after Job Ochieng was ruled to have handled in the area.

Jonathan David then doubled the lead as he showed his composure to slot home his first goal for the club. Giuliano Simeone then added gloss to the scoreline in the 95th minute with a fine individual goal.

Atletico are five points behind LaLiga leaders Barcelona after the defending champions beat Levante 4-2 to make it five wins from five.

Elsewhere, Celta Vigo drew 1-1 with Malaga and Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang scored his fifth Deportivo La Coruna goal to keep them unbeaten with a 1-1 draw at Getafe.

Juve stunned by their own player

Juventus suffered their first Serie A defeat of the season as they were stunned by one of their own in a 3-2 defeat to Sassuolo.

Sebastiano Esposito put Sassuolo ahead in the 65th minute by scoring on his full debut for the hosts.

Edon Zhegrova levelled eight minutes from the end of normal time with the Sassuolo goalkeeper out of position after failing to claim a cross.

Kieron Bowie restored Sassuolo’s lead in the 89th minute after brilliant work from Darryl Bakola, only for Zhegrova to rifle Juve level again.

But there was a remarkable final twist as Juve were caught on the counter, with Vasilije Adzic — on loan from Juve — settling a dramatic contest by curling home the winner against his parent club.

Napoli avoided a third straight league defeat as Stanislav Lobotka’s goal gave them a 1-0 win over Bologna.

Elsewhere, Lecce beat Monza 3-2.

articles.title: ProRef acknowledge ‘error of judgement’ over Haaland’s Manchester derby-winning goal
articles.summary: The refereeing body conceded a mistake was made.
articles.content:
ProRef acknowledge ‘error of judgement’ over Haaland’s Manchester derby-winning goal

The refereeing body conceded a mistake was made.

Last Update:

Refereeing body ProRef has contacted Manchester United to acknowledge an error in awarding the goal scored by Erling Haaland that condemned them to defeat in the derby.

Manchester City claimed all three points at Old Trafford despite seeing Phil Foden sent off kicking Bruno Fernandes in the stomach in the 23rd minute.

The crucial moment came on the hour mark as Haaland steered the ball into the top-left corner from Josko Gvardiol’s deflected left-wing cross.

Haaland was initially flagged for offside but, after a lengthy VAR check, the goal was controversially awarded.

City’s Norwegian talisman was ruled to have been played onside by Patrick Dorgu, but the more contentious aspect of the decision concerned the involvement of Enzo Fernandez.

Fernandez was stood in an offside position when the cross was played in and attempted to get his head onto the ball. However, as he failed to do so, Fernandez was deemed not to be interfering with play.

ProRef acknowledge Haaland goal error

With Fernandez’s presence attracting the attention of Lisandro Martinez and, as such, leaving Haaland unmarked, that appeared to be an at best dubious interpretation of the rules, one that left United boss Michael Carrick “confused”.

And in a statement released late on Sunday, a ProRef spokesperson conceded a mistake on the part of the officials.

It read: “Following the incident in the 60th minute of Sunday’s Premier League fixture between Manchester United and Manchester City at Old Trafford, we can provide clarification regarding Erling Haaland’s awarded goal.

“The on-field decision was offside against Erling Haaland – that was checked by VAR and he was found to be in an onside position.

“In the same attack, it was established that Enzo Fernandez did not play the ball and therefore that makes any offside offence subjective, however, on this occasion, the VAR did not recognise the likely impact of his position and should have recommended an on-field review.

“Contact has been made with Manchester United this evening to acknowledge what we deem is an error of judgement. A review of the incident will take place.”

How did the managers react?

Speaking to Sky Sports after the game, Carrick said of the decision: “I’m confused. We put things in place in the game now. We have people in offices with all the screens for this decision.

“It’s more worrying if that’s the interpretation of football now. If that’s the interpretation of not interfering in the game now, that’s really worrying for me. It’s a staggering explanation.

“The decision isn’t going to change the season, but it’s had a major impact on the game. That decision wasn’t on us today. It’s up to us to create and score after that. We had moments. Of course it’s up to us to do that, but big moments in games like that have a big impact.”

His City counterpart Enzo Maresca unsurprisingly had a different view.

“It was completely clear that the goal was not offside,” Maresca told Sky Sports. “In the moment I was told by the fourth official, I celebrated early, because I knew.”

articles.title: ‘It was completely clear’ – Maresca claims he knew Haaland goal was not offside
articles.summary: The City boss never had any doubts.
articles.content:
‘It was completely clear’ – Maresca claims he knew Haaland goal was not offside

The City boss never had any doubts.

Last Update:

Enzo Maresca claimed he celebrated early for Erling Haaland’s controversial winner for 10-man Manchester City in the derby at Old Trafford as he knew it was not offside.

Haaland secured a 1-0 victory for City over arch rivals Manchester United, which maintained their perfect Premier League start under Maresca, as he netted the game’s only goal on the hour mark, steering Josko Gvardiol’s deflected cross to the far post into the top-left corner.

That goal was just reward for the way in which City adapted to going down to 10 men after Phil Foden was sent off for kicking Bruno Fernandes in the stomach in the 23rd minute.

It looked as if it would not be allowed to stand as the offside flag cut short Haaland’s celebrations. However, a lengthy VAR check deemed Haaland was being played onside by Patrick Dorgu. Enzo Fernandez, who was offside and only narrowly failed to make contact with Gvardiol’s delivery, was ruled to not have interfered with play.

While that decision left managerial counterpart Michael Carrick “confused”, City boss Maresca insisted it was obvious the goal was going to be allowed to stand.

“It was completely clear that the goal was not offside,” Maresca told Sky Sports. “In the moment I was told by the fourth official, I celebrated early, because I knew.”

Maresca heaped praise on the performance of City’s record signing Fernandez, and also had plenty of plaudits for goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma, who produced a brilliant save to deny Bryan Mbeumo late on after he was played through by Fernandes.

“Enzo Fernandez was unbelievable today and it was a nice for him to help us get the win,” Maresca added.

“And oh my God, the save. That’s why Donnarumma’s here. That’s why we bought him because he’s a fantastic goalkeeper.”

But the Italian took issue with referee Michael Oliver’s decision to only send Foden off following his altercation with Fernandes.

Foden kicked out at Fernandes after the Portuguese appeared to foul him and then kick the City forward while he was on the ground.

Maresca felt both infractions could be considered red card offences.

“The decision can be a red card for Foden,” he said. “But in the same action, it can be a red card for Bruno because he also kicks Phil.”

articles.title: Carrick ‘confused’ by VAR decision to allow Haaland goal as he defends United derby display
articles.summary: United endured a frustrating afternoon against 10-man City.
articles.content:
Carrick ‘confused’ by VAR decision to allow Haaland goal as he defends United derby display

United endured a frustrating afternoon against 10-man City.

Last Update:

Manchester United boss Michael Carrick was left “confused” and “worried” by the decision to allow Erling Haaland’s decisive goal in their derby defeat at Old Trafford.

United slumped to their second defeat of the campaign as they were beaten 1-0 at home by 10-man Manchester City, who had Phil Foden sent off in the 23rd minute for kicking Bruno Fernandes in the stomach.

But the Red Devils failed to make the extra man count, though Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo each hit the post, and they were punished as Haaland produced a fine close-range finish to steer Josko Gvardiol’s deflected cross to the far post back across goal and into the top-left corner.

Haaland’s celebrations were initially cut short by the offside flag but, after a lengthy VAR review, it was ruled that the Norway talisman was onside. Enzo Fernandez, who attacked the cross from an offside position but failed to make contact with his attempt to head the ball, was controversially ruled to not have interfered with play.

And it was that interpretation of the rules that left Carrick scratching his head, declaring it to be a “staggering” explanation.

“I’m confused,” Carrick told Sky Sports.

“We put things in place in the game now. We have people in offices with all the screens for this decision. It’s more worrying if that’s the interpretation of football now. If that’s the interpretation of not interfering in the game now, that’s really worrying for me. It’s a staggering explanation.

“The decision isn’t going to change the season, but it’s had a major impact on the game. That decision wasn’t on us today. It’s up to us to create and score after that. We had moments. Of course it’s up to us to do that, but big moments in games like that have a big impact.”

United had 16 shots in the game, with only three hitting the target.

Gianluigi Donnarumma tipped Rashford’s free-kick onto the post in first-half stoppage time and Mainoo rattled the frame of the goal seven minutes before Haaland broke the deadlock.

But Carrick’s men struggled to craft clear-cut opportunities from open play, their best coming right at the death as Fernandes threaded a ball through to Bryan Mbeumo, only for the forward to be denied by an excellent save from Donnarumma.

Despite a frustrating afternoon for United, Carrick defended his side’s performance after they suffered a second defeat in four Premier League games to start his first season in permanent charge.

“We did a lot of things well, it looked like we were growing well into the game,” Carrick added.

“We looked dangerous. We’ll take the positives from the game today and move on well, but we’re not moving on lightly.

“We could have created more. That’s an answer for us, but we could have. That’s our second defeat now, since I’ve been in charge, but we’re a good team and we’ll get back to wining ways.

articles.title: Lampard rues ‘difficult’ afternoon as Coventry hammered by rampant Brighton
articles.summary: Coventry remain without a point and a goal following a 5-0 hammering by Brighton this afternoon
articles.content:
Lampard rues ‘difficult’ afternoon as Coventry hammered by rampant Brighton

Coventry remain without a point and a goal following a 5-0 hammering by Brighton this afternoon

Last Update:

Frank Lampard conceded it was a “difficult scoreline” to contend with after his Coventry side were hammered 5-0 by Brighton this afternoon.

The Sky Blues competed well for the opening half-hour but fell apart after Brighton scored through Charalampos Kostoulas and Malick Yalcouye either side of the break.

Taiwo Awoniyi was sent off for an awful elbow in the face of Maxim De Cuyper and the 10-man hosts had no answers as Brighton scored again through a Pascal Gross penalty and long-range strikes from Lewis Dunk and Yasin Ayari.

The defeat means Coventry have yet to pick up a point, or score a goal, in their four games following promotion.

Lampard told BBC Match of the Day: “It’s a difficult scoreline and it’s not easy at home. The first half was pretty good, we created some chances, better chances and we had them under a lot of pressure. Then a mistake to make it 2-0 and the red card makes it very difficult.

“We have to take responsibility. We did some good stuff, then the game became very, very difficult for us. We have to keep working. At [Manchester] City last week we created a few big chances and [Gianluigi] Donnarumma made some good saves. The pressure of the Premier League for these players is new. We have to continue to work and hopefully when we start scoring, and this team scored a lot of goals last season, but we have to keep working.

“I can’t complain with the players at the end.”

Hurzeler playing it cool after superb Brighton move fourth

The win moved Brighton up to fourth in the Premier League table but boss Fabian Hurzeler was not getting carried away.

He said: “It’s important to stay humble and not take these things for granted. Overall we are a team where a lot of players can score goals and that brings us a lot of flexibility which is good for a coach as well.”

Dunk’s was the goal of the game, the former England centre-half smashing a stunning 25-yard effort into the top corner.

“I’ve got that sort of shot in my locker and I just had a shot and it went in the top corner. I shocked myself but it was lovely,” he said on Sky Sports.

“We’ve shown fluidity and we have some real quality high up the pitch. If we keep scoring goals like that and keeping clean sheets, we’ll have a great season.”

articles.title: Ronaldo speaks out after Neves subjected to vile abuse from fans over Jota death
articles.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo has leapt to the defence of Ruben Neves after his fellow Portuguese was mocked over the death of his best friend Diogo Jota
articles.content:
Ronaldo speaks out after Neves subjected to vile abuse from fans over Jota death

Cristiano Ronaldo has leapt to the defence of Ruben Neves after his fellow Portuguese was mocked over the death of his best friend Diogo Jota

Last Update:

Cristiano Ronaldo has demanded lifetime bans for supporters who taunted Ruben Neves over the death of former Liverpool star Diogo Jota.

Fans of Saudi Pro League side Al-Taawoun repeatedly chanted Jota’s name in Neves’ direction during the game against Al-Hilal on Saturday.

Jota, a former Portugal team-mate of both Neves and Ronaldo, was killed in a car crash in Northern Spain in July 2025. Neves was Jota’s best friend and a pallbearer at his funeral.

Ronaldo, who also plays in Saudi Arabia for Al-Nassr, took to social media to demand action be taken.

He wrote: “The league must take action and punish this kind of fan behaviour. This is no longer football, and there have to be limits. People who behave like this should never be allowed to enter a stadium again.”

Neves showed his disgust during the game, indicating that ‘God is watching’ by pointing at the sky, his eyes and then the fans during a game his side won 6-0.

Afterwards, he was asked about the incidents, and said: “I hope they [the fans] don’t go to prayer later.”

Saudi international disgusted by chants

Al-Ahli’s Saudi Arabia international Saleh Abu Al-Shamat, also spoke out against the fans’ actions.

“I wanted to draw attention to something we all witnessed today. I felt it was my duty – as a Muslim – to share this and raise awareness,’ Abu Al-Shamat wrote on Instagram.

“No-one is perfect, of course, but regarding the actions of some Al-Taawoun fans during the match against Al-Hilal: this isn’t just about our club; it concerns our great religion, Islam.

“No matter how intense the rivalry or the situation, we should never stoop to gloating over the dead, engaging in slander, or attacking people’s families or the deceased.

“We live in an Islamic country, and it is our duty to show the world what Islam truly represents—a religion of love, tolerance, and respect. I hope we can leverage the massive attention our league is receiving to project the best possible image of Islam.

“By doing so, we might foster goodwill and help others learn about our faith. That is the message I wanted to convey; I felt a personal obligation, as a Muslim living in this great Islamic nation, to speak out against what is happening – because it is wrong and unacceptable.”

articles.title: Lionel Messi goal not enough as Inter Miami’s miserable run continues
articles.summary: Inter Miami have won just one of their last nine games in all competitions. Lionel Messi scored again against Nashville SC last night but it was not enough to give the home side all three points.
articles.content:
Lionel Messi goal not enough as Inter Miami’s miserable run continues

Inter Miami have won just one of their last nine games in all competitions. Lionel Messi scored again against Nashville SC last night but it was not enough to give the home side all three points.

Last Update:

Lionel Messi’s superb second-half strike was not enough as Inter Miami’s hopes of regaining the MLS Supporters’ Shield were hit by a 2-2 draw against Eastern Conference leaders Nashville SC at Nu Stadium on Saturday night.

Messi scored with a trademark left-footed curling strike in the second half but Sam Surridge had the final say with a dramatic injury-time equaliser as Nashville preserved their nine-point lead at the top of the table.

Surridge had earlier given Nashville an early lead only for visiting defender Reed Baker-Whiting to glance Messi’s corner into his own net after 19 minutes.

The Argentine superstar was a constant threat and had two more chances to make it 2-1 before half-time. His first effort was blocked and the second, a free-kick from outside the area, flew just wide.

He did find the back of the net shortly after the hour mark, trading passes with Rodrigo De Paul, before placing his shot past Nashville goalkeeper Brian Schwake. It was Messi’s 19th goal of the season, moving him one ahead of FC Dallas’ Petar Musa in the race for the Golden Boot.

Surridge has final say to deny Messi and Miami

Schwake kept his side in the contest, tipping Messi’s shot on to the post, before Nashville defender Jeisson Palacios produced a brilliant last-ditch headed clearance to deny him again.

And Nashville applied the sucker punch late on when Surridge tapped in after Shak Mohammed’s shot was palmed into his path by home goalkeeper Dayne St Clair.

There was still time for De Paul to hit the post but Nashville held on. The draw means Miami, who claimed the Supporters’ Shield in 2024, have won just one of the last nine games in all competitions.

Defender Facunda Mura said: “Obviously, there’s frustration – feeling like we were the better side only to have the three points snatched away in the final moments. But there’s also the feeling that the team did manage to keep possession and create scoring chances.

“We need to improve so that we don’t always have to score so many goals just to get the win; we need to feel a bit more secure at the back and stop conceding, so that the goals we do score are enough.”

Guillermo Hoyos continues to lead the side while Miami wait for a work visa for new coach Kily Gonzalez. Hoyos is likely to be in charge again for Wednesday night’s Campeones Cup clash with Mexican side Cruz Azul.

“We have great players, and we have to compete for every trophy we play for,” Mura added. “Unfortunately, things haven’t gone our way in the CONCACAF Champions Cup or the Leagues Cup. We haven’t gotten the results we wanted; we’re well aware of that. But ultimately, we’re here to keep working and keep growing.

“We’re starting a new phase with a new coach, and we all know we need to give more to help the team improve and reach a higher level – especially since we have a final coming up in just four days that we really want to win.”

Nashville march on as Messi’s hopes wilt

While there was frustration for Miami, it was a superb result for Nashville, who are now in pole position to land silverware with just nine games remaining in the regular season.

“This was a big boys’ game tonight,” Nashville head coach BJ Callaghan said. “Two really good teams going toe to toe.

“I thought the game had a lot of intensity, a lot of physicality, some high-level play. Really proud of the group.”

Nashville are in action again next Saturday when they face Chicago Fire at GEODIS Park.

articles.title: Premier League round-up: Jesus condemns Villa to another defeat, Ipswich stun 10-man Palace
articles.summary: Aston Villa's problems are mounting, but Ipswich are in dreamland after a late win in south London.
articles.content:
Premier League round-up: Jesus condemns Villa to another defeat, Ipswich stun 10-man Palace

Aston Villa's problems are mounting, but Ipswich are in dreamland after a late win in south London.

Last Update:

Igor Jesus condemned Aston Villa to their third defeat in four Premier League games as his late strike gave Nottingham Forest a 2-1 away win, their first triumph under Oliver Glasner.

After a goalless first half, the game burst into life quickly after the second-half restart when Liam Delap broke the deadlock with his first goal for Forest, beating Zion Suzuki by finding the bottom-left corner from 20 yards out.

Dan Ndoye headed over from close range as he wasted a clear chance to make it 2-0, and Delap had the ball in the net again, only to see that effort ruled out for offside.

It looked as if Forest would live to rue those missed opportunities when Alysson scored Villa’s first league goal of the season by nodding in from John McGinn’s cross.

But there was a sting in the tail in the 88th minute with Villa down to 10 after Ian Maatsen limped off with the hosts having made all of their five substitutions.

Morgan Gibbs-White flicked a Daniel Munoz cutback into the path of Jesus, who steered home from six yards out to seal the points.

Villa are second-bottom with just one point from four games, while Forest are in a quartet of teams on five points.

Flemming the hero as Ipswich win thriller

While Hull City made more headlines by maintaining their remarkable unbeaten start with a 2-2 draw at Chelsea, their fellow newly promoted side Ipswich Town moved into the top half by emerging victorious from an incredible game against Crystal Palace, winning 3-2 at Selhurst Park.

Palace, who claimed their first league win of the season at Fulham last week, took the lead in the 14th minute when Anan Khalaili netted his first goal for the club, arrowing home from Daichi Kamada’s pass.

Nine minutes later Ipswich levelled as Emersonn was giving a simple header to restore parity from Leif Davis’ left-wing cross.

Palace’s problems mounted when they were reduced to 10 men as Axel Disasi saw red for a late and high tackle on Jack Clarke.

The Tractor Boys took advantage as Emersonn and Davis swapped roles, the Brazilian flicking on for the left-back to head home at the back post.

Yet Palace appeared to have rescued a share of the spoils 15 minutes from the end of normal time when Jorgen Strand Larsen fired home on the turn.

Khalaili spurned a chance for his second as Palace looked to complete the turnaround, and the Eagles paid for his profligacy as Zian Flemming tucked home on the rebound after Walter Benitez had kept out Davis’ header. Flemming’s first goal since joining from Burnley moved Ipswich up to seventh in the table.

Bournemouth let another lead slip

Bournemouth are still waiting for a first league win under Marco Rose as they let another winning position slip in a 2-2 draw with Brentford.

Kevin Schade gave Brentford the lead on the south coast by heading in from Yehor Yarmoliuk’s cross after a defensive error from Adrien Truffert.

Rayan inexplicably missed from six yards out as Bournemouth sought a leveller, which arrived through Justin Kluivert’s left-footed drive.

The Cherries completed the turnaround seven minutes into the second half when Marcus Tavernier capped off a well-worked move by slotting into the far corner.

But four minutes later Bournemouth threw the lead away, Schade restoring parity with a lob over the head of Djordje Petrovic after the goalkeeper had passed the ball straight to the winger.

Bournemouth have led in all four of their Premier League games this season without winning any of them. They are 15th with three points from four games, while an impressive start from Brentford has them fifth with six points.

articles.title: Watford sign former West Ham striker Michail Antonio after car crash incident
articles.summary: Michail Antonio has finally found a new club in England
articles.content:
Watford sign former West Ham striker Michail Antonio after car crash incident

Michail Antonio has finally found a new club in England

Last Update:

Former West Ham striker Michail Antonio has called Watford “a big club” after joining the Hornets on a free transfer on a one-year deal.

The 36-year-old has spent a month training with Alessio Dionisi’s side and is awaiting international clearance to make his debut at home to Stoke City on Saturday.

“It’s a good set of boys here,” Antonio told Watford’s website. “They are focused and ready to show their abilities this season.

“Watford is a big club and hopefully I can come in and bring success and help wherever I can.

“I’ve scored a few goals against Watford, so hopefully I can score some for Watford now when I’m fully up to speed.”

Antonio’s final appearance for West Ham came in a 3-1 defeat at Leicester City in the Premier League on December 3, 2024.

Four days later, Antonio suffered a broken leg in a car crash and spent several months recovering.

The Jamaica international was released by West Ham in June 2025 following a 10-year spell with the club, but returned to train with his former club during his rehabilitation.

Still the Hammers’ 68-goal all-time top scorer in the Premier League, Antonio made two appearances for their Under-21 side in Premier League 2 before continuing his search for a return to senior football.

The former Nottingham Forest, Sheffield Wednesday, Reading and Tooting & Mitcham United hitman briefly joined Qatari side Al-Sailiya this year, making the last of his four appearances for the club in April.

Watford drew 1-1 at home to West Ham in the second tier last month and are scheduled to visit the London Stadium on April 17.

articles.title: Lucas Bergvall signs new contract at Tottenham
articles.summary: Tottenham’s Lucas Bergvall has extended his contract at the club
articles.content:
Lucas Bergvall signs new contract at Tottenham

Tottenham’s Lucas Bergvall has extended his contract at the club

Last Update:

Tottenham midfielder has signed a new contract with the club, ending speculation that the Swedish midfielder is looking for a move away from North London.

The 20-year-old has already made 80 appearances across all competitions for Spurs and is valued highly by head coach Roberto De Zerbi.

Speaking on his new deal, Bergvall said: “We’re building something great here. It’s an exciting time for the club and that’s why I’m happy to extend my contract.

“I’m always trying to achieve as much as possible, to be the best version of myself both on and off the pitch and I know this is the right place to do that.

“Personally, my goal is to produce more for the team – performances, goals and assists – to help as much as I can. I’m getting better every day in training and I’m looking forward to what will be a really good season ahead.”

De Zerbi added: “Every day in training you can see Lucas’ desire to learn, improve and push himself to the highest level.

“Lucas is brave, he wants responsibility and has the personality to play in big moments. He also understands that development is a process and he has shown a fantastic attitude towards working on the areas of his game where he can become even better.

“I believe his best football is still ahead of him and we want to give Lucas the platform to reach his full potential.”

Nottingham Forest and Chelsea were interested in Bergvall this summer, but he has opted to commit his long-term future to Spurs after playing a key role for Sweden at the World Cup this summer.

articles.title: Carrick hails ‘fantastic’ Mainoo as United impress on Champions League return
articles.summary: Michael Carrick praised Kobbie Mainoo’s impressive performance and paid tribute to a stubborn Sabah side as Manchester United marked their return to the Champions League with a 4-0 win at Old Trafford on Thursday night. Matheus Cunha opened the scoring in the 27th minute, touching in Patrick Dorgu’s cross delicately at the back post, before […]
articles.content:
Carrick hails ‘fantastic’ Mainoo as United impress on Champions League return

Last Update:

Michael Carrick praised Kobbie Mainoo’s impressive performance and paid tribute to a stubborn Sabah side as Manchester United marked their return to the Champions League with a 4-0 win at Old Trafford on Thursday night.

Matheus Cunha opened the scoring in the 27th minute, touching in Patrick Dorgu’s cross delicately at the back post, before Bruno Fernandes and Benjamin Sesko both struck in the closing stages of the first half to put the tie beyond the Azerbaijani side.

Lisandro Martinez added a fourth in the second period after an impressive showing from substitute Joshua Zirkzee.

Sabah, making their Champions League proper debut, caused United some discomfort in the early stages and Joy-Lance Mickels spurned a genuine opportunity to equalise after Cunha’s opener, but the gulf in quality told emphatically as the evening wore on.

Carrick was fair in his assessment when speaking post-match, acknowledging that the scoreline flattered United’s evening.

“It’s nice to have a clean sheet! And obviously win the game,” he said.

“There was a lot. I thought some of our attacking play was fantastic, some of the football we played was really good, dangerous on transition. Defended for the most part really well.

“I have to give them a lot of credit, really tough team to play against. They play little connections and make you really work to get the ball back.

The result looks comfortable, it wasn’t always like that. But I thought we just did a lot of good things tonight which gave us a good result.”

Carrick salutes Mainoo

The performance that drew most attention came from Kobbie Mainoo, who completed 81 passes across his 64 minutes on the pitch,the most by an Englishman in a Champions League match for United since Carrick himself made 89 against Olympiakos in February 2014.

“He’s a fantastic player, Kobbie, I think it’s pretty obvious to see,” Carrick said. “The way he’s performing, playing that little bit deeper, really, and connecting the attacks, starting the attacks.

“Having a massive influence on our games. He’s a real joy to have – he wants to learn, he wants to listen – and he expresses himself on the pitch. It’s great to see.”

articles.title: Man United teenager Gabriel scores hat-trick in UEFA Youth League demolition
articles.summary: JJ Gabriel furthered his case for an historic first-team appearance by scoring a hat-trick on his Youth League debut.
articles.content:
Man United teenager Gabriel scores hat-trick in UEFA Youth League demolition

JJ Gabriel furthered his case for an historic first-team appearance by scoring a hat-trick on his Youth League debut.

Last Update:

JJ Gabriel has been compared to Wayne Rooney by Ryan Giggs, and the Manchester United teenager produced a performance to further the hype around him in a 5-0 win over Sabah in the UEFA Youth League on Thursday.

Gabriel, 15, was a regular feature in United’s pre-season squads this summer, though he featured in just one of those games, against Atletico Madrid in Stockholm. However, his proximity to Michael Carrick’s squad and his performances at youth level have led to talk of him becoming United’s youngest first-team player.

David Gaskell, who made his debut in the 1956 Charity Shield aged 16 years and 19 days, holds the honour of being the youngest player in United’s history.

Gabriel does not turn 16 until October and furthered his case for inclusion by scoring a hat-trick as United crushed Azerbaijani side Sabah to open their Youth League campaign.

It was one way traffic throughout, with United attempting a remarkable 44 shots to Sabah’s 0.

United were 2-0 up inside 16 minutes, but Gabriel’s first did not arrive until the stroke of half-time as he volleyed in from close range after excellent chest control.

His second came five minutes before the end of normal time as he cut inside a defender and slotted into the bottom-right corner.

Two minute he completed the treble by latching onto a ball over the top and rifling into the top-left corner, marking his debut in the Youth League in sublime fashion.

What has Michael Carrick said about Gabriel?

When previously asked about Gabriel, Carrick indicated there is no rush for him to be moved into the first-team squad for competitive games.

“JJ is one of the boys,” Carrick said. “He’s obviously got a really big talent. He’s trained with us quite a bit and is getting experience all the time.

“He’s physically adapting to each step, and we’re just continuing his development.”

Any need Carrick feels to protect Gabriel would be understandable, but the more he continues to shine to this extent, the more it may be harder to avoid giving the teenager an historic debut.

BREAKING: Real Madrid star Guler agrees new contract

Turkey midfielder Arda Guler has committed his future to Real Madrid, according to reports in Spain

Real Madrid midfielder Arda Guler has agreed terms on a new contract that will tie him to the Spanish giants until 2031, according to reports.

Guler originally signed a contract until 2029, when he moved to Real Madrid.

The new terms are intended to recognise Guler’s growing importance to the first team rather than the status he had when he first arrived in Spain.

According to AS, the new agreement is already complete and is expected to take effect from the beginning of the current season.

Mourinho’s plans for Guler

Jose Mourinho’s arrival at Real Madrid has also helped clarify Guler’s role within the team.

The Portuguese manager views him as an attacking midfielder rather than a central midfielder.

That could provide Guler with a clearer path into the starting XI, given the competition for central midfield places from players including Bernardo Silva, Federico Valverde, Eduardo Camavinga and Aurelien Tchouameni.

Madrid were initially forced to be patient with Guler as he adapted to the demands of playing for one of the world’s biggest clubs.

His situation is now very different, with the club viewing him as an increasingly important part of their first-team plans.

articles.title: Jaissle ‘in love’ with Hall amid reports of new contract for Newcastle left-back
articles.summary: Newcastle's left-back has reportedly agreed to a new contract to stay at the club until 2031.
articles.content:
Jaissle ‘in love’ with Hall amid reports of new contract for Newcastle left-back

Newcastle's left-back has reportedly agreed to a new contract to stay at the club until 2031.

Last Update:

Newcastle United boss Matthias Jaissle is excited at the prospect of working with Lewis Hall, claiming he is “in love” with the left-back amid reports he has agreed to a new contract with the club.

Hall was the subject of speculation linking him with a move to Manchester United this summer, as several other key members of the Magpies squad left for pastures new.

But the England international, a surprise omission from the World Cup squad, stayed at St James’ Park, and has reportedly agreed a new deal to remain with Newcastle until 2031.

That is unlikely to stop future gossip about a potential move, but Jaissle is relishing the opportunity to further Hall’s development after an impressive start to the new campaign from the 22-year-old.

“Without speaking about his contract, I can just say that I’m in love with what I’ve seen so far from him,” Jaissle told a press conference ahead of Monday’s Premier League clash with Leeds United at Elland Road.

“It’s an amazing player with huge potential still, and this makes me so happy to, hopefully, have him here for the next years in the long term.

“He’s fitting so good to to this identity, how we want to play football, and again, he’s doing an excellent job.”

Newcastle boss: Fernandez-Pardo ‘getting closer’ to first start

Newcastle’s final signing of a busy summer transfer window saw them bring in Belgium forward Matias Fernandez-Pardo from Lille in a £51million deal.

The 21-year-old has since made two substitute appearances for the Magpies, and it was he and Hall who combined to tee up Joe Willock for the only goal in Newcastle’s 1-0 EFL Cup win over Millwall on Tuesday.

Asked if Fernandez-Pardo is ready to start against Leeds, Jaissle replied: “He’s getting closer. I said that we need to be smart with his load management.

“Now he’s getting more and more minutes. He has now almost a full training week to Leeds, that helps him a lot. I think it’s the first time now since he arrived, and then we can make the decision on Sunday, maybe even on Monday.”

Newcastle are unbeaten in five games in all competitions under Jaissle, defying expectations following the loss of Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimaraes in the summer and the departure of former manager Eddie Howe at the end of July.

“We are happy with the start we’ve had definitely,” Jaissle added.

“It’s not normal after such a short amount of time together, but the Premier League is the Premier League. Every matchday it’s top opponents. Again, against Leeds it will be a tough away match. We want to continue that journey. We are ambitious but we are realistic.”

Jaissle revealed that a hamstring injury to right-back Amar Dedic “does not look too serious”. Tino Livramento will likely start at that spot if the Bosnia-Herzegovina international is unavailable.

articles.title: French Football Federation withdraws support for Infantino’s re-election bid
articles.summary: It's another setback for the embattled FIFA president.
articles.content:
French Football Federation withdraws support for Infantino’s re-election bid

It's another setback for the embattled FIFA president.

Last Update:

The French Football Federation (FFF) has withdrawn its support for the re-election of Gianni Infantino as FIFA president.

Infantino, who is currently set to run unopposed next March, has faced widespread criticism over his failed plans to sell stakes in the World Cup and FIFA’s other major tournaments to private investors.

Those proposals sparked outrage across the football world, and it emerged last month that European football’s governing body, UEFA, is pursuing a criminal complaint against Infantino.

UEFA, the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) and North America’s CONCACAF have all called for change at the top of FIFA and are seeking a credible alternative to Infantino.

England’s Football Association and the Italian Football Federation are among the European FIFA members to have withdrawn their backing for Infantino.

And on Thursday they were joined by the FFF after its Executive Committee voted unanimously to take that step.

A statement from the FFF read: “The FFF withdraws its support for Gianni Infantino’s re-election and calls for fundamental reform of FIFA’s governance.

“Meeting today in Paris at the request of its President, Philippe Diallo, the Executive Committee of the French Football Federation unanimously decided to withdraw the FFF’s support for Gianni Infantino ahead of the FIFA presidential election, which is due to take place on 18 March 2027 in Rabat (Morocco).

“Whilst support had initially been given to the FIFA President, who was then the sole candidate for his own succession, the conditions for that support are no longer met.

“A series of events directly involving FIFA’s governance and its President, and in direct conflict with the fundamental principles of good governance and the values of football, occurred after the FFF expressed its support on 29 June.”

FFF: FIFA governance not fixed by failure of Infantino’s plans

The FFF made it clear that, while Infantino’s ‘FIFA Forward Enterprise’ plans had not come to fruition, the failure of the proposals does not fix the problems at the top of world football’s governing body.

Its statement continued: “At the end of July, a plan spearheaded by the FIFA President was revealed, aimed at creating a commercial company incorporating, in particular, the rights to the World Cup and opening up its share capital to external investors.

“The FFF, through its President, emphasised that “a project with such a significant impact on the future of football could not be envisaged without comprehensive information, in-depth consultation and a fully transparent decision-making process. FIFA’s governance does not live up to the standards that football represents.”

“Today, whilst this project has been definitively abandoned thanks to a concerted response within UEFA in conjunction with several other confederations, the issue of FIFA’s governance cannot be considered resolved.

“It is against this backdrop – where the FIFA President’s recent initiatives have seriously damaged the image and unity of football – that the FFF has decided to withdraw its support for Gianni Infantino ahead of the FIFA presidential election in March 2027.

“The FFF calls for the development, in consultation with the confederations, national associations and all stakeholders (players, supporters, etc.), of a plan for world football to undertake a far-reaching reform of FIFA’s governance and to continue the development of football by combining excellence and solidarity.

“With this objective in mind, the FFF will, in the coming days, launch a series of consultations with leading French and international figures whose expertise in governance, including beyond the sporting sphere, is widely recognised.

“The aim of these consultations will be to foster collective reflection and to draw up proposals for a far-reaching transformation of FIFA’s governance, with a view to restoring confidence, enhancing transparency and ensuring the independence and exemplary conduct of world football’s governing body.

“The FFF, a founding member of FIFA, thus intends to contribute to a debate that is vital for the future of football, its regulation and its development.”

articles.title: Barcelona chief Deco says Lamine Yamal should win the 2026 Ballon d’Or, ‘no discussion’
articles.summary: Barcelona winger Lamine Yamal is among the favourites to win the Ballon d"or and his case has been endorsed by the club's sporting director Deco
articles.content:
Barcelona chief Deco says Lamine Yamal should win the 2026 Ballon d’Or, ‘no discussion’

Barcelona winger Lamine Yamal is among the favourites to win the Ballon d"or and his case has been endorsed by the club's sporting director Deco

Last Update:

Barcelona sporting director Deco says there should be “no discussion” around the winner of the 2026 Ballon d’Or and also outlined his anger at the omission of two Blaugrana favourites among the 30 contenders.

The shortlist was revealed on Tuesday with Barca winger Lamine Yamal one of the favourites after a brilliant season that, although derailed towards the end by injury, saw him play a pivotal role as the Catalan giants retained La Liga.

The 19-year-old then helped Spain win the World Cup in the United States, Canada and Mexico.

Deco believes those achievements place him above the likes of Harry Kane, Kylian Mbappe and Lionel Messi.

He told RAC 1: “Lamine should be the favourite for the Ballon d’Or. For me, no discussion. Remember everything he’s done with Barça and the national team. He’s had some decisive moments, even going to the World Cup with an injury. Last season was key.

“It’s like when [former Barcelona winger] Leo [Messi] won and Leo was the best.”

Deco angry at omission of Pedri and Raphinha

Deco could not hide his irritation when asked about the non-inclusion of two more Barca players – Pedri and Raphinha – describing it as a “world scandal”.

He added: ”I don’t understand the lists and how they are made, but there are injustices in the awards.

”That Pedri is not in for his talent, like Raphinha, is difficult to see.”

Barca did have a couple of other players on the shortlist – Pau Cubarsí and new signing Rodri – and president Joan Laporta expressed his delight on Wednesday at recognition of the club’s achievements.

“Barça is a unique club and proof of this is in these nominations. We are very proud,” Laporta said. “The players we have must be grateful to Barcelona Football Club for what it gives them. I will be immensely happy if a Barça player wins.”

On Yamal, he added: “He’s spectacular. He has an exceptional quality, he is a genius and I think his nomination for the Ballon d’Or is more than deserved. He has a maturity for his age, [that’s] fantastic. I feel bad when you talk about the nominations that neither Pedri nor Raphinha are nominated. I think they have also made a case; for their quality they deserved to be nominated.”

The full list of nominees for the men’s 2026 Ballon d’Or award

Jude Bellingham (Real Madrid)Pau Cubarsi (Barcelona)Marc Cucurella (Real Madrid)Ousmane Dembele (PSG)Luis Diaz (Bayern Munich)Bruno Fernandes (Manchester United)Erling Haaland (Manchester City)Gabriel (Arsenal)Harry Kane (Bayern Munich)Achraf Hakimi (PSG)Lamine Yamal (Barcelona)Khvicha Kvaratskhelia (PSG)Marquinhos (PSG)Sadio Mane (Al-Nassr)Lautaro Martinez (Inter Milan)Kylian Mbappe (Real Madrid)Nuno Mendes (PSG)Lionel Messi (Inter Miami)Michael Olise (Bayern Munich)Joao Neves (PSG)Willian Pacho (PSG)Julian Quinones (Al-Qadsiah)Declan Rice (Arsenal)Rodri (Barcelona)Fabian Ruiz (PSG)Ferran Torres (PSG)William Saliba (Arsenal)Dayor Upamecano (Bayern Munich)Vinicius Jr (Real Madrid)Vitinha (PSG)

How does the voting for the Ballon d’Or work?

The 30-player shortlist for the main awards is voted for by a panel of journalists from France Football and L’Equipe.

One journalist from each of the top 100 countries in the FIFA rankings then votes for their top 10 from each list with each position afforded a certain number of points.

Which players have won the men’s award previously?

2025: Ousmane Dembele2024: Rodri 2023: Lionel Messi2022: Karim Benzema 2021: Lionel Messi 2019: Lionel Messi

When will the award be handed out?

The ceremony will take place on Monday, October 26 in London.

articles.title: ‘Who are you dummy? I’ve won two Copas America and the World Cup’ – Messi’s mate De Paul lashes out at Lewandowski
articles.summary: Robert Lewandowski scored a brilliant goal as the Chicago Fire secured a 1-1 draw with Lionel Messi's Inter Miami on Wednesday night
articles.content:
‘Who are you dummy? I’ve won two Copas America and the World Cup’ – Messi’s mate De Paul lashes out at Lewandowski

Robert Lewandowski scored a brilliant goal as the Chicago Fire secured a 1-1 draw with Lionel Messi's Inter Miami on Wednesday night

Last Update:

Robert Lewandowski stole the limelight from Lionel Messi with a brilliant goal and a verbal spat with Rodrigo De Paul as the Chicago Fire secured a 1-1 draw with Inter Miami.

A crowd of over 63,000 at Soldier Field was treated to a tetchy encounter lit up initially by Lewandowski’s brilliant volley that put the home side ahead after nine minutes. The Pole found space at the far post and acrobatically fired into the left-hand corner although credit must also go to Andrew Gutman for a superb cross from the left.

Miami responded well and Fire goalkeeper Chris Brady made three good saves, the best of which saw him get down low to deny German Berterame in the 16th minute.

Brady started the second half the same way, keeping out a Messi effort while former Miami defender Noah Allen also distinguished himself with a goal-saving tackle. But the hosts could not repel the subsequent corner from Messi with Casemiro heading home.

De Paul mocks Lewandowski but ends up looking the fool

The two teams traded chances before they then traded insults.

The spark was a push by Lewandowski on Fire defender Ian Fray. Fray responded with a push of his own, prompting other players to get involved, including De Paul who shouted in Lewandowski’s face: “Who are you, dummy? I’ve won two Copas América and a World Cup. You?”

The actions of De Paul, who was a key part of Argentina’s lamentable behaviour during the World Cup, actually diffused the situation with players from both sides finding his intervention comical.

The draw saw Miami cut their deficit to Eastern Conference leaders Nashville, who lost to Toronto FC earlier in the day, to nine points. Chicago are a further five points back after their fourth successive draw.

“We still have work to do, and you can see it,” Chicago Fire director of football and head coach Gregg Berhalter said. “We need to get better because we weren’t in a position to dictate the game for long enough. We’re hanging out, and we don’t want to be in that position. They have a good team. I don’t want to take anything away from their team, but we can do a better job.”

Hoyos feels Miami deserved the win

articles.title: Arteta says Arsenal performance ‘was superb’ despite missed chances in Champions League win over Napoli
articles.summary: Martin Odegaard proved the difference maker on tricky trip
articles.content:
Arteta says Arsenal performance ‘was superb’ despite missed chances in Champions League win over Napoli

Martin Odegaard proved the difference maker on tricky trip

Last Update:

Mikel Arteta heaped praise on his Arsenal side’s dominant display after Martin Odegaard’s decisive strike earned the Gunners a hard-fought 1-0 victory away against Napoli in their Champions League opener.

The Gunners controlled proceedings at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona, dominating territory and carving out 26 attempts while limiting the hosts to just five shots all evening.

Despite the overwhelming superiority, Arsenal repeatedly failed to convert their openings, with Bukayo Saka, Mikel Merino, Piero Hincapié, and Noni Madueke all missing clear sights of goal.

The breakthrough finally arrived 15 minutes from time when substitute Christos Tzolis helped orchestrate a neat move, allowing captain Odegaard to step up and fire home the crucial winner.

‘The team was superb’

“It was a fully deserved three points. The performance probably doesn’t reflect the result, the team was superb,” Arteta said.

“We showed quality in a lot of moments to break them down and it was a shame because we missed so many great chances. On any other day the result would be different. We should have done it in a different way because of the amount of chances we created.”

The Spanish manager also singled out his match-winning skipper for special praise, highlighting the midfielder’s growing knack for delivering decisive goals when his side needs them most to maintain their 100 per cent start to the campaign.

“Martin is contributing with goals that are impacting results which is what we want from our attacking players, being decisive and certainly he was again today,” Arteta added.

The narrow victory gets Arsenal’s European journey off to a winning start, rewarding their territorial control and adding vital momentum ahead of their upcoming Premier League trip to face Sunderland.

articles.title: Flick proud of Barcelona identity and says he is ‘really enjoying’ Camp Nou reign
articles.summary: Barcelona are flying at the start of the season
articles.content:
Flick proud of Barcelona identity and says he is ‘really enjoying’ Camp Nou reign

Barcelona are flying at the start of the season

Last Update:

Hansi Flick hailed the collective mentality of his Barcelona side, insisting he is “really enjoying” life in the dugout as the Blaugrana continued their flawless start to the season with a 5-1 thrashing of Feyenoord.

The German coach has overseen five consecutive victories across all competitions to open the 2026–27 campaign, with Barca already racking up 21 goals in that span.

After the latest Champions League rout at Camp Nou, Flick made no secret of his happiness with how quickly his squad have adopted his intense tactical blueprint.

‘I’m really happy to be here’

“I’m really pleased that all I can talk about is enjoying myself,” Flick said. “I am the coach of Barça, and I’m truly happy to be here.

“In our first five games we have done really well. We’ve scored a lot of goals, but for me, the most important thing is that we are playing as a team, as a unit. We dominate and control games. That’s the style we want to play; we want our supporters to enjoy our football, and right now they are really enjoying it.”

Barca set the tone inside three minutes when captain Raphinha sidestepped two defenders in the area to lash home his seventh goal of the campaign.

Summer arrival Karim Adeyemi, stepping into the starting lineup for Anthony Gordon, quickly doubled the lead with a sensational 20-yard curler into the corner. Raphinha grabbed his second after the interval courtesy of a pinpoint through ball from Pedri, before Lamine Yamal’s dipping free-kick crept through the Feyenoord wall.

Deadline-day signing Gabriel Jesus then rounded off the five-star display, nodding home his first goal for the club just two minutes after coming off the bench.

‘The mentality of this team is incredible’

The high-pressing style and seamless squad rotation drew special praise from Flick, who pointed to the relentless work ethic running through the squad.

“The mentality of this team is incredible,” Flick added. “We have controlled games and dominated possession at a very high level. We are training really hard and it is very demanding, but everyone has that hunger to improve and be better.

“For our philosophy, intensity is everything. When we lose the ball, the distances between our players are short, which allows us to counter-press immediately. What pleases me most is seeing everyone committed in both attack and defence.”

articles.title: Torres hits hat-trick as holders PSG make crushing start in Champions League
articles.summary: World Cup final hero is at it again
articles.content:
Torres hits hat-trick as holders PSG make crushing start in Champions League

World Cup final hero is at it again

Last Update:

World Cup winner Ferran Torres hit a clinical hat-trick as holders PSG smashed Slovan Bratislava 6-1 in their Champions League opener.

The Spain forward, who scored the winner in the final in the USA this summer, scored twice on his league debut for PSG last month and went one better in the Champions League.

Ousmane Dembele also scored twice with midfielder Fabian Ruiz adding a late sixth.

Elsewhere, Stuttgart beat newcomers Viking 3-1, and Sporting proved too strong for Galatasaray.

For Dembele, his double offered a welcome and timely return to form following a frustrating start to the domestic season. The reigning Ballon d’Or winner was taken off at halftime in PSG’s Ligue 1 opener against Rennes, left out against Lille, and proved ineffective off the bench in a 2-1 defeat to Monaco last Friday.

Against Slovan at the Parc des Princes, however, the Frenchman looked back to his electric best. He broke the deadlock in the 17th minute by reacting quickest to turn in the rebound after Nuno Mendes’ swerving shot hit the post, before heading home his second six minutes later from 18-year-old midfielder Dro Fernandez’s cross.

Dembélé also turned provider, setting up Torres for his first before floating in a corner for the summer signing to nod home his third in the 57th minute. Torres had earlier doubled his tally shortly after the break with a delightful touch and curled finish from the edge of the area, following a brilliant jinking run from Maghnes Akliouche.

Suleiman Camara grabbed a brief consolation for the visitors with a fine finish, but Slovan’s overwhelmed defence was repeatedly punished. A sloppy error gifted Ruiz possession late on to wrap up the scoring, capping a dominant night where Luis Enrique’s side racked up 35 shots and bounced back emphatically from a four-game winless streak.

Raphinha drives Barcelona into early Champions League lead

Barcelona's captain is in sensational form

Barcelona took just three minutes to fly into the lead of their Champions League opener at home to Dutch side Feyenoord.

Hansi Flick’s side have won all four games in La Liga so far and wasted no time in firing ahead in the driving rain at the still-to-be completed Nou Camp.

Much of the speculation through the summer surrounded Barca’s failure to recruit a number nine but Raphinha has wasted no time in making that shirt his own.

And it was soon 2-0.

Karim Adeyemi, in for England winger Anthony Gordon, was allowed to come inside from wide on the left and arrowed in a curler from 20 yards.
