articles.content:
Barcelona chief Laporta warns Real Madrid boss Mourinho not to overstep the mark in criticism of referees

Barcelona president Joan Laporta has no issue with Jose Mourinho criticising referees providing it does step into anti-Barcelona sentiment

Last Update:

Barcelona president Joan Laporta has warned Jose Mourinho not to overstep the mark following his criticism of referees after Real Madrid’s controversial defeat at Real Betis on Friday night.

Mourinho lashed out at match official Alejandro Hernandez Hernandez and VAR Javier Iglesias Villanueva after they dismissed Madrid’s claims that Kylian Mbappe’s late penalty should have been retaken due to encroachment by home defender Marc Bartra.

Although the officials were later proved to be correct, that did not stop Mourinho launching a tirade that implied Madrid were victimised and that other clubs – most notably Barcelona – were given preferential treatment.

Laporta, speaking before the traditional directors’ lunch that preceded tonight’s Champions League clash with Feyenoord, was asked about Mourinho’s complaints and said: “What has us very excited is Barça. What the other teams do [is up to them], as long as they do not cross the line of respect and institutional harmony that must be maintained.

“Other teams do what they deem appropriate. We respect it as long as there is obviously no transgression of what is normal in relations between clubs.”

La Liga 2026

Spain

Barcelona target Champions League – Laporta

Barca have had the upper hand over Madrid in recent years, winning the last two La Liga crowns while Madrid have had back-to-back trophyless seasons.

Laporta said there would be no easing up and admitted the Champions League – a trophy they have not won since 2015 – was a priority.

He added: “Our goal is to win our third league trophy in a row, which would be extraordinary. We aim to continue being the king of cups, which would also be very good. We aim to win the Super Cup in the middle of the season. And, of course, this year we want to win the Champions League. If you say the big goal, yes, I would say yes [it is the Champions League].”

Barcelona star Yamal is ‘spectacular’, says Laporta

It has been a good week for Barca with three players named on the 30-man shortlist for the 2026 Ballon d’Or, including new signing Rodri.

Pau Cubarsi is an outsider but Lamine Yamal is among the leading candidates to claim the prize after a stellar year for the Blaugrana and Spain.

“Barça is a unique club and proof of this is in these nominations. We are very proud,” Laporta said. The players we have must be grateful to Barcelona Football Club for what it gives them. I will be immensely happy if a Barça player wins.”

On Yamal, he added: “He’s spectacular. He has an exceptional quality, he is a genius and I think his nomination for the Ballon d’Or is more than deserved. He has a maturity for his age, [that’s] fantastic. I feel bad when you talk about the nominations that neither Pedri nor Raphinha are nominated. I think they have also made a case; for their quality they deserved to be nominated.”

articles.title: Vinicius Jr jeered again by Real Madrid fans but Jose Mourinho leaps to his defence
articles.summary: Vinicius Jr is still some way short of his best form but Real Madrid boss Jose Mourinho praised the Brazil winger for his hard work against Inter Milan last night
articles.content:
Vinicius Jr jeered again by Real Madrid fans but Jose Mourinho leaps to his defence

Vinicius Jr is still some way short of his best form but Real Madrid boss Jose Mourinho praised the Brazil winger for his hard work against Inter Milan last night

Last Update:

Jose Mourinho leapt to the defence of Vinicius Jr after the Real Madrid winger was again the subject of boos and whistles from frustrated supporters.

The Brazil international, who ended a lengthy contract stand-off by signing a new six-year deal last month, struggled to make an impact as Madrid edged out Inter Milan 2-1 in a wild Champions League encounter last night, first half goals from Kylian Mbappe and Federico Valverde proving enough despite Carlos Augusto’s reply.

Match Statistics

Vinicius Jr was eventually taken off with three minutes to go and the home fans were less than generous with their reception, but Mourinho insisted his best form would return.

“If he works for the team, he always has my support,” said Mourinho. “Does this mean that you have to be a starter in each game? Does he have to play for 90 minutes each game? No. But you will always have my respect and affection.

“And he has worked a lot for the team. Playing against a team that plays with its eyes closed, with three behind and that projects to the sides the way they do… it is very difficult for the wingers. His work and Brahim Diaz’s has been very good. Closing well on the inside and letting the full-backs press on the outside. He has done a very good job for the team.

“Obviously, in one of those actions where he had a one-on-one on the left wing, the Vini who is at full tilt kills games. He kills them, like he killed me last year here, with Benfica. Then we were 1-1, in a very close match. And he took a transition and ended the game. This is what we expect from him. But those who give everything, are not obliged to give more. He has no more to give. And he has given everything. When he gives everything, the coach is with him.”

Diplomatic Mourinho refuses to criticise Real Madrid fans

Vinicius Jr’s relationship with the Madrid crowd has deteriorated over the past 12 months but Mourinho refused to criticise supporters who vented their irritation last night.

He added: “I don’t criticise the fans, I don’t talk about the fans. I speak as a coach and about my relationship with him: he deserves all my respect. He’s not at his best, I see that, we all see it. But he’s the first one to know. He is working hard to be the Vinicius who decides game after game.

“But by not being at his best, at the moment, he is working more than ever… whether in training or in games. The few times he has not been able to get back and defend with the block, it was due to fatigue. Because he has made four, five, six sprints. And it’s not easy.

“I have a lot of respect for this Vinicius that I have found. And it will come… the time will come when he decides matches. And he wins them.”

Courtois saves Real Madrid

Madrid were somewhat fortunate to emerge with the three points with goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois having to pull off a series of brilliant saves to preserve their advantage.

“The summary is that it could have ended 5-1 or 6-1 for us or it could have finished 6-6,” Mourinho said. “I don’t want to say that Inter could have won the game, because we have created more and in crucial moments, such as the [possible] 3-0 in the last moment of the first half or Jude Bellingham’s at the beginning of the second.

“But, crazy game. A madness that I don’t like. I don’t like it. I like it much more to be able to score five, six or seven but having absolute control and not needing an absolutely incredible goalkeeper.

“And I can’t isolate my words from the context that we play against a great team. Great team. With a thousand options. They made changes and I couldn’t make the changes I wanted in the centre of the field.

“It was a very tough game, with three very important points. There are already three less to qualify. I am absolutely convinced that we are going to do it. But getting these three points the first time is important.”

Next up for Madrid is a home game with Rayo Vallecano on Saturday before two more league matches prior to the international break: at Elche and then the season’s first derby at home to Atletico on September 20.

Mourinho’s men are third in La Liga after four games.

articles.title: Carabao Cup: Wins for Newcastle, Palace, Sunderland and Bournemouth in third round
articles.summary: A host of Premier League sides secured victories in the Carabao Cup third round on Tuesday night. Crystal Palace beat Middlesbrough 3-0, as Bournemouth secured their first victory under Marco Rose by beating Lincoln City 4-0, with Newcastle and Sunderland both edging through with 1-0 wins. Read on for our summary of the action from […]
articles.content:
Carabao Cup: Wins for Newcastle, Palace, Sunderland and Bournemouth in third round

Last Update:

A host of Premier League sides secured victories in the Carabao Cup third round on Tuesday night.

Crystal Palace beat Middlesbrough 3-0, as Bournemouth secured their first victory under Marco Rose by beating Lincoln City 4-0, with Newcastle and Sunderland both edging through with 1-0 wins.

Read on for our summary of the action from all five games below.

Bournemouth 4–0 Lincoln City

Bournemouth produced the most emphatic win of the night, with Ryan Christie scoring a hat-trick as they dismantled Lincoln. Christie struck in the seventh, 69th and 88th minutes before Alex Scott’s stoppage-time goal made it four. It was Marco Rose’s first competitive win as Bournemouth boss and a very encouraging cup performance.

Crystal Palace 3–0 Middlesbrough

Palace took control through Jorgen Strand Larsen, who headed them in front before adding a second after half-time. Daichi Kamada then made it 3–0 in the 72nd minute to put the tie beyond doubt. A comfortable night for Palace against Championship opposition and a place in the last 16 secured.

Leyton Orient 1–3 Bradford City

Orient actually went ahead through an own goal, but Bradford turned the game around just before half-time when Ollie Sanderson levelled. Kyle Hudlin then put Bradford in front after the break, before Bobby Pointon added a late third to seal an impressive away victory.

Sunderland 1–0 Hull City

This was a much tighter affair, with neither side able to find a breakthrough for most of the night. Chemsdine Talbi finally settled it in the 71st minute, cleverly chipping Hull goalkeeper Dillon Phillips after being set up by Thomas Meunier. Hull pushed for an equaliser but Sunderland held on to reach the fourth round.

Millwall 0–1 Newcastle United

Newcastle survived a serious scare at The Den, with Millwall arguably creating the better chances for long periods and even hitting the post late on. Joe Willock finally broke the deadlock in the 81st minute, his effort taking a deflection after Lewis Hall’s work down the left. Millwall couldn’t find a response, so the holders scraped through 1–0 despite a far from convincing performance.

articles.title: Champions League: Dortmund and Betis win five-goal thrillers
articles.summary: Troy Parrott and Serhou Guirassy were the heroes
articles.content:
Champions League: Dortmund and Betis win five-goal thrillers

Troy Parrott and Serhou Guirassy were the heroes

Last Update:

The Champions League 2026-27 began in thrilling style with 21 goals across six games on the first part of Matchday 1 on Tuesday.

Borussia Dortmund and Real Betis both secured 3-2 wins over Villarreal and Lille, after Aston Villa also won by the same scoreline earlier in the night.

We have already covered Manchester City’s 2-0 win over Porto and Real Madrid’s 2-1 victory over Inter Milan too, but read on as we run you through the remainder of the action on Tuesday evening.

Borussia Dortmund 3-2 Villarreal

Serhou Guirassy’s brace in the final 10 minutes of the game earned Borussia Dortmund an entertaining win over Villarreal, with the striker also scoring an own goal in a crazy game.

Renato Veiga’s own goal gave BVB the lead in the first half, but Villarreal equalised in the 66th minute through Santiago Mourino, only for Guirassy to make himself the hero with his match-winning brace – the second of which came from the penalty spot.

Guirassy then turned the ball into his own net in bizarre fashion to give the Yellow Submarine late hope, but the Bundesliga outfit were able to hold on and grab the victory.

Lille 2-3 Real Betis

Troy Parrott was the hero once again for Real Betis as the Spanish side twice came from behind to win 3-2 in the Champions League.

Lille had twice gone in front through goals from Ayase Ueda and Alexsandro, but Marc Bartra levelled the game both times with headers before the hosts went down to 10 men when Ethan Mbappe was sent off.

Parrott then came up with another crucial moment, just as he did against Real Madrid at the weekend, drilling in from Isco’s ball to complete the Real Betis comeback and earn a huge victory in their first Champions League game since 2005-06.

AEK Athens 1-0 LASK

AEK Athens edged LASK 1–0 in the remaining Champions League game on Tuesday, with Razvan Marin producing the decisive moment in the 21st minute by curling a superb free-kick from outside the box into the top corner.

AEK largely controlled the game after going ahead, while Luka Jović had several chances and even found the net in the second half, only for his header to be ruled out for offside.

LASK pushed for an equaliser late on and came close in stoppage time, but AEK held firm to secure three valuable points on their return to the Champions League.

articles.title: Ballon d’Or: Full list of 30 nominees as Messi is included but Ronaldo snubbed
articles.summary: Lionel Messi will challenge the European elite to be named winner of the 2026 Ballon d'Or after being included on the 30-man shortlist
articles.content:
Ballon d’Or: Full list of 30 nominees as Messi is included but Ronaldo snubbed

Lionel Messi will challenge the European elite to be named winner of the 2026 Ballon d'Or after being included on the 30-man shortlist

Last Update:

Lionel Messi, Harry Kane, Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal are expected to fight it out for the 2026 Ballon d’Or after today being named on the list of 30 nominees for football’s biggest individual prize.

Messi returned to the shortlist for the first time in three years following his remarkable performances at the World Cup, where he guided Argentina to the final before losing to Spain.

The 39-year-old also had another brilliant year with Inter Miami in the United States, helping them win a maiden MLS Cup in December.

Messi has won the award eight times previously but it would be a major surprise if he were to add a ninth.

His long-time rival Cristiano Ronaldo, who has five Ballons d’Or to his name, was not included despite helping Al-Nassr to the title in Saudi Arabia.

Kane is favourite with the bookmakers after netting 61 times for Bayern Munich in all competitions as they clinched another league and cup double. The 33-year-old also scored six times as England finished third at the World Cup.

France captain Mbappe scored 42 goals in 44 games for Real Madrid last season, and added another 10 in the United States, Canada and Mexico over the summer. But Madrid’s failure to land any major silverware could hamper his chances.

Yamal lifted La Liga – he scored 16 times as the Catalans retained the trophy – and also played a key role as Spain backed up their 2024 European Championship success by winning the World Cup.

There are nine members of the team that helped PSG retain the Champions League, including 2025 winner Ousmane Dembele.

The full list of nominees for the men’s 2026 Ballon d’Or award

Jude Bellingham (Real Madrid)Pau Cubarsi (Barcelona)Marc Cucurella (Real Madrid)Ousmane Dembele (PSG)Luis Diaz (Bayern Munich)Bruno Fernandes (Manchester United)Erling Haaland (Manchester City)Gabriel (Arsenal)Harry Kane (Bayern Munich)Achraf Hakimi (PSG)Lamine Yamal (Barcelona)Khvicha Kvaratskhelia (PSG)Marquinhos (PSG)Sadio Mane (Al-Nassr)Lautaro Martinez (Inter Milan)Kylian Mbappe (Real Madrid)Nuno Mendes (PSG)Lionel Messi (Inter Miami)Michael Olise (Bayern Munich)Joao Neves (PSG)Willian Pacho (PSG)Julian Quinones (Al-Qadsiah)Declan Rice (Arsenal)Rodri (Barcelona)Fabian Ruiz (PSG)Ferran Torres (PSG)William Saliba (Arsenal)Dayor Upamecano (Bayern Munich)Vinicius Jr (Real Madrid)Vitinha (PSG)

How does the voting for the Ballon d’Or work?

The 30-player shortlist for the main awards is voted for by a panel of journalists from France Football and L’Equipe.

One journalist from each of the top 100 countries in the FIFA rankings then votes for their top 10 from each list with each position afforded a certain number of points.

Which players have won the award previously?

Men’s award:

2025: Ousmane Dembele2024: Rodri 2023: Lionel Messi2022: Karim Benzema 2021: Lionel Messi 2019: Lionel Messi

Women’s award:

2025: Aitana Bonmati2024: Aitana Bonmati 2023: Aitana Bonmati 2022: Alexia Putellas 2021: Alexia Putellas 2019: Megan Rapinoe

When will the award be handed out?

The ceremony will take place on Monday, October 26 in London.

articles.title: Alexis Mac Allister ‘very sad’ after Liverpool snub chance to offer him a new  contract
articles.summary: Alexis Mac Allister is willing to fight for his Liverpool future despite being overlooked for a new contract at Anfield
articles.content:
Alexis Mac Allister ‘very sad’ after Liverpool snub chance to offer him a new  contract

Alexis Mac Allister is willing to fight for his Liverpool future despite being overlooked for a new contract at Anfield

Last Update:

Alexis Mac Allister has outlined his disappointment at not being offered a new contract at Liverpool, describing the club’s reluctance to extend his stay at Anfield as “very sad”.

The Argentina midfielder’s current deal still has two years left to run and attempts by his agent to negotiate fresh terms this summer were rebuffed by the Merseyside club.

Mac Allister insisted, however, that he was still committed to Liverpool despite confirming he had offers from elsewhere.

He said: “I received the news that the club was not in a position to renew my contract, which of course makes me very sad.

“I think everyone can see I give 100% for this club, every single day in training, I have good games, bad games. I always give my best.

“I see Dominik [Szoboszlai] and Ryan [Gravenberch] renewing their contracts, which makes me happy. But at the same time it makes me sad I didn’t get mine.

“There is still time, I will give 100% until my last day. We will see what happens.

“There were options to leave this summer. Right now I’m in the right club.”

Asked if he knew why the club were not willing to give him a new deal, the 27-year-old added: “Not really, I did not have any direct conversations. They were with my agent.

“I don’t want to say things they never said, but they said they were not in the position to renew me.”

Mac Allister confident of strong season for Liverpool

Mac Allister joined Liverpool from Brighton in 2023 for a bargain £35million and played a key role in the club’s title success under Arne Slot in the 2024/25 season.

He struggled the following year, as did many of his team-mates, but is relishing life under Andoni Iraola and is hoping to help the club get off to a winning start in the Champions League on Wednesday night when Atletico Madrid visit Anfield.

“I am very confident about this season,” he said.

“We have a lot of quality, we have a very good coach that brought his ideas.

“I think we improved a lot since the beginning of the season, we have the desire to win trophies. We have experience, we have trophies, we have everything to be successful, but we need to be all together.

“You can have the best players, best ideas, but if we are not on the same page, it’s impossible.”

Working with new Liverpool boss Iraola excites Mac Allister

On former Bournemouth boss Iraola, he added: “He’s a really good coach, he knows what he wants to do and we are trying to get there.

“I haven’t had any conversations with him about it [the contract].

“I think this can be a successful year, that’s why I think this is the right club and the right moment to be here.”

articles.title: Liverpool boost revenue after striking record deal with Turkish Airlines
articles.summary: Liverpool's revenue will be enhanced by a new deal with Turkish Airlines
articles.content:
Liverpool boost revenue after striking record deal with Turkish Airlines

Liverpool's revenue will be enhanced by a new deal with Turkish Airlines

Last Update:

Liverpool will have a new front-of-shirt sponsor next season for the first time in 17 years after the club announced a bumper deal with Turkish Airlines.

The airline’s name and logo will adorn the Reds’ shirts for the next five years, replacing Standard Chartered, whose contract expires at the end of the current campaign.

The Athletic report the agreement with Turkish Airlines is worth in excess of £300million (£60m per season) with the club claiming it is the most lucrative front-of-shirt contract in the history of the Premier League.

Ben Latty, chief commercial officer at LFC, told the club’s official website: “This is a milestone announcement for us and we are delighted to welcome Turkish Airlines as our main club partner from June 2027.

“The front of the Liverpool shirt holds a special place in the history of our club. Turkish Airlines is a globally recognised organisation with an extensive international network, and we look forward to beginning our partnership and building a strong relationship together, with already strong foundations built from those special memories back in 2005.

“This announcement also provides an opportunity to recognise the extraordinary contribution Standard Chartered has made to Liverpool FC over the past 17 years.

“They have been an important part of our journey through an exceptional period in the club’s history, and we are delighted that Standard Chartered will remain part of the Liverpool FC family as a global partner from June 2027.

“As we prepare for this transition, we look forward to this new season and welcoming Turkish Airlines as our main club partner from June 2027.”

Liverpool rarely change front-of-shirt sponsors

Turkish Airlines will become just the sixth company to have their name on the front of Liverpool’s shirts since sponsorship was introduced in the late 1970s, following on from Hitachi (1979-1982), Crown Paints (1982-1988), Candy (1988-1992), Carlsberg (1992-2010) and Standard Chartered (2010-2027) .

Ahmet Olmustur, Turkish Airlines CEO, said: “Liverpool Football Club is one of the world’s most recognised and respected football clubs, with an exceptional heritage and a truly global community of supporters.

“We are very pleased that Turkish Airlines will become the club’s main club partner and that our name will take its place on one of the most iconic shirts in world sport.”

articles.summary: O'Reilly was injured in the warm-up at the weekend. Doku has not played in the league this season.
articles.content:
Man City: Maresca provides optimistic updates on O’Reilly and Doku with derby on horizon

O'Reilly was injured in the warm-up at the weekend. Doku has not played in the league this season.

Last Update:

Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca expects Nico O’Reilly to be fit for the Manchester derby but is unsure if Jeremy Doku will be able to feature.

Maresca’s side open their Champions League campaign at Porto on Tuesday, before making the shorter journey to Old Trafford on Sunday for their first under derby under the guidance of the Italian.

City made it three wins from three in the Premier League last Saturday with a 1-0 home win over newly promoted Coventry City.

O’Reilly did not feature in that game after sustaining an injury in the warm-up. Winger Doku, meanwhile, has not played since the 3-0 defeat to Arsenal in the Community Shield with a calf problem.

Maresca optimistic over City pair

Both players will miss the game at Estadio do Dragao, however, at least one of them should be available for the derby.

Asked about their availability for the clash with Michael Carrick’s men in a pre-match press conference, Maresca said: “Nico probably yes, Jeremy we’re not sure yet, we need to wait.

“Jeremy got injured in the Community Shield. That’s three weeks ago.

“But he’s back, I don’t know if available for the weekend but slowly, slowly he’s coming back.”

Maresca was given an extremely difficult to act to follow succeeding Pep Guardiola.

This week will provide an indication of City’s progress under the former Chelsea boss since that disappointing Community Shield display as they face a pair of challenging away games in two different competitions.

But right-back Matheus Nunes has been impressed with Maresca’s impact to this point.

“He has brought so much energy, there feels like a new energy around,” Nunes said. “He has very good energy. He sets the standard.”

Asked to compare Maresca to Guardiola, Nunes said: “I was with Pep for three seasons and Enzo just a couple of months.

“Maybe in a few months I can answer that question. They are both very passionate so I see more comparisons than differences.”

articles.summary: He will not make his first appearance until October at the earliest.
articles.content:
Goretzka’s Villa debut delayed until after international break

He will not make his first appearance until October at the earliest.

Last Update:

Aston Villa midfielder Leon Goretzka has been ruled out until after the international break.

Goretzka joined Villa last month following the expiration of his contract at Bayern Munich.

It had been hoped that the Germany international, who has not played since Die Mannschaft’s exit from the World Cup at the hands of Paraguay in the round of 32, could be involved in Villa’s season immediately having signed four days after their opening 4-0 loss to Brighton and Hove Albion.

But the 31-year-old has yet to build his fitness back up and, after a setback, will now have to wait until October to make his Villa bow.

Gortezka wrote on Instagram: “Dear Villans. First of all, thank you for the incredible welcome. After my first few days at this club, the feeling that I’m exactly where I’m meant to be has grown stronger with each passing day.

“Unfortunately, my body has reacted to the increased workload after my time away from the pitch. It’s frustrating, but I need this short break now to come back at full strength.

“I’ll use the coming days, including the international break, to recover fully and I’ll be back ready to fight and give everything for you and for Villa. Can’t wait to see you on the pitch soon! Thank you for your support, Leon.”

Goretzka made to wait for debut

Villa are winless through their first three Premier League games after following up the loss at Brighton with a 1-0 home defeat to Arsenal and a 0-0 draw at newly promoted Hull City.

They visit Club Brugge in the Champions League on Tuesday before welcoming Nottingham Forest to Villa Park.

After an EFL Cup clash with Coventry City, their final game before the break sees Villa visit Tottenham.

Goretzka could then make his debut against Brentford on October 10.

articles.title: Belgian FA still seeking answers over Balogun World Cup incident
articles.summary: The Belgian FA are still seeking clarity on why Folarin Balogun's red card was overturned in World Cup.
articles.content:
Belgian FA still seeking answers over Balogun World Cup incident

The Belgian FA are still seeking clarity on why Folarin Balogun's red card was overturned in World Cup.

Last Update:

Belgium’s Football Association has called for FIFA to explain why Folarin Balogun was allowed to play against them at the 2026 World Cup and wants the issue discussed at the next FIFA Council meeting.

Balogun was controversially cleared to feature for the United States in their last-16 meeting with Belgium after his one-match suspension for a straight red card was suspended for a year by FIFA.

The decision attracted widespread criticism, particularly after it emerged that US President Donald Trump and White House officials had lobbied FIFA over the situation.

UEFA and the Royal Belgian Football Association (RBFA) were among those to question the decision, with Belgium now demanding greater clarity over how the case was handled.

Balogun had scored three goals at the tournament before his red card and was named in the starting XI against Belgium after FIFA suspended his ban.

The United States ultimately lost the match 4-1, with Belgium progressing to the quarter-finals before being eliminated by Spain.

The RBFA had previously asked FIFA for “a clear justification of the decisions taken and details on how such situations will be handled in the future”.

Two months on from the incident, the Belgian association says it is still waiting for a satisfactory response.

RBFA president Pascale van Damme said: “Two months after the events, our questions remain unanswered.

“Given the importance of transparency and clarity for all parties involved, we request the necessary explanations and, at the same time, wish to explore where improvements to the current processes are possible, so that similar cases can be handled in a clear, consistent and efficient manner in the future.

“Together with Uefa, the other confederations and the national associations, we remain committed to transparency in decision-making, strong governance and clear processes. We remain open to constructive cooperation, in the interest of the trust, integrity and future of football.”

articles.title: Kane hungry for Ballon d’Or after ‘best season so far’
articles.summary: Harry Kane is looking to win the Ballon d'Or for the first time this year.
articles.content:
Kane hungry for Ballon d’Or after ‘best season so far’

Harry Kane is looking to win the Ballon d'Or for the first time this year.

Last Update:

Harry Kane says he is “extremely proud” of his goalscoring record last season and is delighted to be in contention for the Ballon d’Or.

The Bayern Munich striker scored 73 goals for club and country during the 2025-26 campaign, a tally bettered only by Lionel Messi’s 82 in 2011-12.

Kane is currently the bookmakers’ favourite to win the award in October and would become only the fifth Englishman to claim the prize if he is successful.

Kane proud of record-breaking season

Kane described last season as the best of his career after scoring 73 times for Bayern and England.

“Of course, I’m extremely proud of the season I put up, for sure,” Kane told TNT Sports’ Owen Hargreaves.

“Not that long ago, I was that fan wanting to become a professional footballer and I am here now and winning awards and the Ballon d’Or is the same.

“Of course, now it is out of my hands, it is down to the voters and the people who decide it. The season I had was my best season by far and we’ll have to wait and see.”

Kane’s tally saw him surpass Cristiano Ronaldo’s previous record of 69 goals in a season, while only Messi has scored more in a single campaign during the modern era.

Kane embraces Ballon d’Or debate

Despite being among the leading candidates for the Ballon d’Or, Kane knows the final decision is out of his hands.

He believes the debate surrounding the award is part of what makes football so interesting, with different players valued for different qualities.

“It is a weird one because I am already focused on this season now and the next season. Can I be better? Can I improve? But I also want to appreciate what I did,” he said.

“The thing with football opinions – there are so many opinions, so many arguments for different players and people love this player because he’s fast and he’s got great IQ and his finishing is great.

“So I think that is what makes football special, all those debates, and the Ballon d’Or is definitely one of them. I’m happy that I am in contention.”

articles.title: ‘It wouldn’t be stolen’ – Mbappe makes emphatic case for his Ballon d’Or candidacy despite lack of trophies
articles.summary: Mbappe believes his goalscoring form for Madrid and France merits the award.
articles.content:
‘It wouldn’t be stolen’ – Mbappe makes emphatic case for his Ballon d’Or candidacy despite lack of trophies

Mbappe believes his goalscoring form for Madrid and France merits the award.

Last Update:

Kylian Mbappe is convinced he has a strong case for the Ballon d’Or this year despite his lack of silverware with Real Madrid and France.

Football’s most prestigious individual prize is an honour that has escaped Mbappe to this point in his illustrious career.

Mbappe finished third in the voting in 2023 when Lionel Messi won for the eighth time, with that year marking the only one in which he has featured in the top three.

Bayern Munich and England talisman Harry Kane is the bookmakers’ favourite for the award, with Lamine Yamal also seemingly ahead of Mbappe following Spain’s triumph at the World Cup.

Mbappe backs himself for Ballon d’Or

Mbappe endured disappointment this summer as France lost to Spain in the semi-finals, with that unsuccessful campaign following a second season with Real Madrid in which Los Blancos went without a trophy.

Individually, however, Mbappe enjoyed an extremely prolific 2025-26 season, scoring 42 goals in 44 games for Madrid. He then scored 10 at the World Cup to become the tournament’s all-time top scorer with 22, and has already found the net four times for Madrid this term.

And he believes those feats should trump his fortunes in terms of team silverware when it comes to the Ballon d’Or voting.

“I would vote for myself to win the Ballon d’Or,” Mbappe told L’Equipe.

“I’m convinced that I can win it this year, so I haven’t taken any distance from it.

“Of course. I see it as an individual award. People look at what the player has contributed individually.

“Then some say I haven’t won titles, but I haven’t seen a Ballon d’Or awarded unanimously that meets all the conditions every time.

“Has it ever been awarded with 100 per cent of the votes? That means there’s always someone who thinks the winner doesn’t deserve it. From that point, I’m not saying I’ll win it unanimously.

“But I believe I have the arguments: to be the all-time top scorer in the World Cup, and to surpass all the legends of the sport in the most important tournament this sport has ever created.

“That’s something that sticks in people’s minds, it’s a global event. To finish as the top scorer in the most important competition where the world’s best players participate is a big deal.

“I don’t know if that’s ever been achieved before, but the principle says that making history should always be rewarded.

“I’d vote for myself. But I can understand those who vote for someone else. We’re not in a dictatorship of thought.

“But when I look at the arguments, and when I look at the competition, I look at myself and say: Yes… it wouldn’t be stolen.”

When is the 2026 Ballon d’Or ceremony?

The 2026 Ballon d’Or winner will be named on October 26.

In a departure from tradition, the ceremony will be held in London, rather than in Paris.

The award is based on performance for the 2025-26 season, rather than the calendar year. It covers the period from August 1, 2025 to July 31, 2026, with the exploits of players for their clubs and at the World Cup taken into account.

Mbappe’s France team-mate Ousmane Dembele won the award in 2025, emerging victorious ahead of Yamal and Paris Saint-Germain midfielder Vitinha after PSG won the Champions League for the first time in 2024-25, a title they successfully defended last season.

As Mbappe’s former club again tasted European success, Madrid exited the Champions League at the quarter-final stage. They finished eight points behind Barcelona in LaLiga and went out of the Copa del Rey in the round of 16 at the hands of second-tier Albacete.

Despite those disappointments, Mbappe is still firmly in the running to receive the prize for the first time, with PSG star Kvicha Kvaratskhelia and Spain’s World Cup Golden Ball winner Rodri also considered among the favourites. Barcelona midfielder Rodri won in 2024 during his time with Manchester City.

articles.content:
Champions League Predictions: Delight for Manchester clubs and Arsenal but frustration for Villa and Liverpool

The Champions League is BACK! Here are the pick of the matchweek one ties and our predictions...

Last Update:

The Champions League returns this week and there are some mouthwatering ties to get the competition up and running.

All 36 teams are in action with the fixtures unusually taking place across three nights.

Here, we take a look at the five British clubs and also the European elite as they get their campaigns underway.

UEFA Champions League

– League Stage – 1

Tuesday 8, September 2026

Wednesday 9, September 2026

Thursday 10, September 2026

TUESDAY, SEPTEMBER 8

Club Brugge v Aston Villa (5.45pm)It has been a difficult few months for Aston Villa following their Europa League triumph last season. Unai Emery’s squad has been decimated with the likes of Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans, Ezri Konsa and Emiliano Martinez all moving on. Villa have replaced them but it will inevitably take time for the newboys to gel and their Premier League performances have, so far, looked disjointed. Club Brugge have won four of five in the Belgian First Division and will see this as an opportunity. The teams met in the Champions League two seasons ago with Club Brugge winning a league phase clash at home before Villa won home and away in the round of 16.Prediction: Club Brugge 2-1 Aston Villa

Porto v Manchester City (8pm)Enzo Maresca has made an impressive start at Manchester City with three wins from three in the Premier League. A revamped squad appears to be taking shape and they will head to Portugal in confident mood. The same can be said for Porto, though, with Francesco Farioli’s side winning all five domestic contests so far. The home side have won just two of their last 16 matches against Premier League clubs and the financial might of the English clubs will probably be on display once again at the Dragao.Prediction: Porto 1-2 Manchester City

Real Madrid v Inter Milan (8pm)Two of Europe’s biggest clubs clash in what is likely to be an emotional night for Jose Mourinho. The Real Madrid boss led Inter to Champions League glory in 2010 before taking over at the Santiago Bernabeu for the first time. He is now back at the Spanish giants and in need of a win after Friday’s controversial defeat at Real Betis. Mourinho has made a largely positive start to his second spell but successive defeats would prompt the usual tongue wagging. Inter are not the same force they were 16 years ago but have made a strong start domestically, winning their first three Serie A fixtures. Keeping the likes of Kylian Mbappe, Jude Bellingham and Vinicius Jr quiet is a much greater task, though.Prediction: Real Madrid 2-0 Inter Milan

WEDNESDAY, SEPTEMBER 9

Barcelona v Feyenoord (5.45pm)Barcelona continue to march on with four successive wins to open the new La Liga season. They have scored five goals in three of those four games and already have the advantage over likely title rivals Real Madrid. The signing of Rodri has improved an already formidable squad and they will take some stopping both domestically and in Europe. Feyenoord are unbeaten in the Eredivisie but this is an altogether different challenge. Expect Barca to win and win well.Prediction: Barcelona 4-0 Feyenoord

Liverpool v Atletico Madrid (8pm)Liverpool enjoyed their first victory of the season at Ipswich on Friday night but there are still question marks around Andoni Iraola’s side, particularly in midfield. The main takeaway from the triumph at Portman Road was the return to form of Alexander Isak and the Sweden international will be key to their chances of beating Atletico. The Rojiblancos are a different beast to previous iterations under Diego Simeone who is tasked with maintaining their free-scoring form of last season while also tightening up at the back.Prediction: Liverpool 1-1 Atletico Madrid

Napoli v Arsenal (8pm)Arsenal flexed their muscles once again against Chelsea on Sunday, overpowering Xabi Alonso’s side with a 2-1 win that was more emphatic than the scoreline suggested. The English champions have a 100% record after three games and already look a good bet to repeat their title win of last season. Napoli have limped out of the gate in comparison and their 3-2 defeat at Inter at the weekend was their second in succession. Having also lost to Como, Max Allegri’s side have shown a vulnerability against good sides and Arsenal should have the quality to take advantage.Prediction: Napoli 0-3 Arsenal

PSG v Slovan Bratislava (8pm)It’s definitely not a crisis at PSG but a run of four domestic games without a win is a huge surprise given their superiority in recent seasons. Luis Enrique’s side have won this tournament in each of the last two years and they will undoubtedly challenge again this term. If they could handpick an opponent to get back to winning ways, it could well be Slovan Bratislava. This could be a very long night for the Slovakians.Prediction: PSG 5-0 Slovan Bratislava

THURSDAY, SEPTEMBER 10

Manchester United v Sabah (8pm)Sabah have come through four knockout ties to reach the league phase and were rewarded with a dream trip to Old Trafford to face a Manchester United side back in the Champions League for the first time since December 2023. United will be eager to get off to a wining start and banish the frustration of conceding an injury-time equaliser at Everton on Sunday. Michael Carrick’s side continue to show progress but still lack the quality to stage a genuine title challenge.Prediction: Manchester United 4-0 Sabah

articles.title: Angry Real Madrid boss Mourinho lashes out at integrity of VAR as backlash to Betis defeat continues
articles.summary: Jose Mourinho has claimed Real Madrid were hard done to against Real Betis - and questioned the integrity of the VAR after a late penalty was not re-taken
articles.content:
Angry Real Madrid boss Mourinho lashes out at integrity of VAR as backlash to Betis defeat continues

Jose Mourinho has claimed Real Madrid were hard done to against Real Betis - and questioned the integrity of the VAR after a late penalty was not re-taken

Last Update:

Real Madrid boss Jose Mourinho could find himself in hot water after questioning the integrity of the video assistant referee during Friday night’s shock defeat at Real Betis.

Madrid suffered their first loss of the season in Seville with Troy Parrott scoring the only goal with nine minutes to go.

The visitors had an excellent chance to equalise in stoppage time when Vinicius Jr went down theatrically under a challenge from Natan and referee Alejandro Hernandez Hernandez pointed to the spot. Kylian Mbappe took responsibility but saw his effort saved by Álvaro Valles.

The controversy came when Betis defender Marc Bartra got to the rebound ahead of Mbappe despite having one leg inside the area, albeit in the air. IFAB guidance suggests if his other leg was outside the area, and touching the ground, then it is okay and the VAR Javier Iglesias Villanueva rightly opted not to intervene.

Mourinho was incensed and used part of his pre-match press conference ahead of tomorrow night’s Champions League clash with Inter Milan to express his unhappiness.

He said: “We lost to Betis because we didn’t convert our attacking opportunities into goals. But the penalty… Why wasn’t it retaken?

“Well, because the VAR doesn’t know the rules… or because they didn’t want to. This is a question I’d like the people in charge to answer. Why?

“If VAR didn’t order it to be retaken because they didn’t know the rules, they should just go home and leave it at that. If they didn’t order it to be retaken because they didn’t want to, that’s even worse.

“And then there’s another, even worse question: if they didn’t know the rules, why didn’t they call the referee over to review it on the monitor? A bit strange.”

What do IFAB rules state?

If a player is airborne when a restart is taken (e.g. at a penalty kick), their position is now determined by the projected position of their feet if they were touching the ground. ‘Airborne’ only applies when the whole of the body is off the ground.

In other cases, a player’s position at a restart is determined by the position of their feet or any part of their body which is touching the ground (except as outlined in Law 11 – Offside).

Mourinho insistent Madrid were robbed

Although Bartra seemingly did nothing wrong, Mourinho believes the officiating team committed an error.

He added: “I want to assume honesty and think that he didn’t know he was in the penalty area. I prefer to go down that road. But if that’s the case, the referee can’t do it, VAR has to. Because in a few weeks or months, if something similar happens, it will be retaken.

“And I want to make it clear that we didn’t lose because of this, because we could have even missed the retake.

“But as the Real Madrid coach and as a player, I’d like to know why the message wasn’t repeated. I’d like people to answer me responsibly.”

Mourinho was also baffled by the fact Vinicius Jr was shown a yellow card for approaching the referee when he, as captain, is permitted to do so.

He said: “The other thing about this match, which is unrelated, is why the Real Madrid captain received a yellow card.

“When Vinicius approached the referee and saw the card before he even reached him, I’d like to know why. Why are we always told that the captain has the right to politely approach the referee to ask for an explanation.”

The defeat meant Madrid ended the weekend in third place on nine points, three behind Barca.

articles.title: The Sack Race: Arbeloa and De Zerbi tipped to leave Fulham and Tottenham
articles.summary: Fulham and Tottenham have had difficult starts to the new Premier League season, leading to speculation they could leave their posts
articles.content:
The Sack Race: Arbeloa and De Zerbi tipped to leave Fulham and Tottenham

Fulham and Tottenham have had difficult starts to the new Premier League season, leading to speculation they could leave their posts

Last Update:

Alvaro Arbeloa and Roberto De Zerbi have emerged as the early favourites to be the first manager to leave their post in the Premier League this season.

Fulham boss Arbeloa saw his odds cut to 9/4 following the home defeat by Crystal Palace at the weekend while online rumours suggest all is not well off the field at Craven Cottage.

The West London club have yet to register a point this season after also losing to Chelsea and Sunderland in the Premier League.

Arbeloa only joined Fulham over the summer after a largely miserable spell at Real Madrid which resulted in the Spanish giants finishing second behind arch-rivals Barcelona amid dressing room discontent that culminated in a ruck between Aurelien Tchouameni and Federico Valverde.

De Zerbi also under pressure at Tottenham

De Zerbi is undoubtedly on more solid ground having led Tottenham to Premier League survival last season. However, a slow start to the new campaign means he is 4/1 to leave first.

Spurs spent heavily during the transfer window on the likes of Sandro Tonali, Savio and Mateus Fernandes but the results have not yet followed with the weekend draw at Nottingham Forest seeing them pick up a first point.

And while De Zerbi is unlikely to face the sack, the volatile Italian does have a reputation for falling out with directors with disagreements bringing an end to his spells at both Brighton and Marseille.

Aston Villa had a difficult window and had to lose several key players. They are also stuck on one point from three games, heaping the pressure on Unai Emery but the Spaniard is well regarded at Villa Park.

Spokesperson for William Hill, Lee Phelps said: “There’s been a shake up in the sack race betting, with Alvaro Arbeloa and Roberto De Zerbi favoured to leave their posts first following poor results for Fulham and Tottenham.

“Fulham remain pointless following their defeat to Crystal Palace, seeing Arbeloa cut to 9/4 favourite to leave first, whilst De Zerbi has also seen his odds narrow to 4/1, with Spurs only picking up a point in their first three games.

articles.title: Goalkeeper scores twice in Dutch top flight to rescue point
articles.summary: The second goal came in the 101st minute of the match.
articles.content:
Goalkeeper scores twice in Dutch top flight to rescue point

The second goal came in the 101st minute of the match.

Last Update:

Goalkeeper Ronald Koeman Jr, the son of the former Netherlands defender and head coach Ronald Koeman, scored two goals for Eredivisie side Telstar to rescue a point in their league match against Cambuur.

Koeman Jr netted twice from the penalty spot to earn a 2-2 draw with the second spot-kick coming in the 11th minute of second-half stoppage time.

The 31-year-old keeper is not a stranger complete stranger at finding the back of the net, having scored a penalty previously, when he converted the winner against FC Volendam to confirm Telstar’s safety from relegation back in may.

In the clash on Sunday, Telstar had a player sent off in the 22nd minute and conceded two second-half goals to trail bottom side Cambuur with less than half an hour to play.

However, the hosts were awarded two spot-kicks – in the 63rd and 101st minute – and Koeman duly converted to become the first keeper to score twice in an Eredivisie game.

Famous father

Koeman Jr’s father, Ronald, was also known for his goalscoring exploits despite being utilised predominantly as a defender.

He played for clubs including PSV, Ajax and Barcelona, and was part of the Netherlands side that lifted the 1988 European Championship – to date the only major senior competition the men’s national team have won.

As a manager, Koeman was Netherlands head coach from 2023 to 2026, stepping down after the country’s last-32 exit at the hands of Morocco at this summer’s World Cup.

articles.title: Arteta: Arsenal a ‘joy to watch’ in derby victory over Chelsea
articles.summary: The Gunners maintained their winning start to the season.
articles.content:
Arteta: Arsenal a ‘joy to watch’ in derby victory over Chelsea

The Gunners maintained their winning start to the season.

Last Update:

Mikel Arteta admitted it was “an absolute joy” to watch his Arsenal team come from behind to beat London rivals Chelsea to maintain their winning start to the defence of their Premier League title.

Kai Havertz and Martin Odegaard scored the goals in a 2-1 win after Arteta’s side had fallen behind after just 77 seconds, courtesy of a strike from a summer target of Arsenal, Morgan Rogers.

In a pulsating clash at the Emirates that lived up to the pre-match billing, the Gunners saw off the challenge of a Blues team who, under new boss Xabi Alonso, have themselves enjoyed a positive start to the campaign.

Arteta thrilled with performance

Speaking to Sky Sports after the match, a jubilant Arteta hailed the performance of his team, despite the early set-back.

“I was very disappointed with the way we conceded the first goal. Bu as well, credit to them [Chelsea] and the finish that Morgan [Rogers] had,” the Gunners’ boss said.

“But the way we reacted, the way we played was a fascinating game. From start to finish, it was an absolute joy to watch our team play and compete. The composure, the personality, the threat that we generated – some huge individual performances as well.

“The atmosphere inside the stadium is something great to witness.”

The result means the champions are level on points with rivals Manchester City – the only two sides with 100% records in the top flight.

Next up for Arteta’s men is a midweek trip to Naples to face Napoli in their Champions League opener before facing Sunderland at the Stadium of Light on Saturday.

articles.title: Sesko pleased to grab first Manchester United goal but disappointed with collapse at Everton
articles.summary: Benjamin Sesko has reflected on Manchester United's draw with Everton.
articles.content:
Sesko pleased to grab first Manchester United goal but disappointed with collapse at Everton

Benjamin Sesko has reflected on Manchester United's draw with Everton.

Last Update:

Benjamin Sesko scored his first goal of the season for Manchester United but was left frustrated after Ainsley Maitland-Niles’ late strike secured a 2-2 draw at Everton on Sunday.

The Slovenian striker came off the bench at the Hill Dickinson Stadium and looked to have repeated his impact from last season, when he regularly made a difference after being introduced as a substitute.

However, Maitland-Niles’ spectacular effort in the final minute denied United all three points and left Sesko disappointed despite his own contribution.

The 23-year-old had missed much of pre-season through injury and has been eased back into action in recent weeks, making substitute appearances against Hull City and Ipswich Town.

He needed less than 20 minutes to make his mark against Everton.

Sesko makes instant impact

Sesko was introduced from the bench and quickly gave United the lead with a powerful header from Luke Shaw’s cross.

The effort proved too strong for Everton goalkeeper Jordan Pickford and appeared to have put United on course for a valuable away win.

Instead, Maitland-Niles produced a stunning late strike to earn Everton a point and leave Sesko and his teammates frustrated.

Speaking to MUTV after the match, Sesko admitted that the late equaliser was particularly difficult to accept given how close United had come to securing victory.

“We’re very disappointed of course because we were very close [to winning] and yet so far,” he said.

“To concede a goal like that in the last minute, it’s painful for everyone because everyone was giving everything to try and win the game.

“Every single person here wants that. In the moments like this where a last shot decides it, it’s very painful.”

Sesko happy to be back

Despite the disappointment of the result, Sesko was pleased to find the net and continue his return to full fitness.

The striker said scoring remains one of the best feelings for him, particularly when he can contribute directly to United’s results.

“For me, it’s the best feeling when I’m scoring, especially for the club like that,” Sesko said.

“When I can provide the goals and the points for the team – it’s my job at the end of the day. It’s nice to be back with the team to experience all the games again.

“Of course I wish today that we had won, but we can’t change that.”

articles.title: Watch: Rogers gives Chelsea early lead before Havertz levels for Arsenal
articles.summary: It was a pulsating start to the game at the Emirates.
articles.content:
Watch: Rogers gives Chelsea early lead before Havertz levels for Arsenal

It was a pulsating start to the game at the Emirates.

Last Update:

Morgan Rogers continued his fine start to life in a Chelsea shirt by volleying the Blues in front against Premier League champions Arsenal inside the opening two minutes of a pulsating tie at the Emirates.

Rogers, who became the most expensive British player ever when he signed from Aston Villa for £177m, swept home after just 77 seconds to give Xabi Alonso’s side the early advantage in the heavyweight derby clash.

In what was being billed as one the big early clashes of the top flight season quickly lived up to the excitement in front of an electric crowd in north London.

The goal was the first the Gunners have conceded in the league this season, as Mikel Arteta’s men look to defend the club’s first top-flight title in 22 years.

Riccardo Calafiori thought he had equalised for the hosts inside a quarter of an hour, however, the goal was ruled out after Ezri Konsa – making his first Arsenal start – was adjudged to have been in an offside position.

But just over 10 minutes later, the Gunners did draw level when Kai Havertz rifled an effort past Emi Martinez, much to the visible delight of Arteta.

Chelsea, up to that point had looked dangerous, as they aim to continue their fine start to the campaign, having won their opening two league matches.

articles.title: FIFA confirm Infantino set to stand for re-election
articles.summary: Gianni Infantino will stand for re-election as FIFA President.
articles.content:
FIFA confirm Infantino set to stand for re-election

Gianni Infantino will stand for re-election as FIFA President.

Last Update:

Gianni Infantino will stand for re-election as FIFA president in March 2027, despite growing opposition to his leadership from European football.

Infantino has held the position since 2016 and had been expected to secure another term without a serious challenge.

However, his position has come under greater scrutiny following his controversial plan to sell stakes in FIFA competitions to private investment firms.

The proposal was eventually scrapped after sparking widespread criticism, with UEFA even threatening to boycott FIFA competitions, including the World Cup.

FIFA has now confirmed that Infantino intends to seek another term, which would keep him in charge of world football until 2031 if he is successful.

“The Fifa president announced in April that he will stand for re-election in 2027,” a Fifa statement said.

“Of course, nothing has changed. Mr Infantino will be standing for re-election.”

Infantino refused to answer questions about his future when approached by reporters at the Women’s Under-20 World Cup in Poland on Saturday.

articles.summary: The 39-year-old spent last season playing in Serie A
articles.content:
Jamie Vardy joins Burnley on short-term deal

The 39-year-old spent last season playing in Serie A

Last Update:

Former Leicester City and England strike Jamie Vardy has joined Burnley until the end of the season.

The 39-year-old signs for the Clarets having spent last term in Italy with Cremonese, who were relegated from Serie A last season.

Vardy, who netted 200 times for Leicester during a 13-year spell at the club and was part of the Premier League-winning side of 2016, arrives at Turf Moor with Burnley currently rooted to the bottom of the Championship following relegation from the top-flight last term.

Vardy experience ‘invaluable’

Burnley head coach Nicky Hayen described Vardy’s experience as invaluable, saying: “We are delighted to welcome Jamie to Burnley FC. His experience and leadership will be invaluable to our squad, and we believe he can make a significant impact on our campaign.

“Jamie has a proven track record, and we are looking forward to seeing him in a Claret shirt.”

On returning to England, Vardy said: “I’m really happy to now be here at Burnley FC.

“This club has a proper footballing history and passionate fans who deserve a team that represents them and their town.

“I can’t wait to get going on the pitch and help the team move in the right direction.”

Burnley fell to a 2-1 defeat to Bristol City yesterday, a result that extends their winless run in the second tier to five matches.

articles.title: Messi bags two assists for Inter Miami in first match after Argentina retirement
articles.summary: Lionel Messi was up to his usual antics for Inter Miami after retiring from international football.
articles.content:
Messi bags two assists for Inter Miami in first match after Argentina retirement

Lionel Messi was up to his usual antics for Inter Miami after retiring from international football.

Last Update:

Lionel Messi marked his first appearance since retiring from international football with two assists as Inter Miami were held to a 2-2 draw by Atlanta United in MLS.

The 39-year-old announced last week that he had brought his Argentina career to an end, but returned to club action on Saturday night and immediately made his influence felt.

Messi provided the deliveries for goals from Casemiro and Luis Suarez, although Inter Miami were denied all three points after Breel Embolo converted a late penalty for Atlanta.

Messi creates two goals on Inter Miami return

Casemiro opened the scoring in the 32nd minute when he headed home a corner from Messi.

Atlanta responded just two minutes later through Miguel Almiron, setting up an entertaining contest at Miami’s Nu Stadium.

Messi then produced another moment of quality shortly before half-time, lofting a pass towards Telasco Segovia.

Segovia turned the ball into the path of Suarez, who made no mistake from the centre of the box to score his 12th MLS goal of the season.

The result looked set to give Inter Miami another important three points, but Atlanta were awarded a penalty with three minutes of normal time remaining.

Embolo stepped up and converted from the spot in the 87th minute before Atlanta survived a late barrage of chances from the hosts to claim a point.

The draw leaves Inter Miami with ground to make up on Nashville at the top of the Eastern Conference, although they still have 11 regular-season matches remaining.

Emotional Messi return after Argentina retirement

Messi’s return to club football came just days after he confirmed that his time with Argentina was over.

The Inter Miami forward ended his international career as Argentina’s record appearance maker and goalscorer after helping the country win the 2022 World Cup and 2021 Copa America.

There was a special atmosphere around Saturday’s match, with heavy rain causing a delay of more than an hour before the players were able to begin their warm-ups.

Supporters cheered both sets of players when they emerged, but the loudest reception was reserved for Messi as he walked out of the tunnel.

Rodrigo De Paul, who played alongside Messi for Argentina, spoke about the significance of seeing his former international teammate back on the pitch.

“Very emotional,” De Paul said in Spanish during a pre-match interview with Apple TV.

“We lived with so much excitement having him out there on the field. It brought us so much joy to see the Argentina jersey all over the world, and it always had a No. 10 on the back.”

articles.title: De Zerbi claims Tottenham need time to gel after another winless outing
articles.summary: Roberto De Zerbi has had his say on Tottenham's 0-0 draw with Nottingham Forest.
articles.content:
De Zerbi claims Tottenham need time to gel after another winless outing

Roberto De Zerbi has had his say on Tottenham's 0-0 draw with Nottingham Forest.

Last Update:

Tottenham have gone three league games without scoring to start a season for the first time in more than 50 years after Roberto De Zerbi’s side were held to a goalless draw by Nottingham Forest.

Spurs were the better side for much of the contest at the City Ground but were unable to find a way through, leaving them with just one point from their opening three Premier League matches.

Defeats to Brentford and Newcastle had already left Tottenham under pressure, and another blank means they have now failed to score in their first three league games for the first time since the 1974-75 season.

De Zerbi urged patience after the match, with Tottenham having brought in 10 senior players during the summer as they attempt to build a new-look squad.

“We bought very, very good players but you can’t just build the team with the names like in Football Manager,” he told Sky Sports.

“We are disappointed for the result but for the performance very happy. Considering we started to work together last Thursday for the first time, for the first day.

“We have to improve in every part of football, organisation with and without the ball. Even today I thought we defended very well.

“We have to work because I think we played very well with the ball, we found the solution. I think we can be much better in the final third.”

De Zerbi calls for better decisions

The Tottenham manager was particularly frustrated by the choices his players made when they reached dangerous positions.

One example came in the second half when Omar Marmoush opted to shoot rather than play the ball across to Andy Robertson, who had made an overlapping run, or Mohammed Kudus at the far post.

De Zerbi believes those moments will improve as his new-look squad develops a better understanding.

“I think we played well, in the last third we have to improve, we have to take better decisions, maybe keep calmer when we are close to doing something important,” he said.

“The chance when Marmoush shot, we had Robertson overlapping. If we take the right decision and if we play with Robertson on the second post there is Kudus to score.

“I am very happy with the spirit, with the organisation, their style of play is very clear, long ball and second ball, even the second ball we won many duels. They are good players.

“Taking a point in this stadium is not so easy. We are not happy because we didn’t win but this is the right spirit and the right way to move on in this moment.”

articles.title: Maresca claims City spending necessary to match Arsenal
articles.summary: Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca says the club must spend to match Arsenal.
articles.content:
Maresca claims City spending necessary to match Arsenal

Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca says the club must spend to match Arsenal.

Last Update:

Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca has defended the club’s £450 million summer spending spree, insisting the overhaul was necessary if they are to challenge Arsenal for the Premier League title.

City completed a major rebuild during the transfer window, with deadline-day arrivals Enzo Fernandez and Iliman Ndiaye making their debuts in Sunday’s 1-0 win over Coventry.

The pair were the final additions to a squad that has undergone significant changes, with City spending more than £450 million during the summer.

Maresca believes the depth available to Arsenal shows why City needed to strengthen their own squad if they are serious about competing at the top of the table.

“If you see since the Community Shield, Arsenal play two more games [against Coventry and Aston Villa] and they have five changes in every game,” Maresca said.

“Two World Cup winners, [Mikel] Merino and [Martin] Zubimendi, two England players, [Eberechi] Eze and [Noni] Madueke, and the other one I don’t remember, I think it was [Piero] Hincapie.

“In the end, if you want to be there you need options. Arsenal have options. We have options. More teams have options so it’s not just us. I’m very happy with the options we have, that is something important for us if you want to compete.”

Maresca praises Anderson’s attitude

Maresca was particularly impressed by Anderson’s approach since joining the club, highlighting his willingness to learn as well as his performances on the pitch.

“Really impressed, but not just today,” Maresca said.

“He was very good against Palace. He was also very good against Bournemouth having only been one week with us when we changed him for cramp.

“But the best thing with Elliot is the day by day. He is asking how he can learn, we sit with him in one-on-one video [analysis] and he wants to be better and that is the best thing for any player.”

City have won all three of their Premier League matches under Maresca so far and currently sit among the early challengers at the top of the table.

City completed a major rebuild during the transfer window, with deadline-day arrivals Enzo Fernandez and Iliman Ndiaye making their debuts in Sunday’s 1-0 win over Coventry.

The pair were the final additions to a squad that has undergone significant changes, with City spending more than £450 million during the summer.

Maresca believes the depth available to Arsenal shows why City needed to strengthen their own squad if they are serious about competing at the top of the table.

“If you see since the Community Shield, Arsenal play two more games [against Coventry and Aston Villa] and they have five changes in every game,” Maresca said.

“Two World Cup winners, [Mikel] Merino and [Martin] Zubimendi, two England players, [Eberechi] Eze and [Noni] Madueke, and the other one I don’t remember, I think it was [Piero] Hincapie.

“In the end, if you want to be there you need options. Arsenal have options. We have options. More teams have options so it’s not just us. I’m very happy with the options we have, that is something important for us if you want to compete.”

Maresca praises Anderson’s attitude

Maresca was particularly impressed by Anderson’s approach since joining the club, highlighting his willingness to learn as well as his performances on the pitch.

“Really impressed, but not just today,” Maresca said.

“He was very good against Palace. He was also very good against Bournemouth having only been one week with us when we changed him for cramp.

“But the best thing with Elliot is the day by day. He is asking how he can learn, we sit with him in one-on-one video [analysis] and he wants to be better and that is the best thing for any player.”

City have won all three of their Premier League matches under Maresca so far and currently sit among the early challengers at the top of the table.

articles.title: Premier League round-up: Draws for Brighton and Brentford as Palace win thriller
articles.summary: Catch up with the action from Saturday afternoon's Premier League games.
articles.content:
Premier League round-up: Draws for Brighton and Brentford as Palace win thriller

Catch up with the action from Saturday afternoon's Premier League games.

Last Update:

Brentford 1-1 Sunderland

A Vitaly Janelt goal and an Enzo Le Fee penalty shared the spoils at the Gtech Community Stadium in a match that both sides will feel they could have won.

Janelt gave Brentford the lead in the 57th minute, arriving from deep to steer a composed finish past Anthony Patterson, and Keith Andrews’ side looked on course for their second home win of the season.

Sunderland, however, refused to fold. With eight minutes remaining, Le Fee stepped up to convert from 12 yards, drawing the visitors level.

Both teams finish the afternoon on four points after three games. Kevin Schade has led the line with real threat for Brentford and continues to generate the most chances of any Bee this season, while Igor Thiago pressed and harassed throughout.

Brighton 1-1 Leeds

Leeds extended their unbeaten start to the Premier League season with a hard-earned point at the Amex, though Joel Bogle will consider himself lucky to have still been on the pitch when he opened the scoring.

The right-back was shown a yellow card in the sixth minute for a serious foul play challenge on Maxim De Cuyper that could quite easily have resulted in red, and the controversy lingered over the opening exchanges.

But Bogle made amends in the 15th minute, converting coolly from Ao Tanaka’s delivery to give Leeds an unexpected lead.

Brighton, who dominated possession as they have done in both previous league fixtures this season, pushed with increasing urgency in the second half and eventually levelled to take a share of the spoils.

Fabian Hurzeler’s side have now scored in both home games and shown genuine attacking threat, but conceding first has been a recurring problem that will need addressing.

Fulham 2-3 Crystal Palace

Crystal Palace claimed their first Premier League win of the season in dramatic fashion at Craven Cottage, coming from behind to beat Fulham 3-2.

Fulham had fought their way in front at 2-1 through Cesar Palacios, a goal that seemed to give Alvaro Arbeloa’s side the platform they desperately needed after two opening defeats.

But Palace, also without a point going into the afternoon, refused to accept the situation and produced a rousing finale.

Ben Chilwell was the match-winner, turning the tie on its head with the goal that made it 3-2 and prompted scenes of celebration from the travelling contingent at Craven Cottage.

articles.title: Barnes hits beauty but Bournemouth dominate at Newcastle
articles.summary: Three goals in a thrilling first half
articles.content:
Barnes hits beauty but Bournemouth dominate at Newcastle

Three goals in a thrilling first half

Last Update:

Bournemouth put in a superb first-half showing to lead Newcastle 2-1 at the break of the early Premier League game.

The Cherries were relentless in their pressing and attacking and fired into a 2-0 lead through Marcus Tavernier and a Malick Thiaw own goal.

Newcastle looked shocked but Harvey Barnes gave them some hope before half time with a fantastic curler.

The visitors went ahead when Rayan made a run and cross down the left. When Alex Scott’s shot on the egde of the box was blocked, the ball span kindly into the path of Tavernier to bury from close rnage.

Justin Kluivert had a shot well charged down as Scott ran the show.

Another rapid attack came from Scott winning the ball back. Kluivert hit the post with a stunning long range strike and when Scott retrieved the ball to fire it across goal it struck Thiaw and looped in.

The home crowd were incensed but Barnes then instantly reduced the deficit with a cracking curling shot after cutting in from the left.

articles.title: Liverpool sporting director Hughes leaves Anfield with Al Hilal move on the cards
articles.summary: Reds looking for new sporting director after transfer window closes
articles.content:
Liverpool sporting director Hughes leaves Anfield with Al Hilal move on the cards

Reds looking for new sporting director after transfer window closes

Last Update:

Liverpool sporting director Richard Hughes has stepped down from his position at Anfield, bringing an end to a two-year stint that saw the Reds capture their 20th title.

Hughes, 47, is reportedly poised to take up a lucrative sporting director role with Saudi Pro League champions Al-Hilal. The move will see Hughes reunite with former AFC Bournemouth technical director Simon Francis in Riyadh.

Al-Hilal have orchestrated an aggressive raid on the Premier League in recent windows, splashing out massive fees to land Gabriel Martinelli from Arsenal, Ollie Watkins from Aston Villa, and Crysencio Summerville from West Ham United.

Appointed from Bournemouth in June 2024, Hughes arrived during a period of massive transition at Anfield. Working alongside former head coach Arne Slot, Hughes helped deliver immediate domestic success with the 2024-25 Premier League crown.

Speaking on behalf of the club’s ownership, FSG president Mike Gordon praised Hughes’ leadership throughout a crucial chapter in modern club history:

“Richard joined us at the start of a period of change, embracing that responsibility by leading our football operations department and overseeing recruitment while also providing valuable support to our coaching staff,” he said.

“The results we achieved in these areas during this period are testament to this contribution. Nevertheless, we respect Richard’s life choices and wish him and his family well in their next venture.”

In an official farewell statement, Hughes expressed deep gratitude to the Anfield hierarchy, staff, and fanbase:

“First and foremost, I would like to reiterate what I said upon my arrival – it has been a source of great pride to have been given the opportunity to serve this incredible and unique institution. That is something I will always be grateful for.

“My appreciation extends to ownership for their support and leadership, to club staff at all levels who give so much to make Liverpool FC what it is, to the players who make such an enormous contribution and to the fans who support the team in great numbers whenever and wherever games take place.

“I’ll always follow and support the club with great affection, and I wish everyone involved nothing but success for this season and beyond.”

articles.title: Mourinho: ‘Sometimes you lose and you can’t explain it’
articles.summary: Real were beaten for the first time this season by Betis
articles.content:
Mourinho: ‘Sometimes you lose and you can’t explain it’

Real were beaten for the first time this season by Betis

Last Update:

Real Madrid manager Jose Mourinho said he had no complaints with his side’s performance as they were beaten 1-0 by Real Betis on Friday night.

Republic of Ireland striker Troy Parrott scored his first La Liga goal and Alvaro Valles saved a late Kylian Mbappe penalty to deny Real.

Mourinho, whose side are now level on nine points with both Betis and Barcelona, was happy with his team despite tasting defeat for the first time this season.

He said: “I think the team played a great game. Sometimes you lose and you don’t know how to explain it.

“We were very dominant with a lot of attacking play. If it had ended in a draw, we would have been frustrated.”

Mbappe, Jude Bellingham and Vinicius Jr all hit the woodwork on a frustrating night for Real which also led to Mourinho being shown a yellow card.

He said: “I don’t know why I saw a yellow card. I accept it. I stood up because a Betis player looked like he’d died in front of the bench.

“I saw a lot of people frustrated with the plays, but I didn’t see it myself and I can’t comment. The referee let the game flow, and that’s something I like.

“I don’t know why we lost because collectively we played very well. I have nothing to reproach any player for regarding their attitude. We deserved to win, but deserving doesn’t get you points.”

articles.title: Iraola hails Isak after first Liverpool win at Ipswich: ‘He’s a massive player for us’
articles.summary: Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola has heaped praise on Alexander Isak
articles.content:
Iraola hails Isak after first Liverpool win at Ipswich: ‘He’s a massive player for us’

Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola has heaped praise on Alexander Isak

Last Update:

Andoni Iraola praised the impact of Alexander Isak and the discipline of his Liverpool side after a dominant 2-0 win at Ipswich Town gave the new head coach his first Premier League win and lifted the Reds to fifth in the table.

Isak struck twice in the opening nine minutes at Portman Road to put the result beyond doubt before half-time, converting a near-post finish from Cody Gakpo’s first assist in the sixth minute before showing quick feet to round Kjell Scherpen and roll into an open goal three minutes later.

The goals are Isak’s second and third of the Premier League season, matching his entire tally from a difficult debut campaign at Anfield plagued by injury under Arne Slot.

The win arrived at a critical moment for Iraola, who had drawn his opening two matches and been under growing scrutiny following a chaotic summer. The Basque manager was clearly relieved in his post-match interviews.

“Definitely to get the first win. We needed that one with the way it has been. We got a clean sheet. Controlling the game quite well – I think that we started the game really strong, and then it was another kind of second half. Probably wasn’t as good as the first one,” he said.

Iraola on Isak: ‘My fight with him will be about other stuff’

Iraola was adamant about the quality Isak brings to this Liverpool side, while also revealing that his expectations of the striker extend well beyond the goals.

“He’s a massive player for us. My demands will probably not be about the goals, I know he is fit and in good shape. He’s going to produce the numbers.

“My fight with him will be more about other stuff, how to help the team in other situations, but it is good he has already played two full games, scoring the goals, so I am very happy to have him.

“Today I thought we were much better in our press in the first half, so we were covering very high and we could make contact with him in good positions. If we recover the ball lower, it will be harder to find him, so it’s all about a community effort to get our number nine in situations that he was in today.”
